items.ma-1363: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Shall I not teach you words which, if you say them, you will be forgiven, even though [it] is forgiven for you: There is no deity except Allah, al-ʿAlī, al-ʿAẓīm; there is no deity except Him, al-Ḥalīm, al-Karīm; glory be to Allah, Rabb of the Great ʿArsh; praise be to Allah, Rabb of the worlds.”
items.ma-2012: Yaḥyā narrated to us; Hishām narrated to us; Qatādah narrated to us, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say at times of distress: “There is no deity except Allah, al-ʿAẓīm, al-Ḥalīm. There is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the Mighty Throne. There is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the heavens and the earth, Rabb of the Noble ʿArsh.”
items.ma-2137: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yazīd Abū Khālid, who said: I heard al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr narrating, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “There is no Muslim servant who visits a sick person whose appointed time has not arrived, and says seven times: I ask Allah the Great, Rabb of the Great ʿArsh, to cure you, except that he is granted well-being.”
items.ma-2138: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from Ibn ʿAbbās – Abū Muʿāwiyah said: I think he raised it – he said: “Whoever visits a sick person and says, I ask Allah the Great, Rabb of the Great ʿArsh, to cure you, seven times, Allah will cure him, if he has been delayed” meaning in his appointed time. ʿAbd Allāh said: My father said: And Yazīd narrated it to us without doubting its being raised, and he agreed with him on the isnād.
items.ma-2182: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Khālid Yazīd, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Whoever comes to a sick person whose appointed time has not arrived, and says seven times: I ask Allah the Great, Rabb of the Great ʿArsh, to cure him, except that he is granted well-being.”
items.ma-2297: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abān ibn Yazīd narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah al-Riyāḥī, from the cousin of your Prophet – meaning Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate with these supplications in distress: “There is no deity except Allah, the All-Knowing, the Great; there is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the Great ʿArsh; there is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the seven heavens and Rabb of the Noble ʿArsh.”
items.ma-3315: Yazīd narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀbis, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: It used to please the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, on the day of ʿĪd, to take his family out. He said: So we went out, and he prayed without adhān or iqāmah, then he addressed the men, then he came to the women and addressed them, then he commanded them to give ṣadaqah. And I indeed saw the woman throwing her pearl and her ring, giving it to Bilāl to give in ṣadaqah with it.
items.ma-3316: Yazīd narrated to us, ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The best day on which you may undergo cupping is the seventeenth, the nineteenth, and the twenty-first.” And he said: “I did not pass by a company of the angels on the night I was taken on the Night Journey, except that they said: Hold to cupping, O Muḥammad.”
items.ma-3317: Yazīd narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwn informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: We travelled with the Prophet ﷺ between Makkah and al-Madīnah, and we were secure, fearing nothing, and he prayed two rakʿahs, two rakʿahs.
items.ma-3318: Yazīd narrated to us, ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a kohl-container with which he would apply kohl at the time of sleep, three [strokes] in each eye.
items.ma-3319: Yazīd narrated to us, Hishām informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith at Sarif while he was muḥrim, then he consummated the marriage with her after he returned, at Sarif.
items.ma-3320: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ used to apply kohl with antimony every night before he slept, and he used to apply in each eye three mīls.
items.ma-3322: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿah, from Ḥakīm ibn Ḥakīm ibn ʿAbbād ibn Ḥunayf, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Jibrīl ﵇ led me in prayer at the House twice, then he said: O Muḥammad, this is your time and the time of the Prophets before you.” He prayed the Ẓuhr prayer with him when the shadow was the measure of the sandal-strap, and he prayed the Maghrib prayer with him when the fasting person breaks his fast and food and drink become permissible.
items.ma-3323: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined the Ẓuhr and the ʿAṣr, and the Maghrib and the ʿIshāʾ, in al-Madīnah, without fear or rain. I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Why did he do that? He said: So that he would not put his ummah in hardship.
items.ma-3324: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from al-Ḥakam, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I spent the night with my maternal aunt Maymūnah. He said: The Prophet ﷺ rose during the night and performed wuḍūʾ. He said: So I rose and performed wuḍūʾ. Then he stood and prayed, and I stood behind him, or on his left, and he turned me around until he stood me on his right.
items.ma-3325:
Wakīʿ and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Mukhawwal ibn Rāshid, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ used to recite in the Fajr prayer on the day of Jumuʿah {Alif-Lām-Mīm. The Revelation}, al-Sajdah, and {Has there not come upon man}.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said in his ḥadīth: and in the Jumuʿah [prayer], with al-Jumuʿah and al-Munāfiqūn.
items.ma-3326: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite on the day of Jumuʿah in the Fajr prayer: {Alif-Lām-Mīm. The Revelation}, al-Sajdah, and {Has there not come upon man a period of time}.
items.ma-3327: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed in a cloak, guarding with its excess [folds] against the heat of the ground and its cold.
items.ma-3328: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I watched the Prophet ﷺ closely when he prostrated, and the whiteness of his armpits would be seen when he prostrated.
items.ma-3329: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Ṣāliḥ ibn Rustum narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The prayer was established while I had not prayed the two rakʿahs. He saw me while I was praying them, so he pulled me, and said: “Do you want to pray the Ṣubḥ prayer as four?” It was said to Ibn ʿAbbās: From the Prophet ﷺ? He said: Yes.
items.ma-3330: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Arqam ibn Shuraḥbīl al-Awdī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ, when he came, took up the recitation from where Abū Bakr ﵁ had reached.
items.ma-3331: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Hishām ibn Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kinānah, from his father, he said: One of the governors sent me to Ibn ʿAbbās to ask him about the prayer, in [the prayer for] rain. Ibn ʿAbbās said: What prevented him from asking me? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out humble, unadorned, submissive, unhurried, imploring, and prayed two rakʿahs as he prays on ʿĪd; he did not deliver these sermons of yours.
items.ma-3332: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Allah ﷿ made obligatory the prayer of the resident as four, and in travel two rakʿahs, and in fear one rakʿah, upon the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-3333: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAdī ibn Thābit, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on the day of the ʿĪd of Fiṭr or Aḍḥā, and prayed two rakʿahs with the people, then departed; he did not pray before it nor after it.
items.ma-3334: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Qurrah ibn Khālid and Yazīd ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ travelled from Makkah and al-Madīnah, fearing none but Allah, shortening the prayer.
items.ma-3335: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us. And ʿAbd al-Razzāq, he said: Sufyān informed us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no hijrah after the Conquest, but [there is] jihād and intention, and when you are summoned to march out, then march out.”
items.ma-3336: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Mālik ibn Mighwal narrated to us, from Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Thursday, and what is Thursday! Then I looked at his tears running down on his cheeks like a string of pearls. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Bring me the tablet and the inkwell – or the shoulder-blade – so that I may write for you a writing after which you will never go astray.” So they said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ is yahjuru!
items.ma-3337: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿUbayd al-Bahrānī, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to have nabīdh steeped for him in a waterskin.
items.ma-3338: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was given victory by the east wind, and ʿĀd were destroyed by the west wind.”
items.ma-3339: Wakīʿ narrated to us, ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ performed liʿān concerning pregnancy.
items.ma-3340: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Abū Isrāʾīl al-ʿAbsī narrated to us, from Fuḍayl ibn ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Faḍl, or one of them from the other, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever wants Ḥajj, let him hasten, for the sick person may fall ill, the riding-beast may go astray, and a need may arise.”
items.ma-3341: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Jamrah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A red velvet cloth was placed in the grave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-3342: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best of your garments is white, so wear them, and shroud your dead in them; and the best of your kohl is antimony.”
items.ma-3343: Wakīʿ narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mawhab narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The ayyim has more right over herself than her walī, and the virgin is consulted about herself, and her silence is her consent.”
items.ma-3344: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Qays ibn Ḥabtar, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the mahr of a prostitute, the price of a dog, and the price of khamr.
items.ma-3345: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Qays ibn Ḥabtar, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he raised the ḥadīth, he said: “The price of a dog, the mahr of a prostitute, and the price of khamr are ḥarām.”
items.ma-3346: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever buys food, let him not sell it until he takes possession of it.” I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Why? He said: Do you not see that they trade in gold while the food is deferred?
items.ma-3347: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Makkah in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyah, he passed by Quraysh while they were sitting in Dār al-Nadwah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “These have been saying that you are enfeebled, so perform ramal for three [circuits] when you arrive.” He said: So when they arrived, they performed ramal for three [circuits]. He said: The polytheists said: Are these the ones about whom we were saying that they have weakness? These were not content with walking until they ran hard.
items.ma-3348: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaym, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah: that Ibn ʿAbbās wrote to him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The one against whom the claim is made has more right to the oath.”
items.ma-3349: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Shufayy, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was travelling, he would pray two rakʿahs.
items.ma-3350: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sukayn ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ saw al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās looking at a woman on the evening of ʿArafah, so the Prophet ﷺ did thus with his hand over the eye of the boy, [and] said: “Indeed this is a day on which whoever guards his sight and his tongue is forgiven.”
items.ma-3351: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn al-Ward, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said to ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr: O ʿUrwah, ask your mother: Did your father not come with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and then come out of iḥrām?
items.ma-3352: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from Zayd, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ ate a bone with meat on it, then went out to the prayer.
items.ma-3353: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn: that ʿUmar asked Ibn ʿAbbās about this verse: {When the victory of Allah and the Conquest comes}. He said: When it was revealed, his own death was announced to the Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-3354: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say at times of distress: “There is no deity except Allah, al-ʿAlī al-ʿAẓīm. There is no deity except Allah, al-Ḥalīm al-Karīm. There is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the Great ʿArsh. There is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the heavens and the earth, and Rabb of the Great ʿArsh.”
items.ma-3355:
Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Arqam ibn Shuraḥbīl, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell ill with the illness in which he died, he was in the house of ʿĀʾishah, and he said: “Call ʿAlī for me.” ʿĀʾishah said: Shall we call Abū Bakr for you? He said: “Call him.” Ḥafṣah said: O Messenger of Allah, shall we call ʿUmar for you? He said: “Call him.” Umm al-Faḍl said: O Messenger of Allah, shall we call al-ʿAbbās for you? He said: “Call him.” When they had gathered, he raised his head and did not see ʿAlī, so he was silent. Then ʿUmar said: Rise away from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then Bilāl came to notify him of the prayer, and he said: “Command Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ʿĀʾishah said: Abū Bakr is a ḥaṣir man, and whenever the people do not see you they weep; if only you would command ʿUmar to lead the people in prayer. So Abū Bakr went out and led the people in prayer, and the Prophet ﷺ felt lightness in himself, so he went out, supported between two men, his feet dragging on the ground. When the people saw him, they made tasbīḥ to Abū Bakr, and he began to step back, but he signalled to him: that is, [stay in] your place. The Prophet ﷺ came until he sat. He said: And Abū Bakr stood on his right. Abū Bakr was following the Prophet ﷺ, and the people were following Abū Bakr. Ibn ʿAbbās said: And the Prophet ﷺ took up the recitation from where Abū Bakr had reached, and he died in that illness of his ﵇.
Wakīʿ said once: Abū Bakr was following the Prophet ﷺ, and the people were following Abū Bakr.
items.ma-3356: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Arqam ibn Shuraḥbīl, he said: I travelled with Ibn ʿAbbās from al-Madīnah to al-Shām, and I asked him: Did the Prophet ﷺ make a bequest? … So he mentioned its meaning, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not complete the prayer until he became very heavy, so he went out supported between two men, his feet dragging on the ground. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, and he had not made a bequest.
items.ma-3357: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ was taken while I was ten years old, circumcised, and I had recited the muḥkam of the Qurʾān.
items.ma-3358: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀbis, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: I went out with the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Fiṭr, or Aḍḥā, and he prayed, then delivered a sermon, then came to the women and admonished them, and reminded them, and commanded them to give ṣadaqah.
items.ma-3359: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, he said: I asked Ibrāhīm about a man who prays with the imām. He said: He stands on his left. So I said: Sumayʿ al-Zayyāt narrated to me, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās narrating: that the Prophet ﷺ stood him on his right, so he adopted it.
items.ma-3360: Rawḥ ibn ʿUbādah narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd informed me, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I have had no contact with my wife since the ʿafār of the palms – He said: And the ʿafār of the palms is that when they are pollinated, they are left [unwatered] for forty days, not watered after the pollination – and I found a man with my wife. And her husband was yellowish, thin-legged, with lank hair, and the one she was accused with was thick-limbed, towards dark, with tightly curled hair. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, make it clear.” Then he performed liʿān between them, and she gave birth to a man resembling the one she was accused with.
items.ma-3361: Rawḥ narrated to us, Zakariyyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to us, that Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Fruit is not sold until it is eaten.”
items.ma-3362: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Mūsā, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Whoever dwells in the desert becomes harsh, and whoever follows game becomes heedless, and whoever comes to the ruler is put to fitnah.”
items.ma-3363: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Zāʾidah. And ʿAbd al-Ṣamad, he said: Zāʾidah narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis – ʿAbd al-Ṣamad said: and those with him – for sixteen months, then the qiblah was changed afterwards. ʿAbd al-Ṣamad said: Then the qiblah was made toward Bayt al-Maqdis. And Muʿāwiyah – meaning Ibn ʿAmr – said: Then the qiblah was changed afterwards.
items.ma-3364: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Bakr – meaning Ibn Abī al-Jahm –, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the prayer of fear at Dhū Qarad, one row behind him and one row parallel to the enemy, and he prayed one rakʿah with them; then these went to the places of those, and those came, and he prayed one rakʿah with them, then gave the salām. So for the Prophet ﷺ it was two rakʿahs, and for each group one rakʿah.
items.ma-3365: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Ibn Dharr, from his father, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said to Jibrīl: “What prevents you from visiting us more than you visit us?” He said: So there was revealed: {And we do not descend except by the command of your Rabb; to Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that; and your Rabb was never forgetful} [Maryam: 64]. He said: And that was the answer to Muḥammad ﷺ.
items.ma-3366:
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade blowing into food and drink.
ʿAbd Allāh said: My father said: And Abū Nuʿaym narrated it to us, from ʿIkrimah, mursal. And Muḥammad ibn Sābiq narrated to us, he traced it back to Ibn ʿAbbās.
items.ma-3367: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the children of the polytheists, and he said: “Allah created them when He created them, and He is more knowing of what they were doing.”
items.ma-3368: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from Sulaymān ibn Abī Muslim, he heard it from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Prophet ﷺ rose to pray tahajjud during the night, he would say: “O Allah, to You is praise; You are Nūr of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them; and to You is praise; You are Qayyim of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them; and to You is praise; You are Malik of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them; and to You is praise; You are al-Ḥaqq, and Your promise is true, and Your meeting is true, and Paradise is true, and the Fire is true, and the Hour is true, and Muḥammad is true, and the Prophets are true. O Allah, to You I have submitted, and in You I have believed, and upon You I have relied, and to You I have turned in repentance, and by You I have disputed, and to You I have taken judgement. So forgive me what I have put forward and what I have held back, and what I have concealed and what I have made public. You are al-Muqaddim and You are al-Muʾakhkhir. There is no deity except You.” Or: “There is no deity other than You.”
items.ma-3369: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me, that ʿAwsajah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, informed him, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man died and did not leave anyone to inherit from him, so the Prophet ﷺ gave his inheritance to a mawlā of his whom the deceased had freed; he is the one to whom his walāʾ belonged, and the one who had freed.
items.ma-3370: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr, from Abū al-Minhāl, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived, and they were making salaf in fruits for a year and two years, or two years and three. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Make salaf in fruits for a known measure, a known weight, and a known time.”
items.ma-3371: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Zāʾidah – meaning Ibn Qudāmah – narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray on the khumrah.
items.ma-3372: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Mālik, from Makhramah ibn Sulaymān, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I spent the night with my maternal aunt Maymūnah, and I said: I will surely watch the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. A cushion was laid down for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he slept along its length, and his family slept. Then he rose at the middle of the night, or before it, or after it, and began wiping sleep from himself. Then he recited the last ten verses of Āl ʿImrān until he finished. Then he rose and came to a hanging waterskin, took from it and performed wuḍūʾ, then stood praying. So I rose and did the like of what he did, then I came and stood at his side. He placed his hand on my head, then took hold of my ear and began twisting it. Then he prayed two rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then he prayed witr.
items.ma-3373: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Mālik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn Waʿlah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man gave the Prophet ﷺ as a gift a large waterskin of khamr, and he said: “Indeed khamr has been made ḥarām.” Then he called a man and whispered to him, and he said: “What did you command him?” He said: I commanded him to sell it. He said: “Indeed the One who made its drinking ḥarām has made its sale ḥarām.” He said: So it was poured out.
items.ma-3374: I read to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Mālik. And Isḥāq narrated to me, he said: Mālik narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The sun was eclipsed, so the Prophet ﷺ prayed, and the people with him. He stood for a long standing – he said: about the length of Sūrat al-Baqarah – he said: then he bowed a long bowing, then he rose and stood a long standing, which was less than the first, then he bowed a long bowing, which was less than the first bowing, then he prostrated, then he stood a long standing, which was less than the first standing, then he bowed a long bowing, which was less than the first bowing, then he stood a long standing, which was less than the first standing, then he bowed a long bowing, which was less than the first bowing, then he prostrated, then he departed, and the sun had cleared. Then he said: “Indeed the sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of Allah; they are not eclipsed for the death of anyone, nor for his life. So when you see that, remember Allah.” They said: O Messenger of Allah, we saw you reach for something at this place of yours, then we saw you draw back. He said: “Indeed I saw Paradise – or: I was shown Paradise, and Isḥāq did not doubt; he said: I saw Paradise – and I reached for a cluster from it, and had I taken it, you would have eaten from it for as long as the world remains. And I saw the Fire, and I have never seen a sight like today more dreadful, and I saw that most of its people were women.” They said: Why, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “Because of their kufr.” He said: Do they disbelieve in Allah ﷿? He said: “No, but they disbelieve in the spouse, and they disbelieve in kindness. If you were good to one of them for all time, then she saw something from you, she would say: I have never seen any good from you.”
items.ma-3375: I read to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Al-Faḍl was riding behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a woman from Khathʿam came seeking a ruling from him. Al-Faḍl began looking at her and she at him, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began turning the face of al-Faḍl to the other side. She said: O Messenger of Allah, the obligation of Allah upon His servants in Ḥajj has reached my father, an old, aged man, who cannot stay firm on the mount; may I perform Ḥajj on his behalf? He said: “Yes.” And that was in the Ḥajj of the Farewell.
items.ma-3376: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, he said: I do not know whether I heard it from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, or was informed of it from him. He said: I came to Ibn ʿAbbās at ʿArafah while he was eating a pomegranate, and he said: The Messenger of Allah صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ broke his fast at ʿArafah, and Umm al-Faḍl sent milk to him and he drank it.
items.ma-3377: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Abī Isḥāq informed us, he said: Sulaymān ibn Yasār narrated to me – and once he said: narrated to us – he said: One of the two sons of al-ʿAbbās narrated to me, either al-Faḍl or ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ, and a man came and said: Indeed my father, or my mother – Yaḥyā said: and my strongest thought is that he said: my father – is old and has not performed Ḥajj; if I carry him on a camel he will not stay firm on it, and if I tie him on it I am not safe for him; may I perform Ḥajj on his behalf? He said: “Would you have been one who pays a debt, if it were upon him?” He said: Yes. He said: “Then perform Ḥajj on his behalf.”
items.ma-3378: Hushaym narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Abī Isḥāq informed us, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, or from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās: that a man asked the Prophet ﷺ … And he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-3379: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ informed us, from ʿIkrimah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ pressed me to him, and said: “O Allah, teach him the Book.”
items.ma-3380: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, he said: ʿAmmār, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to me, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died while he was sixty-five years old.
items.ma-3381: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb informed us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out from the privy, and food was brought near to him, and they offered him water for wuḍūʾ, so he said: “I was only commanded to perform wuḍūʾ when I stand to the prayer.”
items.ma-3382: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥuwayrith, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out from the privy, and food was brought near to him, and they said: Shall we not bring you water for wuḍūʾ? He said: “Am I to pray, that I should perform wuḍūʾ?!”
items.ma-3383: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Whoever makes an image will be charged on the Day of Resurrection with blowing into it, and he will be punished, and he will never blow into it. And whoever feigns a dream will be charged on the Day of Resurrection with tying two grains of barley – or he said: between two grains of barley – and he will be punished, and he will never tie between them. And whoever listens to the speech of a people who dislike it, ānuk will be poured into his two ears on the Day of Resurrection.” Ismāʿīl said: meaning lead.
items.ma-3384: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Maymūnah while he was muḥrim, and consummated the marriage with her while ḥalāl at Sarif, and she died at Sarif.
items.ma-3385: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb informed us, from ʿIkrimah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said concerning the grandfather: As for the one to whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Were I to take a khalīl from this ummah, I would have taken him,” he ruled him a father; meaning Abū Bakr.
items.ma-3386: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb informed us, from Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: Muḥammad ﷺ said: “I looked into Paradise and saw that most of its people were the poor, and I looked into the Fire and saw that most of its people were women.”
items.ma-3387: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said, concerning the prostration in “Ṣād”: It is not among the ʿazāʾim of prostration, and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrating in it.
items.ma-3388: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Ghaniyyah narrated to us, he said: al-ʿAwwām ibn Ḥawshab informed us, he said: I asked Mujāhid about the prostration which is in “Ṣād”, and he said: Yes, I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about it, and he said: Do you recite this verse: {and from his offspring, Dāwūd and Sulaymān}, and at its end: {so follow their guidance} [al-Anʿām: 84 - 90]? He said: Your Prophet ﷺ was commanded to follow Dāwūd.
items.ma-3389: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I spent the night with my maternal aunt Maymūnah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose to pray during the night, so I rose to pray with him, and I stood on his left. He said to me thus, and took hold of my head and stood me on his right.
items.ma-3390: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, he said: I was informed from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Then the angel came with her until he reached the place of Zamzam, and struck with his heel, and it gushed forth as a spring. The woman hurried, and began scooping into her waterskin. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “May Allah have mercy on the mother of Ismāʿīl; had she not hurried, Zamzam would have been a flowing spring.”
items.ma-3391: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from an old man of Banū Sadūs, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about kissing for the fasting person, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to take from the heads while he was fasting.
items.ma-3392:
Ibn Jaʿfar narrated it to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq, from Ibn ʿAbbās; he mentioned it.
ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated it to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq, from Ibn ʿAbbās; he mentioned it.
items.ma-3393: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Yūnus informed us, from al-Ḥakam ibn al-Aʿraj, he said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, and he said: When you see the new moon of al-Muḥarram, count; and when you reach the morning of the ninth, rise fasting. Yūnus said: And I was informed from al-Ḥakam that he said: Is it thus that Muḥammad ﷺ fasted? He said: Yes.
items.ma-3394: Ismāʿīl and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, they said: ʿAwf narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan – Ibn Jaʿfar said: Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan narrated to me –, he said: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās, and a man asked him and said: O Ibn ʿAbbās, I am a man whose livelihood is only from the work of my hands, and I make these images. He said: I will only narrate to you what I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; I heard him say: “Whoever makes an image, Allah ﷿ will punish him on the Day of Resurrection until he blows the spirit into it, and he will never be one who blows into it.” He said: The man gasped hard at this, and his face turned yellow. Ibn ʿAbbās said to him: Woe to you! If you refuse but to make, then keep to these trees and everything that has no spirit.
items.ma-3395: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from a man, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to come out of iḥrām, so we came out of iḥrām; and garments were worn, and the censers gave off their scent, and women were married.
items.ma-3396: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Layth informed us, he said: Ṭāwūs said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Indeed the Prophet ﷺ did not pray in it, but he faced its corners.
items.ma-3397: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Layth informed us, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined the Ẓuhr and the ʿAṣr, and the Maghrib and the ʿIshāʾ, in travel and in residence.
items.ma-3398: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ broke his fast at ʿArafah, and Umm al-Faḍl sent milk to him, and he drank it.
items.ma-3399: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb informed us, from ʿIkrimah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited in that in which he was commanded to recite, and was silent in that in which he was commanded to be silent: {and your Rabb was never forgetful} [Maryam: 64], and {There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example} [al-Aḥzāb: 21].
items.ma-3400: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Maymūnah while he was muḥrim.
items.ma-3401: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Seek it in the last ten, in the ninth [night] remaining, or the fifth remaining, or the seventh remaining.”
items.ma-3402: Bahz narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, al-Jaʿd, the one of the jewellery, Abū ʿUthmān, narrated to us, Abū Rajāʾ narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, in what he narrates from his Rabb ﷿: “Indeed Allah ﷿ wrote down the good deeds and the evil deeds, then made that clear. So whoever intends a good deed and does not do it, Allah writes it for him, with Him, as a complete good deed; and if he does it, ten good deeds are written for him, up to seven hundred fold, up to many multiples. And if he intends an evil deed and does not do it, Allah writes it for him, with Him, as a complete good deed; and if he does it, one evil deed is written for him.”
items.ma-3403: Bahz narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ took a bite from a shoulder, then prayed and did not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-3404: Bahz narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿAzrah, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr. And ʿAbd al-Ṣamad, he said: Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from a companion of his, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ used to recite in the Jumuʿah prayer al-Jumuʿah and al-Munāfiqūn.
items.ma-3405: Bahz narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the husband of Barīrah was a black slave called Mughīth, and I used to see him following her in the lanes of al-Madīnah, squeezing his eyes over her. He said: And the Prophet ﷺ gave four judgements concerning her: he judged that the walāʾ is for the one who frees; and he gave her the choice; and he commanded her to observe ʿiddah – Hammām said once: the ʿiddah of a free woman –. He said: And ṣadaqah was given to her, and she gave a gift from it to ʿĀʾishah, and she mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “It is ṣadaqah for her, and a gift for us.”
items.ma-3406: Bahz narrated to us, Abān ibn Yazīd al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, and from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, among them al-Ashajj, the brother of Banū ʿAṣar. They said: O Prophet of Allah, we are a clan of Rabīʿah, and between us and you are the disbelievers of Muḍar, and we cannot reach you except in the sacred month, so command us with a matter by which, if we act upon it, we enter Paradise, and we call those behind us to it. So he commanded them with four and forbade them four: he commanded them to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him, to fast Ramaḍān, to perform Ḥajj to the House, and to give the khumus from the spoils. And he forbade them four: drinking in the gourd, the ḥantam, the naqīr and the pitch-coated vessel. They said: Then in what shall we drink, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “Keep to waterskins of tanned leather whose mouths are tied.”
items.ma-3407: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abān narrated to us, he said: I heard Qatādah mention from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibn ʿAbbās. And ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, among them al-Ashajj, the brother of Banū ʿAṣar … So he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-3408: Bahz narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, from Qatādah. And ʿAffān narrated to us, he said: Hammām narrated to us, from Qatādah – ʿAffān said: Qatādah informed us –, from Abū Mijlaz, he said: I asked Ibn ʿUmar about witr, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “One rakʿah from the end of the night.” He said: And I asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “One rakʿah from the end of the night.”
items.ma-3409: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died while his armour was pawned with a Jew for thirty ṣāʿ of barley, which he had taken as food for his family.
items.ma-3410: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, ʿAwf ibn Abī Jamīlah narrated to us, from Yazīd al-Fārisī, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in sleep in the time of Ibn ʿAbbās. He said: And Yazīd used to write copies of the Qurʾān. He said: So I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in sleep. Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: “Indeed Shayṭān is not able to take my likeness, so whoever sees me in sleep has seen me.” So are you able to describe to us this man whom you saw? He said: I said: Yes. I saw a man between the two men, in his body and his flesh, brown towards white, with a beautiful smile, kohl-eyed, with fine contours of the face; his beard had filled from here to here, until it almost filled his chest. ʿAwf said: I do not know what was with this of the description. He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Had you seen him while awake, you could not have described him more than this.
items.ma-3411: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Muḥammad, from Ibn ʿAbbās: We travelled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ between Makkah and al-Madīnah, fearing none but Allah ﷿, praying two rakʿahs.
items.ma-3412: Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith while he was muḥrim.
items.ma-3413: Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married while he was muḥrim.
items.ma-3414: Isḥāq narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ, when he prostrated, the whiteness of his armpits would be seen while he was prostrating.
items.ma-3415: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ freed, on the day of al-Ṭāʾif, those of the slaves of the polytheists who came out to him.
items.ma-3416: Muʿtamir narrated to us, from Salm, from some of his companions, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no musāʿāh in Islam. Whoever practised musāʿāh in the Jāhiliyyah, I have attached him to his ʿaṣabah; and whoever claims his child not from a rishdah, he neither inherits nor is inherited from.”
items.ma-3417: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ḥabīb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Al-Ṣaʿb ibn Jaththāmah gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a wild donkey as a gift while he was muḥrim, so he returned it, and said: “Were it not that we are muḥrimūn, we would have accepted it from you.”
items.ma-3418: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted the dyed garment, so long as there was no nafḍ in it and no radʿ.
items.ma-3419: Ḥammād ibn Usāmah narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Aʿmash say: ʿAbbād ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When Abū Ṭālib fell ill, a group of Quraysh entered upon him, among them Abū Jahl, and they said: O Abū Ṭālib, your brother's son insults our gods, he says and says, and does and does; so send for him and forbid him. He said: So Abū Ṭālib sent for him. And near Abū Ṭālib was the place of one man, so he feared that if the Prophet ﷺ entered upon his uncle he would be more tender toward him, so he leapt and sat in that place. When the Prophet ﷺ entered, he did not find a seat except by the door, so he sat. Abū Ṭālib said: O son of my brother, your people complain of you, claiming that you insult their gods, and you say and say, and do and do. He said: “O uncle, I only want from them one word by which the Arabs will submit to them, and by which the non-Arabs will pay the jizyah to them.” They said: And what is it? Yes, by your father, ten! He said: “There is no deity except Allah.” He said: So they stood up, shaking out their garments, saying: {Has he made the gods one deity? Indeed this is a strange thing}. He said: Then he recited until he reached: {Rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment} [Ṣād: 5 - 8].
items.ma-3420: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: A woman came to him and said: My mother has died, and upon her was a month of fasting; may I make it up on her behalf? He said: “Do you see: if there had been a debt upon her, would you have paid it?” She said: Yes. He said: “Then the debt of Allah ﷿ is more deserving to be paid.”
items.ma-3421: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Mālik – meaning Ibn Anas – narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Faḍl narrated to me, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The ayyim has more right over herself than her walī, and the virgin is consulted about herself, and her silence is her consent.”
items.ma-3422: Yaʿlā and Muḥammad narrated to us, in meaning, they said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Which of the two recitations do you count as first? They said: The recitation of ʿAbd Allāh. He said: No, rather it is the last. The Qurʾān used to be presented to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ once every year, and in the year in which he was taken it was presented to him twice, and ʿAbd Allāh was present at it, so he knew what was abrogated of it and what was changed.
items.ma-3423: Yaʿlā narrated to us, Ḥajjāj al-Ṣawwāf narrated to us, from Yaḥyā, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled concerning the mukātab who is killed: that for what he had paid of his mukātabah, the blood-money of a free man is paid, and for what remained, the blood-money of a slave.
items.ma-3424: Yaʿlā narrated to us, Ḥajjāj al-Ṣawwāf narrated to us, from Yaḥyā, from ʿIkrimah, he said: I was sitting with Zayd ibn ʿAlī in al-Madīnah, and an old man passed by, who was called Shuraḥbīl Abū Saʿd. He said: O Abū Saʿd, where have you come from? He said: From the Commander of the Believers; I narrated a ḥadīth to him, and he said: For this ḥadīth to be true is dearer to me than for me to have red camels. He said: Narrate it to the people. He said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no Muslim who reaches two daughters, and treats them well for as long as they accompany him – or he accompanies them –, except that they will enter him into Paradise.”
items.ma-3425: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, Ibn Shihāb narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the most generous of people in good, and he was most generous in Ramaḍān, when Jibrīl met him. And Jibrīl used to meet him every night in Ramaḍān until it passed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ presenting the Qurʾān to him. And when Jibrīl met him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was more generous in good than the wind that is sent forth.
items.ma-3426: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym narrated to us. And ʿAbd al-Razzāq, he said: Sufyān informed us, from ʿAbd Allāh, in meaning, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Wear white from among your garments, for they are among the best of your garments, and shroud your dead in them. And indeed the best of your kohl is antimony; it makes hair grow and clears the sight.”
items.ma-3427: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Nāfiʿ narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, he said: I wrote to Ibn ʿAbbās, and he wrote to me: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed the oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made; and if people were given according to their claims, people would claim the wealth of people and their blood.”
items.ma-3428: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the man who comes to his wife while she is menstruating, he said: “He gives a dīnār in ṣadaqah, and if he does not find it, then half a dīnār.”
items.ma-3429: Abū Kāmil and ʿAffān narrated to us, they said: Ḥammād narrated to us, from Abū Jamrah – ʿAffān said: he said: Abū Jamrah informed us – from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed in Makkah thirteen years, and in al-Madīnah ten, being given revelation, and he died when he was sixty-three years old.
items.ma-3430: Abū Kāmil and Yūnus narrated to us, they said: Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ used to deliver the sermon at a trunk, and when the minbar was made and he moved to it, the trunk yearned; so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to it and embraced it, and it became still. And he said: “Had I not embraced it, it would have yearned until the Day of Resurrection.”
items.ma-3431: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from Thābit, from Anas, the like of it.
items.ma-3432: Al-Khuzāʿī narrated it to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah informed us, from ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, from Ibn ʿAbbās. And from Thābit, from Anas: that the Prophet ﷺ used to deliver the sermon at the trunk of the palm tree … So he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-3433: Muḥammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Hishām, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gnawed meat from a bone, then prayed and did not touch water.
items.ma-3434: Muḥammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from Dāwūd ibn Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying ﷿: {So if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them, they will never harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed Allāh Yuḥibbu those who act justly} [al-Māʾidah: 42], he said: Banū al-Naḍīr, when they killed someone from Banū Qurayẓah, would pay them half the blood-money, and when Banū Qurayẓah killed someone from Banū al-Naḍīr, they would pay them the full blood-money; so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the blood-money equal between them.
items.ma-3435: Marwān ibn Shujāʿ narrated to us, Khuṣayf narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he raised it to the Prophet ﷺ: “That the woman in postnatal bleeding and the menstruating woman perform ghusl, enter iḥrām, and complete all the rites, except that she does not perform ṭawāf of the House until she becomes pure.”
items.ma-3436: Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to prostrate in “Ṣād”.
items.ma-3437: Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, Rishdīn ibn Kurayb informed us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, and I stood at his side, on his left, so he took me and stood me on his right. He said: And Ibn ʿAbbās said: And I was ten years old that day.
items.ma-3438:
ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, he said: We were invited to a meal, and in it were Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Miqsam, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās. When the food was set down, Saʿīd said: Has what was said about food reached all of you? Miqsam said: Narrate, O Abū ʿAbd Allāh, for whoever has not heard. So he said:
Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When food is set down, do not eat from its middle, for the blessing descends in its middle; and eat from its two edges.” Or: “its two edges.”
items.ma-3439: ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Bakr narrated to us, they said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me that he heard Ṭāwūs informing, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿUmar: that he witnessed the ruling of the Prophet ﷺ in that. Ḥamal ibn Mālik ibn al-Nābighah came, and said: I was between two women, and one of them struck the other with a tent-pole, and killed her and her foetus. So the Prophet ﷺ ruled concerning her foetus a ghurrah, a slave, and that she be killed. I said to ʿAmr: Ibn Ṭāwūs informed me, from his father, such and such. He said: You have made me doubt. Ibn Bakr said: There was between me and my two wives, and one of them struck the other.
items.ma-3440: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī informed us, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that Khidhām Abū Wadīʿah gave his daughter in marriage to a man, so she came to the Prophet ﷺ and complained to him that she had been given in marriage while she was unwilling, so the Prophet ﷺ removed her from her husband, and said: “Do not compel them.” He said: So after that she married Abū Lubābah al-Anṣārī, and she was previously married.
items.ma-3441: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās … the like of it, and added: Then she came to him afterwards and informed him that he had touched her, so he prevented her from returning to her first husband, and said: “O Allah, if his oaths were that you make her lawful for Rifāʿah, then let her marriage not be completed for him another time.” Then she came to Abū Bakr and ʿUmar in their caliphates, and both of them prevented her.
items.ma-3442: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: Sulaymān al-Aḥwal informed me, that Ṭāwūs informed him, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ, while he was performing ṭawāf of the Kaʿbah, passed by a person leading another person by a nose-ring in his nose, so the Prophet ﷺ cut it with his hand, then commanded him to lead him by his hand.
items.ma-3443: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: Sulaymān al-Aḥwal informed me, that Ṭāwūs informed him, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ, while he was performing ṭawāf of the Kaʿbah, passed by a person who had tied his hand to another person with a strap, or a thread, or something other than that, so the Prophet ﷺ cut it with his hand, then said: “Lead him by the hand.”
items.ma-3444: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ziyād ibn Ḥuṣayn, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by a group who were shooting, and said: “Shoot, O Banū Ismāʿīl, for your father was a shooter.”
items.ma-3445: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, he said: A man came to Ibn ʿAbbās … So he mentioned the ḥadīth, and he said: And I indeed heard your Prophet ﷺ say: “The slain one will come on the Day of Resurrection, holding his head – either he said: in his left hand, or in his right – his jugular veins gushing, in front of the ʿArsh of al-Raḥmān ﵎, saying: O Rabb, ask this one: for what did he kill me?”
items.ma-3446: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, he said: It reached me: that the Prophet ﷺ, when he prostrated, the whiteness of his armpits was seen.
items.ma-3447: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of that from the Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-3448: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Layth, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Teach and make easy, and do not make difficult; and when you become angry, be silent; and when you become angry, be silent; and when you become angry, be silent.”
items.ma-3449: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: I have had no contact with my wife since the ʿafār of the palms – or its ʿiqār, he said: and the ʿafār of the palms or their ʿiqār is that they were pollinated, then tuʿfar, or tuʿqar, for forty days, not watered after the pollination – he said: and I found a man with my wife. And her husband was yellowish, thin-legged, with lank hair, and the one she was accused with was a thick-limbed man towards dark, with tightly curled hair. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, make it clear. O Allah, make it clear.” Then he performed liʿān between them, and she gave birth to a child resembling the one she was accused with.
items.ma-3450: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Shall I not inform you of the wuḍūʾ of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Then he called for water, and began to scoop with his right hand, then pour over the left.
items.ma-3451: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Sumayʿ al-Zayyāt, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: I had stood at the side of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, on his left, so he turned me around and placed me on his right.
items.ma-3452:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a dead sheep belonging to Maymūnah, and said: “Why did you not benefit from its hide?” They said: And how, when it is dead? He said: “Only its meat was made ḥarām.”
Maʿmar said: And al-Zuhrī used to deny tanning, and say: It is benefited from in every case.
items.ma-3453: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Prophet ﷺ performed wuḍūʾ, then cut from a shoulder and ate, then went on to the prayer and did not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-3454: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, and ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ in the Ḥajj of the Farewell – or he said: on the day of the Conquest – while he was praying, I and al-Faḍl riding together on a she-donkey. We crossed the row and dismounted from her, then entered the row, while the she-donkey was passing in front of them, and it did not cut their prayer. And ʿAbd al-Aʿlā said: I was riding behind al-Faḍl on a she-donkey, and we came while the Prophet of Allah ﷺ was leading the people in prayer at Minā.
items.ma-3455: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ, when he saw the images in the House – meaning the Kaʿbah – did not enter, and commanded about them, so they were erased. And he saw Ibrāhīm and Ismāʿīl ﵉ with divining arrows in their hands, and said: “May Allah fight them! By Allah, the two never divined with arrows.”
items.ma-3456: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Thaqafī narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Seek it in the last ten, in the ninth [night] remaining, or the fifth remaining, or the seventh remaining.”
items.ma-3457: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A slave of Banū Bayāḍah performed cupping on the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ gave him his wage; and had it been ḥarām, he would not have given it to him. He said: And he commanded his mawlās to lighten some of his kharāj for him.
items.ma-3458: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr and Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the effeminate men and the women who imitate men.
items.ma-3459: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from ʿIkrimah ibn Khālid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I was in the house of Maymūnah, and the Prophet ﷺ rose to pray during the night, so I stood with him on his left; he took my hand and placed me on his right, then prayed thirteen rakʿahs. I estimated the length of his standing in each rakʿah as the length of {O you who are wrapped up}.
items.ma-3460:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out in the year of the Conquest to Makkah in the month of Ramaḍān, and fasted until he reached al-Kudayd, then broke his fast.
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out in the year of the Conquest in the month of Ramaḍān, and fasted until he passed by a pool on the road, and that was at the height of midday. He said: The people became thirsty and began stretching their necks, and their souls longed for it. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for a cup with water in it, and held it on his hand until the people saw it, then he drank, and the people drank.
items.ma-3461: ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Bakr narrated to us, they said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: I heard ʿAṭāʾ, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās. Ibn Bakr said: Then I heard him afterwards – meaning ʿAṭāʾ – say: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: There was a sheep – or a domestic animal – belonging to one of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, and it died, so the Prophet ﷺ said: “Why did you not benefit from its hide? Or: its skin?”
items.ma-3462: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us. And Rawḥ, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Khuṣayf informed me, that Miqsam, the mawlā of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, informed him, that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him, he said: I was with ʿUmar when Saʿd and Ibn ʿUmar asked him about wiping over the khuffs. ʿUmar ruled in favour of Saʿd. Ibn ʿAbbās said: So I said: O Saʿd, we know that the Prophet ﷺ wiped over his khuffs, but was it before al-Māʾidah, or after it? – He said: Rawḥ said: or after it? – He said: No one will inform you that the Prophet ﷺ wiped over them after al-Māʾidah was revealed. So ʿUmar was silent.
items.ma-3463: ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Bakr narrated to us, they said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: ʿUmar ibn ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī al-Khuwār informed me, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was eating a bone with meat on it, the muʾadhdhin came to him, so he put it down and stood to the prayer, and did not touch water.
items.ma-3464: ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Bakr narrated to us, they said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf informed me, that Sulaymān ibn Yasār informed him, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās, and he saw Abū Hurayrah performing wuḍūʾ, so he said: Do you know from what I perform wuḍūʾ? He said: No. He said: I perform wuḍūʾ from pieces of dried curd that I ate. Ibn ʿAbbās said: I do not care from what you perform wuḍūʾ; I bear witness that I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eat a shoulder of meat, then stand to the prayer and not perform wuḍūʾ. He said: And Sulaymān was present at that from both of them together.
items.ma-3465: ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Bakr narrated to us, they said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me, and he said: My knowledge, and what comes to my mind, is that Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ informed me, that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him: that the Prophet ﷺ used to perform ghusl with the leftover of Maymūnah. ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: And that is because I asked him about the vacating of the two in janābah together.
items.ma-3466: ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Bakr narrated to us, they said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: I said to ʿAṭāʾ: Which time is dearer to you for me to pray the ʿIshāʾ, as an imām or alone? He said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the ʿIshāʾ one night until the people slept and woke, and slept and woke. So ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb stood and said: The prayer! ʿAṭāʾ said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: So the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came out, as though I am looking at him now, his head dripping water, with his hand placed on the side of his head, and he said: “Were it not that I would burden my ummah, I would have commanded them to pray it thus.”
items.ma-3467: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us. And Ibn Bakr, he said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me, that Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ informed him, that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him, he said: I prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eight [rakʿahs] together, and seven together.
items.ma-3468: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: Sulaymān al-Aḥwal informed me, that Ṭāwūs informed him, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: When the Prophet ﷺ prayed tahajjud at night … So he mentioned the like of the supplication of Sufyān, except that he said: “And Your promise is the truth, and Your saying is the truth, and Your meeting is the truth,” and he said: “And what I have concealed and what I have made public; You are my deity, there is no deity except You.”
items.ma-3469: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the most generous of mankind, and no sooner would the month of Ramaḍān enter than Jibrīl ﷺ would study with him, and then he was more generous than the wind.
items.ma-3470: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Salamah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās used to narrate: that Abū Bakr uncovered, from the face of the Prophet ﷺ, while he was dead, the ḥibarah cloak with which he had been covered; he looked at the face of the Prophet ﷺ, then bent over him and kissed him.
items.ma-3471: ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, they said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: Ibrāhīm ibn Maysarah informed me, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he mentioned the saying of the Prophet ﷺ about ghusl on the day of Jumuʿah. Ṭāwūs said: So I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: And does he touch perfume or oil, if he has it with his family? He said: I do not know it.
items.ma-3472: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Khidāsh narrated to me, that Ibn ʿAbbās said: When the Prophet ﷺ looked out over the cemetery – and it was on his first road – he pointed with his hand behind the ḍafīr – or he said: behind the ḍafīrah; ʿAbd al-Razzāq doubted – and said: “What a good cemetery this is.” So I said to the one who informed me: Did he single out the shiʿb? He said: Thus he said; he did not inform me that he singled out anything except for that: he pointed with his hand behind the ḍafīr – or the ḍafīrah –; and we used to hear that the Prophet ﷺ singled out the shiʿb opposite the House.
items.ma-3473: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: ʿAbd al-Karīm and others informed me, from Miqsam, the mawlā of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him: that the Prophet ﷺ made, for the menstruating woman who is approached, a dīnār; and if he approached her after the blood had receded from her and she had not performed ghusl, half a dīnār. All of that is from the Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-3474: ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Bakr narrated to us, they said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me, that he heard Muḥammad ibn Jubayr say: Ibn ʿAbbās used to reject going ahead in the fasting of Ramaḍān when the crescent of the month of Ramaḍān had not been seen, and he would say: The Prophet ﷺ said: “If you do not see the crescent, then complete thirty nights.”
items.ma-3475: ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Bakr narrated to us, they said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Yazīd informed me, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: I do not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek out the fast of a day, seeking its excellence over others, except this day; for the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, or Ramaḍān. Rawḥ said: or the month of Ramaḍān.
items.ma-3476: ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Bakr narrated to us, they said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: ʿAṭāʾ said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās called al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās, on the day of ʿArafah, to food, and he said: I am fasting. ʿAbd Allāh said: Do not fast, for a milk-pail with milk in it was brought near to the Prophet ﷺ on the day of ʿArafah, and he drank from it. So do not fast, for the people follow your example. Ibn Bakr and Rawḥ said: Indeed the people take you as an example.
items.ma-3477: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Zakariyyā ibn ʿUmar informed me, that ʿAṭāʾ informed him: that Ibn ʿAbbās called al-Faḍl …
items.ma-3478: ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Bakr narrated to us, they said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me, that Abū Maʿbad, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, informed him, that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him: that the raising of the voice with dhikr when the people depart from the prescribed prayer was in the time of the Prophet ﷺ; and that he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: I used to know, when they departed, by that, when I heard it.
items.ma-3479: ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Bakr narrated to us, they said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: ʿAṭāʾ informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I spent a night with my maternal aunt Maymūnah, and the Prophet ﷺ rose to pray voluntarily during the night. The Prophet ﷺ went to the waterskin and performed wuḍūʾ, then stood praying. So I stood when I saw him do that, and performed wuḍūʾ from the waterskin, then stood at his left side. He took my hand from behind my back, straightening me thus, from behind my back, to the right side.
items.ma-3480: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās informed me, from ʿIkrimah and from Kurayb, that Ibn ʿAbbās said: Shall I not narrate to you about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when travelling? He said: We said: Yes. He said: When the sun passed the meridian while he was at his halting place, he would combine the Ẓuhr and the ʿAṣr before riding; and if it had not passed the meridian while he was at his halting place, he would travel until, when the time of ʿAṣr came, he would dismount and combine the Ẓuhr and the ʿAṣr. And when the time of Maghrib came while he was at his halting place, he would combine it with the ʿIshāʾ; and if it had not come while he was at his halting place, he would ride until, when the time of ʿIshāʾ came, he would dismount and combine the two.
items.ma-3481: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever buys food, let him not sell it until he takes possession of it.” He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: I reckon everything to be in the position of food.
items.ma-3482: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade that the riders be met, and that a resident sell for a desert-dweller. He said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: What is his saying “a resident for a desert-dweller”? He said: That he not be a broker for him.
items.ma-3483: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from ʿIkrimah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Abū Jahl said: If I see Muḥammad praying at the Kaʿbah, I will surely tread on his neck. That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “If he did, the angels would seize him in plain sight.”
items.ma-3484: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Atānī Rabbī ﷿ fī aḥsani ṣūrah – I think he meant in sleep – and He said: O Muḥammad, do you know about what the exalted assembly dispute? He said: I said: No.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Fa-waḍaʿa Yadahu bayna katifayya, until I found its coolness between my breasts – or he said: my chest – and I knew what is in the heavens and what is in the earth. Then He said: O Muḥammad, do you know about what the exalted assembly dispute? He said: I said: Yes, they dispute about the expiations and the degrees. He said: And what are the expiations and the degrees? He said: Remaining in the mosques after the prayers, walking on foot to the Jumuʿahs, and completing wuḍūʾ in disliked [circumstances]; and whoever does that lives in good, and dies in good, and is from his sin as on the day his mother bore him. And say, O Muḥammad, when you have prayed: O Allah, I ask You for good things, and the leaving of abominable things, and love of the poor; and when You intend a fitnah for Your servants, that You take me to You not put to fitnah. He said: And the degrees: giving out food, spreading the salām, and praying at night while the people are asleep.”
items.ma-3485: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the assembly of Quraysh gathered in al-Ḥijr, and swore a pact by al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt, the third, the other: If we were to see Muḥammad, we would rise to him as one man, and we would not part from him until we killed him. He said: So Fāṭimah came weeping until she entered upon her father, and said: This assembly of your people are in al-Ḥijr; they have sworn a pact that if they see you they will rise to you and kill you, and there is no man among them but he knows his share of your blood. He said: “O my little daughter, bring near water for wuḍūʾ.” So he performed wuḍūʾ, then entered upon them in the mosque. When they saw him, they said: It is him, it is him. So they lowered their gazes, and were rooted in their seats; they did not raise their eyes to him, and not a man of them stood. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ approached until he stood over their heads, then took a handful of dust and pelted them with it, and said: “May the faces be disfigured.” He said: And no pebble struck a man of them but that he was killed on the day of Badr as a disbeliever.
items.ma-3486: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from ʿUthmān al-Jazarī, from Miqsam, he said: I do not know it except from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the banner of the Prophet ﷺ was with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and the banner of the Anṣār was with Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah; and when the killing became intense, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would be among those who were under the banner of the Anṣār.
items.ma-3487: Yazīd narrated to us, Sufyān ibn Saʿīd informed us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀbis, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās, when he was asked: Did you attend the ʿĪd with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: Yes, and were it not for my kinship to him, I would not have attended it, because of [my] youth. He prayed two rakʿahs, then delivered a sermon, then came to the marker which is by the house of Kathīr ibn al-Ṣalt, and admonished the women and reminded them, and commanded them to give ṣadaqah; so they reached for their ears and their throats and gave ṣadaqah with it. He said: And they handed it to Bilāl.
items.ma-3488: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he did not consider it right to alight at al-Abṭaḥ, and he would say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only stayed there for ʿĀʾishah.
items.ma-3489: Yazīd narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah informed us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The mukātab is paid blood-money, by the share of what he has paid, the blood-money of a free man, and for what remains, the blood-money of a slave.”
items.ma-3490:
Yazīd narrated to us, ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr informed us, from ʿIkrimah ibn Khālid al-Makhzūmī, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I came to my maternal aunt Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith, and spent the night with her, and I found that night of hers to be with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the ʿIshāʾ, then entered his house, and put his head on a leather cushion stuffed with palm fibre. So I came and put my head on a side of it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke, and looked, and behold, it was still night; so he returned, and glorified [Allah] and said takbīr until he slept. Then he woke when half of the night – or he said: two thirds of it – had gone. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose and relieved himself, then came to a waterskin on a stand with water in it, and rinsed his mouth three times, and sniffed water three times, and washed his face three times, and his forearms three times each, and wiped his head and his ears once, then washed his feet – Yazīd said: I think he said: three times each. Then he came to his place of prayer. So I rose and did as he had done, then I came and stood at his left, wanting to pray his prayer. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ waited, until when he knew that I wanted to pray his prayer, he turned his right [hand] and took my ear, and turned me around until he stood me at his right. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed, for as long as he saw that night remained, two rakʿahs. When he thought that the dawn had drawn near, he rose and prayed six rakʿahs, and prayed witr with the seventh. Until, when the dawn lit up, he rose and prayed two rakʿahs, then laid his side down and slept until I heard his snoring. Then Bilāl came to him and notified him of the prayer, and he went out and prayed, and did not touch water.
So I said to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: How excellent this is! Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: By Allah, I said that to Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: Enough! It is not for you or for your companions; it is for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; he used to be protected.
items.ma-3491: Yazīd narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from al-Ḥasan al-ʿUranī, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about the man, when he has thrown the jamrah, may he apply perfume? He said: As for me, I saw musk on the head of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; is it among perfume or not?
items.ma-3492: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Jurayrī informed us, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, he said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Narrate to me about riding between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, for your people claim that it is sunnah. He said: They have told the truth and have lied. I said: Told the truth and lied about what? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Makkah, and they went out until the young women went out; and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not one in whose presence anyone was beaten. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rode, and performed ṭawāf while riding; and had he dismounted, walking would have been dearer to him.
items.ma-3493: Muʿādh narrated to us, Ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, from Muḥammad, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: We travelled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ between Makkah and al-Madīnah, fearing none but Allah ﷿, and he prayed two rakʿahs.
items.ma-3494: Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from Mūsā ibn Salamah, he said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about the prayer at al-Baṭḥāʾ, when the prayer in congregation has passed me by. He said: Two rakʿahs; that is the sunnah of Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ.
items.ma-3495: Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Ḥumayd, from Bakr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque on his camel, with Usāmah ibn Zayd behind him, and asked for a drink, so we gave him nabīdh to drink, and he drank, then handed his leftover to Usāmah, and said: “You have done well and done beautifully; so do likewise.” So we do not wish to change that.
items.ma-3496: Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, Misʿar informed us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever buys food, let him not sell it until he takes possession of it.” Misʿar said: And I think he said: “or fodder.”
items.ma-3497: ʿAbdah ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I gave the Prophet ﷺ water from Zamzam to drink, and he drank while standing.
items.ma-3498: Rawḥ ibn ʿUbādah narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, he said: Qays ibn Saʿd informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, when he raised his head from the bowing, would say: “O Allah, our Rabb, to You is praise, [as] the fill of the heaven, and the fill of the earth, and the fill of whatever thing You will after.”
items.ma-3499: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿAṭāʾ say: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When one of you has eaten food, let him not wipe his hand until he licks it, or has it licked.”
items.ma-3500: Rawḥ narrated to us, Zakariyyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to us, that he heard ʿIkrimah say: Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: {And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a fitnah for the people} [al-Isrāʾ: 60].
