He said: It was something the Prophet ﷺ was shown while awake; he saw it with his own eye when he was taken to Bayt al-Maqdis.
items.ma-3501: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us. And ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: I heard ʿAṭāʾ say: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: I heard the Prophet of Allah ﷺ say: “If the son of Ādam had a valley of wealth, he would love to have its like in addition to it; and nothing fills the self of the son of Ādam except dust; and Allah accepts the repentance of whoever repents.” Ibn ʿAbbās said: So I do not know whether it is from the Qurʾān or not.
items.ma-3502: Rawḥ narrated to us, ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr narrated to us, ʿIkrimah ibn Khālid ibn al-Mughīrah narrated to me, that Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated to him, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: I came to my maternal aunt Maymūnah, and I found that night of hers to be with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ … So he mentioned the like of the ḥadīth of Yazīd, except that he said: Until, when the first dawn rose, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ held back for a little while, until, when the Ṣubḥ lit up for him, he rose and prayed the witr, nine rakʿahs, giving the salām after every two rakʿahs. Until, when he finished his witr, he held back a little, until, when it became morning in himself, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose, and prayed the two rakʿahs of Fajr for the Ṣubḥ prayer, then laid his side down and slept until I heard his snoring. He said: Then Bilāl came and woke him for the prayer, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose and prayed the Ṣubḥ.
items.ma-3503: Rawḥ narrated to us, Zakariyyā narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, that Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed in Makkah thirteen years, and he died when he was sixty-three years old.
items.ma-3504: Rawḥ narrated to us, Zakariyyā narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man said: O Messenger of Allah, indeed his mother has died; will it benefit her if I give ṣadaqah on her behalf? He said: “Yes.” He said: Then I have an orchard, and I make you witness that I have given it in ṣadaqah on her behalf.
items.ma-3505: Rawḥ narrated to us, Zakariyyā narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to us: that Ibn ʿAbbās used to mention: that the Prophet ﷺ permitted the menstruating woman to depart before performing ṭawāf, if she had performed ṭawāf in the Ifāḍah.
items.ma-3506: Rawḥ narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥafṣah narrated to us, Ibn Shihāb narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah sought a ruling from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning a vow upon his mother, who died before fulfilling it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Fulfil it on her behalf.”
items.ma-3507: Rawḥ narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Raqabah ibn Maṣqalah ibn Raqabah, from Ṭalḥah al-Iyāmī, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said to me: Marry, for the best of us was the one with the most women, ﷺ.
items.ma-3508: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Yaʿlā informed me, that he heard ʿIkrimah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, say: Ibn ʿAbbās informed us: that the mother of Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah died while he was absent from her, so he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, my mother has died while I was absent from her; will it benefit her if I give ṣadaqah on her behalf? He said: “Yes.” He said: Then I make you witness that my garden, al-Mikhraf, is ṣadaqah on her behalf.
items.ma-3509: Rawḥ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah al-Barrāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ assumed iḥrām for Ḥajj, and arrived on the fourth that had passed of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, and led us in the Ṣubḥ prayer at al-Baṭḥāʾ, then said: “Whoever wishes to make it an ʿumrah, let him make it so.”
items.ma-3510: Rawḥ narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥafṣah narrated to us, Ibn Shihāb narrated to us, from Abū Sinān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Is Ḥajj every year? He said: “No, but one Ḥajj; so whoever performs Ḥajj after that, it is voluntary. And had I said: Yes, it would have become obligatory; and had it become obligatory, you would not have heard and you would not have obeyed.”
items.ma-3511: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah ﵎ will surely resurrect the Stone on the Day of Resurrection, and it will have two eyes with which it sees and a tongue with which it speaks, bearing witness over whoever touched it in truth.”
items.ma-3512: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions performed ʿumrah from al-Jiʿirrānah, and they performed iḍṭibāʿ, placing their cloaks under their armpits and putting them over their shoulders, then they performed ramal.
items.ma-3513: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Abū Bakr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the night of al-Muzdalifah: “O sons of my brother, O Banū Hāshim, hasten before the crowding of the people, and let none of you throw at al-ʿAqabah until the sun rises.”
items.ma-3514: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, he said: Kāmil informed us, from Ḥabīb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I spent the night with my maternal aunt Maymūnah. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke during the night … So he mentioned the ḥadīth. He said: Then he bowed. He said: And I saw him say in his bowing: “Glory be to my Rabb, al-ʿAẓīm.” Then he raised his head and praised Allah as much as he willed to praise Him. He said: Then he prostrated. He said: And he used to say in his prostration: “Glory be to my Rabb, al-Aʿlā.” He said: Then he raised his head. He said: And he used to say between the two prostrations: “Rabb, forgive me, and have mercy on me, and mend me, and raise me, and provide for me, and guide me.”
items.ma-3515: Rawḥ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Murrah narrated to us, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, he said: We tried to sight the crescent of the month of Ramaḍān at Dhāt ʿIrq, so we sent to Ibn ʿAbbās to ask him, and he said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ has extended it for its sighting; so if it is obscured for you, then complete the count.”
items.ma-3516: Rawḥ narrated to us, Zakariyyāʾ ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed in Makkah for thirteen years, and he died when he was sixty-three years old.
items.ma-3517: Rawḥ narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, ʿIkrimah narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent at forty years of age, and he stayed in Makkah for thirteen years while revelation came to him; then he was commanded to emigrate, so he emigrated and [lived] ten years, and he died when he was sixty-three years old, ﷺ.
items.ma-3518: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Abū Ḥāḍir informed me, he said: Ibn ʿUmar was asked about the jar in which nabīdh is made. He said: Allah and His Messenger forbade it. So the man went to Ibn ʿAbbās and told him what Ibn ʿUmar had said, and Ibn ʿAbbās said: He spoke truly. The man said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Which jar did he forbid? He said: Everything that is made of clay.
items.ma-3519: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the verse of debt was revealed, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The first to deny was Ādam ﵇ — he said it three times. When Allah created Ādam ﵊, He wiped his back and brought out from him whatever is to be created until the Day of Resurrection, and He began to present them to him. He saw among them a man who shone, and he said: O Rabb, which of my sons is this? He said: This is your son Dāwūd. He said: O Rabb, how long is his lifespan? He said: Sixty years. He said: O Rabb, increase his lifespan. He said: No, unless you increase it yourself from your own lifespan. The lifespan of Ādam was a thousand years, so he gave him forty years from his lifespan, and Allah ﷿ wrote a document against him and had the angels witness it against him. When Ādam ﵇ was attended [by death], the angels came to him to take his soul, and he said: My appointed term has not yet come; forty years of my lifespan remain. They said: You gave them to your son Dāwūd. He said: I did not do so, and I gave him nothing. And Allah ﷿ produced the document against him, and had the angels stand against him.”
items.ma-3520: Rawḥ narrated to us, Zamʿah narrated to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from Abū Sinān al-Duʾalī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah ﷿ has prescribed the Ḥajj upon you.” Al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis said: Always, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “Rather, one Ḥajj; and had I said: Yes, it would have become obligatory.”
items.ma-3521: Rawḥ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: A sheep belonging to Maymūnah died, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Why did you not benefit from its hide?” They said: It is carrion. He said: “Indeed, the tanning of the skin is its purification.”
items.ma-3522: Rawḥ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Abū Mijlaz: that a man came to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: I threw [pebbles] with six, or seven. He said: I do not know: did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ throw at the Jamrah with six or seven?
items.ma-3523: Rawḥ narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped on his head while in iḥrām, because of a headache he had.
items.ma-3524: Rawḥ narrated to us, Zakariyyāʾ ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to us, from Ṭāwūs: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped on his head while in iḥrām.
items.ma-3525: Rawḥ and Abū Dāwūd narrated to us, in meaning, both said: Hishām ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Abū Ḥassān al-Aʿraj, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ prayed at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, then marked the sacrificial animal on the right side of the hump, then wiped the blood from it, and garlanded it with two sandals, then mounted his she-camel; and when it stood upright with him on al-Baydāʾ, he entered iḥrām. He said: So he entered iḥrām at noon; Abū Dāwūd said: for Ḥajj.
items.ma-3526: Rawḥ narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, from al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Ibn ʿUmar used to perform wuḍūʾ three times, ascribing it to the Prophet ﷺ; and Ibn ʿAbbās used to perform wuḍūʾ once each time, ascribing it to the Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-3527: Rawḥ and ʿAffān narrated to us, both said: Ḥammād narrated to us, from Qays. ʿAffān said: Ḥammād informed us in his ḥadīth, he said: Qays informed us, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The Prophet ﷺ came to Zamzam, and we drew a bucket for him, and he drank, then spat into it; then we poured it back into Zamzam. Then he said: “Were it not that you would be overpowered over it, I would have drawn with my own two hands.”
items.ma-3528: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from Ḥumayd, from Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh: that a Bedouin said to Ibn ʿAbbās: What is the matter with the family of Muʿāwiyah, that they give water and honey to drink, and the family of so-and-so give milk to drink, while you give nabīdh to drink? Is it out of stinginess on your part, or need? Ibn ʿAbbās said: Neither stinginess nor need is in us; rather, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us, with Usāmah ibn Zayd riding behind him, and asked for a drink, so we gave him to drink from this — meaning the nabīdh of the siqāyah — and he drank from it and said: “You have done well; do thus.”
items.ma-3529: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came for the water of Zamzam, and we gave him to drink, and he drank standing.
items.ma-3530: Rawḥ narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Abū Ḥarīz, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ forbade that a woman be married over her paternal aunt, or over her maternal aunt.
items.ma-3531: Ḥujayn ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray the Witr with three [rakʿahs]: with {Glorify the name of your Rabb, al-Aʿlā}, and {Say: O disbelievers}, and {Say: He is Allah, One}.
items.ma-3532: Rawḥ narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us. And ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, he said: Muʿāwiyah would not come to any of the corners of the House without touching it. Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ only used to touch these two corners. Muʿāwiyah said: None of its corners is abandoned. ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said: The two corners: the Yamānī and the Stone.
items.ma-3533: Rawḥ narrated to us, al-Thawrī narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, he said: I was with Muʿāwiyah and Ibn ʿAbbās while they were performing ṭawāf around the House. Ibn ʿAbbās would touch the two corners, and Muʿāwiyah would touch all the corners. Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to touch only these two corners: the Yamānī and the Black. Muʿāwiyah said: None of them is abandoned.
items.ma-3534:
Rawḥ narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he performed ʿumrah from al-Jiʿrānah, and performed raml around the House for three [circuits] and walked four circuits.
Rawḥ narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ghanawī, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, he said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Your people claim that the Prophet ﷺ performed raml around the House and that that is a Sunnah. He said: They spoke truly and they lied. I said: In what did they speak truly and lie? He said: They spoke truly: he performed raml around the House; and they lied: it is not a Sunnah. Quraysh said — at the time of al-Ḥudaybiyah —: Leave Muḥammad and his Companions until they die the death of the nasal worms. Then when they made peace with the Prophet ﷺ on the condition that they come the following year and stay in Makkah for three [days], the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came the following year, while the polytheists were on the side of Quʿayqiʿān, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Perform raml around the House three [circuits],” and it is not a Sunnah.
items.ma-3535: Yūnus and Surayj narrated to us, both said: Ḥammād narrated to us, from Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ghanawī, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
items.ma-3536: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ḥammād — meaning Ibn Salamah — narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that Quraysh said: Muḥammad and his Companions — the fever of Yathrib has weakened them. Then when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in the year in which he performed ʿumrah, he said to his Companions: “Perform raml around the House, so that the polytheists see your strength.” And when they performed raml, Quraysh said: It has not weakened them.
items.ma-3537: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ḥammād — meaning Ibn Salamah — narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The Black Stone is from Paradise, and it was whiter than snow, until the sins of the people of shirk blackened it.”
items.ma-3538: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Yūnus narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rinsed his mouth after milk, and said: “It has fat.”
items.ma-3539: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Yūnus narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among the most generous of people, and he was at his most generous in Ramaḍān, when Jibrīl met him; he would meet him every night and study the Qurʾān with him. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when Jibrīl met him, was more generous than the wind that is sent forth.
items.ma-3540: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Shuʿbah informed us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was given victory by the east wind, and ʿĀd were destroyed by the west wind.”
items.ma-3541: Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, that Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās narrated to him, from his father, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me: that he spent the night at the Prophet's ﷺ, and he woke during the night, took his siwāk and cleaned his teeth with it, then performed wuḍūʾ while saying: {Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth} [Āl ʿImrān: 190], until he had recited these verses and reached the end of the sūrah. Then he prayed two rakʿahs, in which he prolonged the standing, the bowing and the prostration; then he turned away, until I heard the breath of sleep. Then he woke, used the siwāk and performed wuḍūʾ, while saying [it], until he had done that three times. Then he prayed the Witr with three [rakʿahs]. Then Bilāl the muʾadhdhin came to him, and he went out to the prayer, saying: “O Allah, place light in my heart, and place light in my hearing, and place light in my sight, and place light before me, and behind me, and place light on my right, and on my left, and above me, and beneath me. O Allah, magnify light for me.”
items.ma-3542: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Abū Balj, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The first to pray with the Prophet ﷺ after Khadījah was ʿAlī. And once he said: He accepted Islam.
items.ma-3543: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died when I was fifteen years old.
items.ma-3544: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah informed us, al-Ḥakam and Abū Bishr narrated to us, from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade every beast of prey that has a fang, and every bird that has a talon.
items.ma-3545: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad informed us, Thābit informed us. And Ḥasan ibn Mūsā: Thābit narrated to us, he said: Hilāl narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to spend the nights — ʿAbd al-Ṣamad said: successive ones — hungry, and his family did not find supper, and most of their bread was barley bread.
items.ma-3546: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad and Ḥasan narrated to us, both said: Thābit narrated to us — Ḥasan said: Abū Zayd —; ʿAbd al-Ṣamad said: he said: Hilāl narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ was taken by night to Bayt al-Maqdis, then he came back that same night and told them of his journey, and of the sign of Bayt al-Maqdis, and of their caravan. Some people said — Ḥasan said: Do we believe Muḥammad in what he says?! — and they apostatised as disbelievers, so Allah struck their necks together with Abū Jahl. And Abū Jahl said: Muḥammad frightens us with the tree of Zaqqūm! Bring dates and butter, and devour [it]! And he saw the Dajjāl in his form, a vision of the eye, not a vision of sleep, and ʿĪsā, and Mūsā, and Ibrāhīm, صَلَوَاتُ اللهِ عَلَيْهِمْ. And the Prophet ﷺ was asked about the Dajjāl, and he said: “Pale white, pure white — Ḥasan said: He said: I saw him faylamānī, pale white, pure white — one of his eyes is upright, as if it were a brilliant star, as if the hair of his head were the branches of a tree. And I saw ʿĪsā a young man, white, curly-haired, sharp of sight, slender in build; and I saw Mūsā dark, brown, with abundant hair — Ḥasan said: of hair — strong in build; and I looked at Ibrāhīm, and I did not look at any limb of his limbs except that I looked at [its like] from myself; it was as if he were your companion. And Jibrīl ﵇ said: Greet Mālik, so I greeted him.”
items.ma-3547:
ʿAbd al-Ṣamad and Ḥasan narrated to us, both said: Thābit narrated to us, Hilāl narrated to us: that ʿIkrimah was asked — Ḥasan said: I asked ʿIkrimah — about the fasting person: may he have himself cupped? He said: It was only disliked because of weakness.
And he narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās — Ḥasan said: then he narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās —: that the Prophet ﷺ had himself cupped while in iḥrām, because of a morsel he had eaten from a poisoned sheep, which a woman from the people of Khaybar had poisoned.
items.ma-3548: Hushaym narrated to us, Mughīrah narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd narrated to us, he said: I saw Ibn Masʿūd throw at the Jamrah, the Jamrah of al-ʿAqabah, from the bottom of the valley, then he said: This — by the One besides Whom there is no deity — is the standing place of the one upon whom Sūrat al-Baqarah was sent down.
items.ma-3549: Hushaym narrated to us, Ḥuṣayn informed us, from Kathīr ibn Mudrik al-Ashjaʿī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd: that ʿAbd Allāh recited the talbiyah when he moved on from Jamʿ, and it was said: Is this a Bedouin? ʿAbd Allāh said: Have the people forgotten, or have they gone astray?! I heard the one upon whom Sūrat al-Baqarah was sent down say in this place: “Labbayka, O Allah, labbayka.”
items.ma-3550: Hushaym narrated to us, Ḥuṣayn informed us, from Hilāl ibn Yisāf, from Abū Ḥayyān al-Ashjaʿī, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: He said to me: Recite to me from the Qurʾān. He said: I said to him: Did I not learn it from you, while you teach us to recite? He said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ one day, and he said: “Recite to me from the Qurʾān.” He said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, was it not sent down upon you, and have we not learned it from you? He said: “Yes, but I love to hear it from someone other than me.”
items.ma-3551: Hushaym narrated to us, Mughīrah informed us, from Abū Razīn, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I recited to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, and when I reached this verse: {How then will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you against these as a witness?} [al-Nisāʾ: 41], he said: his eyes ﷺ overflowed.
items.ma-3552: Hushaym narrated to us, Sayyār and Mughīrah informed us, from Abū Wāʾil, he said: Ibn Masʿūd said: Two things — meaning: one of them I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the other is from myself: “Whoever dies while setting up a rival to Allah will enter the Fire”; and I say: Whoever dies not setting up a rival to Allah and not associating anything with Him will enter Paradise.
items.ma-3553: Hushaym narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, he said: I heard Abū ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrating, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The drop of fluid remains in the womb for forty days in its state, without changing; then when the forty have passed, it becomes a clot, then a lump of flesh likewise, then bones likewise. Then when Allah wishes to fashion its creation, He sends an angel to it, and the angel who is next to it says: O Rabb, male or female? Wretched or felicitous? Short or tall? Deficient or in excess? His sustenance and his term? Healthy or ailing? He said: So he writes all of that.” Then a man from the people said: Then why is there action, when all of this has already been finished with? He said: “Act, for everyone will be directed to that for which he was created.”
items.ma-3554: Hushaym narrated to us, al-ʿAwwām informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Muḥammad, a mawlā of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from Abū ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There are no two Muslims who have three of their children die, who had not reached the ḥinth, except that they will be for him a strong fortress against the Fire.” It was said: O Messenger of Allah, and if there are two? He said: “Even if there are two.” Abū Dharr said: O Messenger of Allah, I have sent ahead only two. He said: “Even if there are two.” He said: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb Abū al-Mundhir, the master of the reciters, said: I have sent ahead only one. He said: It was said to him: “And if it is one?” And he said: “That is only at the first shock.”
items.ma-3555: Hushaym narrated to us, Abū al-Zubayr informed us, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr, from Abū ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from his father: that the polytheists occupied the Prophet ﷺ on the day of al-Khandaq from four prayers, until what Allah willed of the night had passed. He said: He said: “So he commanded Bilāl, and he called the adhān, then he called the iqāmah and prayed the Ẓuhr prayer, then he called the iqāmah and prayed the ʿAṣr prayer, then he called the iqāmah and prayed the Maghrib prayer, then he called the iqāmah and prayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer.
items.ma-3556: Hushaym narrated to us, al-ʿAwwām informed us, from Jabalah ibn Suḥaym, from Muʾthir ibn ʿAfāzah, from Ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “On the night I was taken by night, I met Ibrāhīm, Mūsā and ʿĪsā.” He said: “They discussed the matter of the Hour, and referred their matter to Ibrāhīm, and he said: I have no knowledge of it. So they referred the matter to Mūsā, and he said: I have no knowledge of it. So they referred the matter to ʿĪsā, and he said: As for its occurrence, no one knows it except Allah. That; and among what my Rabb ﷿ entrusted to me is that the Dajjāl will come out. He said: And with me are two rods; when he sees me, he will melt as lead melts. He said: Then Allah will destroy him, so that the stone and the tree will say: O Muslim, beneath me is a disbeliever, so come and kill him. He said: So Allah will destroy them. Then the people will return to their lands and their homelands. He said: At that time Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj will come out, and they will swarm down from every elevation, and trample their lands; they do not come upon anything except that they destroy it, and they do not pass by any water except that they drink it. Then the people will return to me and complain about them, and I will supplicate Allah against them, and Allah will destroy them and cause them to die, until the earth becomes foul from the stench of their smell. He said: Then Allah ﷿ will send down the rain, and it will sweep away their bodies until it throws them into the sea.” My father said: Something escaped me here which I did not understand: like a hide; and Yazīd — meaning Ibn Hārūn — said: “Then the mountains will be blown away, and the earth will be stretched out as a hide is stretched.” Then he returned to the ḥadīth of Hushaym, he said: “And among what my Rabb ﷿ entrusted to me: that when that is so, the Hour is like the pregnant woman at full term, whose people do not know when she will take them by surprise with her delivery, by night or by day.”
items.ma-3557: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Manṣūr narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: So-and-so slept last night through the prayer. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “That is Shayṭān; he urinated in his ear,” or: “in his two ears.”
items.ma-3558: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, Manṣūr narrated to us, from Muslim ibn Ṣubayḥ, he said: I was with Masrūq in a house in which there was a statue of Maryam, and Masrūq said: Is this the statue of Kisrā? I said: No, but the statue of Maryam. Masrūq said: Indeed, I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, the most severely punished of people on the Day of Resurrection are the picture-makers.”
items.ma-3559: Isḥāq — he is al-Azraq — narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever sees me in sleep has seen me, for it is not fitting for Shayṭān to assume my likeness.”
items.ma-3560: Isḥāq narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When you are three, two must not converse privately without their companion, for that grieves him.”
items.ma-3561: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from Khuṣayf, Abū ʿUbaydah narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the prayer of fear with us. They stood in two rows: one row stood behind the Prophet ﷺ, and one row facing the enemy. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed one rakʿah with the row nearest to him, then they stood up and went away, and stood in the place of those who were facing the enemy, and those came and stood in their place. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed one rakʿah with them, then gave the salām; then they stood and prayed one rakʿah for themselves, then gave the salām; then they went and stood in the place of those who were facing the enemy, and those returned to their place and prayed one rakʿah for themselves, then gave the salām.
items.ma-3562: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, Khuṣayf al-Jazarī narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught him the tashahhud and commanded him to teach it to the people: “All greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.”
items.ma-3563: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We used to greet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in prayer, and he would return the greeting to us. When we returned from al-Najāshī, we greeted him, and he did not return it to us. We said: O Messenger of Allah, we used to greet you in the prayer and you would return it to us? He said: “Indeed, in me — or in the prayer — there is a preoccupation.”
items.ma-3564: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The superiority of a man's prayer in congregation over his prayer alone is twenty-odd degrees.”
items.ma-3565: ʿAmr ibn al-Haytham Abū Qaṭan narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAmr, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: When is Laylat al-Qadr? He said: “Which of you remembers the night of the Ṣahbāwāt?” ʿAbd Allāh said: I do, may my father and my mother be a ransom for you; and in my hand were some dates with which I was eating the suḥūr, screening myself from the dawn with the rear of my saddle, and that was when the moon rose.
items.ma-3566: ʿAmr ibn al-Haytham narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh: that the Prophet ﷺ prayed the Ẓuhr [with] five [rakʿahs], and it was said: Has [something] been added to the prayer? It was said: You prayed five. So he performed two prostrations.
items.ma-3567: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: “The prayer of the group is superior to the prayer of a man alone by twenty-five fold, all of them being like his prayer.”
items.ma-3568: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, he said: Ziyād ibn Abī Maryam informed me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿqil ibn Muqarrin, he said: I entered with my father upon ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, and he said: Did you hear the Prophet ﷺ say: “Remorse is repentance”? He said: Yes. And once he said: I heard him say: “Remorse is repentance.”
items.ma-3569: Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Dharr, from Wāʾil ibn Mahānah, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Give ṣadaqah, O company of women, even from your jewelry, for you are the majority of the people of the Fire.” Then a woman who was not of the prominent women stood up and said: Why, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “Because you curse much, and you are ungrateful to the ʿashīr.”
items.ma-3570: Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh: that the Prophet ﷺ performed the two prostrations after the salām. And once he said: The Prophet ﷺ performed the two prostrations of forgetfulness after the salām.
items.ma-3571: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ: “The Hour will not come until a man from the people of my house takes charge, whose name agrees with my name.” ʿAbd Allāh said: My father said: He narrated it to us in his house, in his upper chamber; I think that one of the children of Jaʿfar ibn Yaḥyā, or Yaḥyā ibn Khālid ibn Yaḥyā, had asked him.
items.ma-3572: ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The days will not come to an end, nor will time pass away, until a man from the people of my house rules over the Arabs, whose name agrees with my name.”
items.ma-3573: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Sufyān, ʿĀṣim narrated to me, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The world will not pass away — or he said: The world will not come to an end — until a man from the people of my house rules over the Arabs, whose name agrees with my name.”
items.ma-3574: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ in a cave, and {By the ones sent forth in succession} was revealed to him, and I took it from his mouth, while his mouth was moist with it. I do not know with which of them he concluded: {Then in what ḥadīth after it will they believe?} [or] {And when it is said to them: Bow down, they do not bow down}. A snake got ahead of us and entered a hole, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “You have been protected from its evil, and it has been protected from your evil.”
items.ma-3575: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We used to greet the Prophet ﷺ when we were in Makkah, before we came to the land of Abyssinia. When we came from the land of Abyssinia, we came to him and greeted him, and he did not return it, and what was near and what was far took hold of me, until they had finished the prayer. Then I asked him, and he said: “Indeed, Allah ﷿ brings about in His command what He wills, and indeed there has been brought about of His command that we do not speak in the prayer.”
items.ma-3576: Sufyān narrated to us, from Jāmiʿ, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Whoever swears an oath by which he takes away the property of a Muslim will meet Allah while He is Ghaḍbān with him.” And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited to us its confirmation from the Book of Allah ﷿: {Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price — those have no share in the Hereafter, and Allāh will not Yukallimuhum} [Āl ʿImrān: 77].
items.ma-3577: Sufyān narrated to us, from Jāmiʿ, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ: “No servant withholds the zakāh of his wealth except that a bald-headed serpent will be made for him, following him; he flees from it while it follows him, and it says: I am your treasure.” Then ʿAbd Allāh recited its confirmation in the Book of Allah: {They will be encircled with that which they were stingy with on the Day of Resurrection} [Āl ʿImrān: 180]. Sufyān once said: It will be encircled around his neck.
items.ma-3578: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, carrying it up to the Prophet ﷺ: “Allah has not sent down a disease except that He has sent down a cure for it; whoever knows it knows it, and whoever is ignorant of it is ignorant of it.”
items.ma-3579: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Shimr, from Mughīrah ibn Saʿd ibn al-Akhram, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not take an estate, lest you become desirous of the world.”
items.ma-3580: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ: “I declare myself free before every khalīl of his khullah; and had I been taking a khalīl, I would have taken Abū Bakr as a khalīl; and your companion is the Khalīl of Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-3581: Sufyān narrated to us, Sulaymān said: I heard Shaqīq say: We were waiting in the mosque for ʿAbd Allāh to come out to us, and Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah — meaning al-Nakhaʿī — came to us. He said: Shall I not go and see? If he is in the house, perhaps I can bring him out to you. So he came to us, and stood over us, and said: Your place is mentioned to me, and I do not come to you only out of dislike that I should bore you. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to take care of us with admonition during the days, out of dislike of weariness for us.
items.ma-3582: Sufyān narrated to us, from Yazīd, from Abū al-Kanūd: I came by a ring one day, and he mentioned it; Ibn Masʿūd saw it on his hand and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the gold ring.
items.ma-3583: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, from Abū Maʿmar, from Ibn Masʿūd: The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two halves, until they looked at it. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Bear witness.”
items.ma-3584: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, from Abū Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: The Prophet ﷺ entered, and around the Kaʿbah were three hundred and sixty idols, and he began to poke them with a stick he had in his hand, saying: {The truth has come, and falsehood neither originates nor repeats} [Sabaʾ: 49], {The truth has come and falsehood has vanished; indeed falsehood is ever bound to vanish} [al-Isrāʾ: 81].
items.ma-3585: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: And none of them is one who goes ahead of it. And it was read to Sufyān: I heard Yaḥyā al-Jābir, from Abū Mājid al-Ḥanafī, he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh say: We asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about walking with the funeral, and he said: “It is followed, and it does not follow.”
items.ma-3586: Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Minā. He said: A snake came out upon us, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Kill it.” So we hurried toward it, but it got ahead of us.
items.ma-3587: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Aʿmash narrating from Shaqīq, he said: ʿAbd Allāh used to come out to us and say: Your place is made known to me, and nothing prevents me from coming out to you except my dislike that I should bore you. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to take care of us with admonition during the days, out of dislike of weariness for us.
items.ma-3588: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad and ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: When one of you bows, let him lay his forearms on his thighs and bend over; then he clasped his palms together, and it is as if I am looking at the splaying of the fingers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: Then he clasped his palms together, and showed them.
items.ma-3589: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: When this verse was revealed: {Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing} [al-Anʿām: 82], it was hard on the people, and they said: O Messenger of Allah, which of us does not wrong himself? He said: “It is not what you mean. Have you not heard what the righteous servant said: {O my son, do not associate anything with Allah; indeed shirk is a great wrong}? [Luqmān: 13] It is only shirk.”
items.ma-3590: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: A man from the People of the Book came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Abū al-Qāsim, has it reached you that Allah ﷿ Yaḥmilu the creatures ʿalā iṣbaʿ, and the heavens ʿalā iṣbaʿ, and the earths ʿalā iṣbaʿ, and the trees ʿalā iṣbaʿ, and the moist earth ʿalā iṣbaʿ?! The Prophet ﷺ laughed until his molars showed, and Allah ﷿ revealed: {And they did not appraise Allah with His true appraisal …} the verse [al-Zumar: 67].
items.ma-3591: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh: that he recited Sūrat Yūsuf at Ḥimṣ, and a man said: It was not revealed like this! ʿAbd Allāh drew near to him and found on him the smell of wine, and said: Do you deny the truth and drink filth?! I will not leave you until I flog you the ḥadd. He said: So he gave him the ḥadd, and said: By Allah, it is thus that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made me recite it.
items.ma-3592: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, he said: I was walking with ʿAbd Allāh at Minā, and ʿUthmān met him and stood with him, talking to him. ʿUthmān said to him: O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, shall we not marry you to a young girl, perhaps she will remind you of what has passed of your time? ʿAbd Allāh said: As for this, if you say that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: “O company of youth, whoever among you is able to bear the capacity for marriage, let him marry, for it is more restraining for the gaze and more protective of the private part; and whoever is not able, let him fast, for it is for him a restraint.”
items.ma-3593: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, he said: ʿUthmān prayed four [rakʿahs] at Minā, and ʿAbd Allāh said: I prayed two rakʿahs with the Prophet ﷺ at Minā, and two rakʿahs with Abū Bakr, and two rakʿahs with ʿUmar.
items.ma-3594: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbīdah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best of people is my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them, then those who follow them; then after that there will come a people whose testimonies precede their oaths, and whose oaths [precede] their testimonies.”
items.ma-3595: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbīdah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I surely know the last of the people of the Fire to come out of the Fire: a man who comes out of it crawling, and it is said to him: Go and enter Paradise. He said: So he goes to enter, and finds that the people have taken the dwellings. He said: So he returns and says: O Rabb, the people have taken the dwellings. He said: It is said to him: Do you remember the time in which you were? He said: He says: Yes. It is said to him: Wish. So he wishes, and it is said: You have what you wished, and ten times the world. He said: So he says: Are You mocking me, when You are al-Malik?!” He said: And I indeed saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laugh until his molars showed.
items.ma-3596: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, if I do well in Islam, will I be held to account for what I did in the Jāhiliyyah? He said: “If you do well in Islam, you will not be held to account for what you did in the Jāhiliyyah; and if you do evil in Islam, you will be taken for the first and the last.”
items.ma-3597: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever swears an oath in which he is a fājir, in order to take away the property of a Muslim man, will meet Allah ﷿ while He is Ghaḍbān with him.” Al-Ashʿath said: Concerning me, by Allah, was that. There was land between me and a man of the Jews, and he denied me, so I brought him before the Prophet ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “Do you have proof?” I said: No. He said to the Jew: “Swear.” I said: O Messenger of Allah, then he will swear and my property will go. So Allah ﷿ revealed: {Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price} [Āl ʿImrān: 77] to the end of the verse.
items.ma-3598: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to me, from Zirr, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I used to graze sheep for ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abū Bakr passed by me. He said: “O boy, is there any milk?” He said: I said: Yes, but I am entrusted. He said: “Then is there a sheep on which the stud has not leapt?” So I brought him a sheep, and he wiped its udder, and milk came down; he milked it into a vessel, and drank, and gave Abū Bakr to drink. Then he said to the udder: “Contract,” and it contracted. He said: Then I came to him after this and said: O Messenger of Allah, teach me from this saying. He said: So he wiped my head and said: “May Allah have mercy on you, for you are a little boy who has been taught.”
items.ma-3599: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, with his chain of narration, he said: Abū Bakr came to him with a hollowed rock, and he milked into it, and he drank, and Abū Bakr drank, and I drank. He said: Then I came to him after that, and said: Teach me from this Qurʾān. He said: “You are a boy who has been taught.” He said: So I took seventy sūrahs from his mouth.
items.ma-3600: Abū Bakr narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: Indeed Allāh Naẓara fī qulūb al-ʿibād, and found the heart of Muḥammad ﷺ the best of the hearts of the servants, so He chose him for Himself and sent him with His message. Then Naẓara fī qulūb al-ʿibād after the heart of Muḥammad, and found the hearts of his Companions the best of the hearts of the servants, so He made them ministers of His Prophet, fighting for His religion. So whatever the Muslims see as good is good with Allah, and whatever they see as bad is bad with Allah.
items.ma-3601: Abū Bakr narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Perhaps you will reach people who pray the prayer not at its time. So when you reach them, pray in your houses at the time that you know, then pray with them, and make it a subḥah.”
items.ma-3602: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed a prayer, and I do not know whether he added or decreased. When he gave the salām, it was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, has something occurred in the prayer? He said: “No; and what is that?” They said: You prayed such and such. He said: So he folded his legs and performed the two prostrations of forgetfulness. When he gave the salām, he said: “I am only a human being; I forget as you forget. And when one of you doubts in the prayer, let him aim for the correct [course of] the prayer; then when he gives the salām, let him perform two prostrations.”
items.ma-3603: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Khaythamah, from a man of his people, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no night-talk after the prayer — meaning: the last ʿIshāʾ — except for one of two men: one who prays, or a traveller.”
items.ma-3604: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Some people said: O Messenger of Allah, will we be held to account for our deeds in the Jāhiliyyah? He said: “Whoever among you does well in Islam will not be held to account for it, and whoever does evil will be taken for his first and last deed.”
items.ma-3605: Jarīr narrated to us, from al-Rukayn, from al-Qāsim ibn Ḥassān, from his paternal uncle ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥarmalah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to dislike ten qualities: wearing a ring of gold, dragging the izār, yellowness — meaning khalūq — changing grey hair — Jarīr said: he only means by that: plucking it —, removing the water from its place, the ruqyahs except with the Muʿawwidhāt, spoiling a child, not forbidding it, tying amulets, displaying adornment in other than its place, and casting the dice.
items.ma-3606: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, Sulaymān narrated to me, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh — Sulaymān said: and part of the ḥadīth is from ʿAmr ibn Murrah. He said: And my father narrated to me, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Recite to me.” He said: I said: Shall I recite to you, when it was revealed upon you? He said: “I love to hear it from someone other than me.” So I recited, until when I reached: {How then will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you against these as a witness?} [al-Nisāʾ: 41], he said: I saw his eyes shedding tears.
items.ma-3607: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq ibn Salamah, he said: A man of Banū Bajīlah, called Nahīk ibn Sinān, came to ʿAbd Allāh and said: O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, how do you recite this verse: do you find it with a yāʾ or with an alif: {from water not āsin} [Muḥammad: 15]? ʿAbd Allāh said to him: Have you counted all of the Qurʾān except this? He said: I recite the Mufaṣṣal in one rakʿah. ʿAbd Allāh said: Hurriedly, like the hurried recitation of poetry?! Indeed among the best of the prayer are the bowing and the prostration; and there will be people who recite the Qurʾān and it will not pass beyond their collarbones, but when it is recited and settles firmly in the heart, it benefits. I indeed know the parallels that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite, two sūrahs in one rakʿah. He said: Then he stood up and went in. Then ʿAlqamah came and went in to him. He said: We said to him: Ask him for us about the parallels that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite, two sūrahs in one rakʿah. He said: So he went in and asked him, then came out to us and said: Twenty sūrahs from the beginning of the Mufaṣṣal, in the arrangement of ʿAbd Allāh.
items.ma-3608: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a distribution one day. He said: A man of the Anṣār said: Indeed this is a distribution by which Wajh Allāh ﷿ was not sought! He said: I said: O enemy of Allah, I will surely inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of what you said. He said: So he mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and his face turned red. He said: Then he said: “May the mercy of Allah be upon Mūsā; he was harmed with more than this, and was patient.”
items.ma-3609: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A woman must not have bodily contact with another woman, so that she describes her to her husband as if he were looking at her.”
items.ma-3610: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We were walking with the Prophet ﷺ, and he passed by Ibn Ṣayyād, and said: “I have concealed something for you.” Ibn Ṣayyād said: Dukh. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Be gone! You will not go beyond your measure.” ʿUmar said: O Messenger of Allah, let me strike his neck. He said: “No. If he is the one you fear, you will not be able to kill him.”
items.ma-3611: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: It is as if I am looking at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recounting a prophet whom his people struck, as he wipes the blood from his face and says: “O my Rabb, forgive my people, for they do not know.”
items.ma-3612: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: Which sin is greatest? He said: “That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you.” He said: Then which? He said: “That you kill your child for fear that he will eat with you.” He said: Then which? He said: “That you commit zinā with the wife of your neighbour.” ʿAbd Allāh said: So Allah revealed the confirmation of that: {And those who do not invoke another deity along with Allah, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit zinā — and whoever does that will meet athām} [al-Furqān: 68].
items.ma-3613: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Muslim, from Masrūq, he said: A man came to ʿAbd Allāh and said: I left a man in the mosque interpreting the Qurʾān by his own opinion; he says about this verse: {The Day when the heaven brings a visible smoke} [al-Dukhān: 10] to its end: A smoke will cover them on the Day of Resurrection, taking hold of their breaths, until there afflicts them from it something like the condition of a cold! He said: ʿAbd Allāh said: Whoever knows a knowledge, let him speak by it, and whoever does not know, let him say: Allah knows best; for it is part of a man's understanding that he says about what he does not know: Allah knows best. This was only because when Quraysh stubbornly disobeyed the Prophet ﷺ, he supplicated against them for years like the years of Yūsuf, so famine and hardship afflicted them until they ate bones, and a man would look at the sky and see between himself and the sky something like the appearance of smoke because of the hardship. So Allah ﷿ revealed: {So watch for the Day when the heaven brings a visible smoke. It will cover the people; this is a painful punishment}. Then [one] came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it was said: O Messenger of Allah, ask Allah for rain for Muḍar, for they have perished. He said: So he supplicated for them, and Allah ﷿ revealed: {Indeed, We are removers of the punishment} [al-Dukhān: 15]. Then when it afflicted them a second time they returned, and it was revealed: {The Day We seize with the greatest seizure; indeed We are Muntaqimūn} [al-Dukhān: 16] — the day of Badr.
items.ma-3614: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿUmārah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I was hiding myself by the coverings of the Kaʿbah, and three persons came: a Qurashī and his two in-laws who were Thaqafīs, or a Thaqafī and his two in-laws who were Qurashīs, abundant in the fat of their bellies, little in the understanding of their hearts. They spoke words that I did not hear! One of them said: Do you think Allāh Yasmaʿu this speech of ours? The other said: I think that when we raise our voices Samiʿahu, and when we do not raise them lam Yasmaʿhu. The other said: If Samiʿa any of it, Samiʿahu all of it. He said: So I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah ﷿ revealed: {And you were not concealing yourselves lest your hearing and your sight and your skins testify against you} up to His saying: {That was your assumption that you assumed about your Rabb; it has ruined you, so you have become among the losers} [Fuṣṣilat: 22–23].
items.ma-3615: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, from the son of the brother of Zaynab, from Zaynab the wife of ʿAbd Allāh, she said: ʿAbd Allāh, when he came back from an errand and reached the door, would clear his throat and spit, disliking to burst in upon something of ours that he dislikes. She said: And one day he came and cleared his throat. She said: And with me was an old woman reciting ruqyah over me for erysipelas, so I put her under the bed. Then he came in and sat beside me, and saw a thread on my neck. He said: What is this thread? She said: I said: A thread in which ruqyah was recited for me. She said: So he took it and cut it. Then he said: Indeed the family of ʿAbd Allāh are free of need of shirk. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed, the ruqyahs, the amulets and the tiwalah are shirk.” She said: So I said to him: Why do you say this, when my eye was discharging, and I used to go to so-and-so the Jew, who would recite ruqyah over it, and when he recited over it, it would settle?! He said: That was only the work of Shayṭān; he used to prod it with his hand, and when you recited ruqyah over it he held back from it. It would have sufficed you to say as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Remove the affliction, Rabb of the people; heal, You are al-Shāfī; there is no healing except Your healing, a healing that leaves no sickness behind.”
items.ma-3616: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no one with more Ghayrah than Allah ﷿, and for that reason He forbade the immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is hidden; and there is no one to whom praise is Aḥabb ilayhi more than to Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-3617: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: To swear by Allah nine times that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was killed is more beloved to me than that I swear once; and that is because Allah ﷿ took him as a prophet and made him a shahīd.
items.ma-3618: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was suffering from fever, and I touched him, and said: O Messenger of Allah, you are suffering a severe fever? He said: “Yes, I suffer fever as two men among you suffer it.” I said: Then you have two rewards? He said: “Yes. By the One in whose Yad is my soul, there is no Muslim on the earth who is afflicted with harm, from illness or other than it, except that Allah removes his sins from him by it, as a tree sheds its leaves.”
items.ma-3619: Yaʿlā narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us …, the like of it.
items.ma-3620: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Keep up with these codices — and perhaps he said: the Qurʾān — for it is more apt to slip away from the breasts of men than livestock from their hobbles. He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﵊ said: “Let none of you say: I have forgotten such-and-such verse; rather, he was made to forget.”
items.ma-3621: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The blood of a Muslim man who bears witness that there is no deity except Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah is not lawful except for one of three: the thayyib who commits zinā, a life for a life, and the one who abandons his religion, separating from the community.”
items.ma-3622: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Whenever we sat with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the prayer, we would say: Peace be upon Allah before His servants; peace be upon Jibrīl; peace be upon Mīkāʾīl; peace be upon so-and-so; peace be upon so-and-so. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard us and said: “Indeed Allāh — He is al-Salām. So when one of you sits in the prayer, let him say: All greetings are for Allah, and the prayers, and the good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. For when he says it, it reaches every righteous servant in the heaven and the earth. I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. Then afterwards let him choose whatever supplication he wishes.”
items.ma-3623:
Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Muslim al-Hajarī narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Whoever is pleased to meet Allah ﷿ tomorrow as a Muslim, let him keep to these obligatory prayers wherever they are called, for they are among the sunnahs of guidance; and Allah ﷿ legislated for your Prophet the sunnahs of guidance. There is none of you but has a place of prayer in his house; and if you prayed in your houses as this one who stays behind prays in his house, you would have abandoned the sunnah of your Prophet, and if you abandoned the sunnah of your Prophet, you would go astray. I saw us when none stayed away from it except a hypocrite whose hypocrisy was known, and I saw the man being supported between two men until he was made to stand in the row.
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no man who performs wuḍūʾ and does the wuḍūʾ well, then comes to one of the mosques and takes a step, except that a degree is raised for him by it, or a sin is removed from him by it, or a good deed is written for him by it” — to the extent that we would bring the steps close together — “and indeed the superiority of a man's prayer in congregation over his prayer alone is twenty-five degrees.”
items.ma-3624: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to us — and he is the truthful, the one who is believed: “Indeed, the creation of each of you is gathered in his mother's belly in forty days; then he becomes a clot likewise; then he becomes a lump of flesh likewise; then the angel is sent to him and breathes the soul into him, and he is commanded with four words: his sustenance, his term, his deeds, and whether he is wretched or felicitous. By the One besides Whom there is no deity, one of you does the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is nothing between him and it except a cubit, then the Book overtakes him, and he is sealed with the deeds of the people of the Fire, and enters it; and a man does the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is nothing between him and it except a cubit, then the Book overtakes him, and he is sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise, and enters it.”
items.ma-3625: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said one word, and I said another. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever dies not associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise.” He said: And I said: Whoever dies associating something with Allah will enter the Fire.
items.ma-3626:
Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Which of you is the one to whom the wealth of his heir is more beloved than his own wealth?” They said: O Messenger of Allah, there is none of us but his own wealth is more beloved to him than the wealth of his heir. He said: “Know that there is none of you but the wealth of his heir is more beloved to him than his own wealth. Your wealth is only what you send ahead, and the wealth of your heir is what you leave behind.”
He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whom do you count among you as the ṣuraʿah?” He said: We said: The one whom men cannot throw down. He said: He said: “No, but the ṣuraʿah is the one who controls himself at the time of anger.”
He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whom do you count among you as the raqūb?” He said: We said: The one who has no child. He said: “No, but the raqūb is the one who has not sent ahead anything of his children.”
items.ma-3627:
Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us two ḥadīths, one of them from himself and the other from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: ʿAbd Allāh said: Indeed the believer sees his sins as if he were at the foot of a mountain, fearing that it will fall upon him; and indeed the sinner sees his sins like a fly that landed on his nose. He said to it thus, and it flew away.
He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allāh Afraḥu bi-tawbat aḥadikum than a man who set out in a desert land, a place of destruction, with his mount carrying his food, his drink, his provisions and what suits him; and he lost it, and went out in search of it, until when death overtook him without his finding it, he said: I will return to my place where I lost it, and die in it. He said: So he came to his place, and his eye overcame him, and he woke, and behold, his mount was at his head, carrying his food, his drink, his provisions and what suits him.”
items.ma-3628: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿUmārah, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh …, like it.
items.ma-3629:
Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd, and al-Aʿmash, from ʿUmārah, from al-Aswad, both said: ʿAbd Allāh said: Indeed the believer sees his sins as if he were at the foot of a mountain, fearing that it will fall upon him; and indeed the sinner sees his sins like a fly that landed on his nose. He said with it thus, and it flew away.
He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allāh Afraḥu bi-tawbat aḥadikum than a man who set out in a desert land — then Abū Muʿāwiyah said: Both said: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us two ḥadīths, one of them from himself and the other from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — a place of destruction, with him his mount, upon it his provisions, his food, his drink and what suits him; and he lost it, and went out in search of it, until when death overtook him, he said: I will return to my place where I lost it, and die in it. He said: So he returned, and his eye overcame him, and he woke, and behold, his mount was at his head, upon it his provisions, his food, his drink and what suits him.”
items.ma-3630: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “No soul is killed unjustly except that upon the first son of Ādam is a share of its blood, because he was the first to set the practice of killing.”
items.ma-3631: Abū Muʿāwiyah and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash; and Yaḥyā, from al-Aʿmash: ʿUmārah narrated to me, al-Aswad narrated to me, in meaning, from ʿUmārah, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh: Let none of you give Shayṭān a share of himself, thinking only that it is a duty upon him not to turn away except to his right. I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and most of his turning away was to his left.
items.ma-3632:
Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: When it was the day of Badr, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “What do you say about these captives?” He said: Abū Bakr said: O Messenger of Allah, they are your people and your family; keep them alive and be lenient with them; perhaps Allah will accept their repentance. He said: And ʿUmar said: O Messenger of Allah, they expelled you and called you a liar; bring them forward and strike their necks. He said: And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah said: O Messenger of Allah, look for a valley with much firewood, and put them into it, then kindle a fire upon them. He said: Al-ʿAbbās said: You have severed your kinship. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went in and did not reply to them with anything. He said: Some people said: He will take the saying of Abū Bakr; and some people said: He will take the saying of ʿUmar; and some people said: He will take the saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah.
He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to them and said: “Indeed Allah softens the hearts of men in Him until they are softer than milk, and indeed Allah hardens the hearts of men in Him until they are harder than stones. And indeed your likeness, O Abū Bakr, is like Ibrāhīm ﵇, who said: {Whoever follows me is of me; and whoever disobeys me — indeed You are al-Ghafūr, al-Raḥīm} [Ibrāhīm: 36]; and your likeness, O Abū Bakr, is like ʿĪsā, who said: {If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Almighty, the Wise} [al-Māʾidah: 118]; and indeed your likeness, O ʿUmar, is like Nūḥ, who said: {My Rabb, do not leave upon the earth any inhabitant of the disbelievers} [Nūḥ: 26]; and indeed your likeness, O ʿUmar, is like Mūsā, who said: My Rabb, harden their hearts, so that they do not believe until they see the painful punishment. You are needy; so let none of them escape except by ransom or the striking of a neck.” ʿAbd Allāh said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, except Suhayl ibn Bayḍāʾ, for I have heard him mention Islam. He said: He was silent. He said: I did not see myself on any day more afraid that stones from the sky would fall upon me than on that day, until he said: “Except Suhayl ibn Bayḍāʾ.” He said: So Allah ﷿ revealed: {It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has caused great slaughter in the land. You desire the goods of this world, while Allah desires the Hereafter; and Allah is Almighty, Wise. Were it not for a Book from Allah that preceded, there would have touched you, for what you took, a great punishment} [al-Anfāl: 67 and 68].
items.ma-3633: Abū Muʿāwiyah — meaning Ibn ʿAmr — narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us …, and he mentioned something like it, except that he said: “Except Suhayl ibn Bayḍāʾ”; and he said regarding the saying of Abū Bakr, he said: Abū Bakr said: O Messenger of Allah, your kindred and your root and your people; overlook them, Allah will rescue them through you from the Fire. He said: And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah said: O Messenger of Allah, you are in a valley with much firewood; so kindle it as a fire, then throw them into it. Al-ʿAbbās said: May Allah sever your kinship.
items.ma-3635: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Jubayr, from Khishf ibn Mālik, from Ibn Masʿūd: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the blood-money in unintentional killing in fifths.
items.ma-3636: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Muslim al-Hajarī narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The needy person is not the one who goes around, nor the one who is turned away by a date or two dates, nor by a morsel or two morsels; rather the needy person is the one who abstains, who does not ask the people for anything, and is not noticed so that ṣadaqah might be given to him.”
items.ma-3637: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿUmārah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: I did not see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray a prayer except at its time, except two prayers: the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers at Jamʿ, and the Fajr prayer on that day, before its time.
items.ma-3638: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Hold to truthfulness, for truthfulness guides to righteousness, and righteousness guides to Paradise; and a man keeps being truthful until he is written with Allah ﷿ as a ṣiddīq. And beware of lying, for lying guides to wickedness, and wickedness guides to the Fire; and a man keeps lying and seeking out lying until he is written with Allah as a liar.”
items.ma-3639: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I am your forerunner at the Ḥawḍ, and I will surely be disputed with over some people, then I will surely be overcome concerning them, and I will say: O Rabb, my Companions! And He will say: You do not know what they innovated after you.”
items.ma-3640: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed there will be rulers over you, and you will see favouritism.” He said: They said: O Messenger of Allah, what should one of us who reaches that do? He said: “Give the right that is upon you, and ask Allah for what is yours.”
items.ma-3641: I heard Yaḥyā, he said: I heard Sulaymān, he said: I heard Zayd ibn Wahb, he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: “Indeed you will see after me favouritism, and matters that you will disapprove of.” He said: We said: What do you command us? He said: “Give them their right, and ask Allah for your right.”
items.ma-3642: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥārithah ibn Muḍarrib, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said to Ibn al-Nawwāḥah: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Were it not that you are a messenger, I would have killed you.” But today you are not a messenger. O Kharashah, stand and strike his neck. He said: So he stood up to him and struck his neck.
items.ma-3643: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, from Abū Qatādah, from Yusayr ibn Jābir, he said: A red wind blew in al-Kūfah, and a man came who had no refrain except: O ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, the Hour has come! He said: And he was reclining, so he sat up, and said: Indeed the Hour will not come until inheritance is not divided and no one rejoices over spoils. He said: An enemy: they gather for the people of Islam, and the people of Islam gather for them … and he mentioned the ḥadīth. He said: The crier comes to them: that the Dajjāl has succeeded them among their offspring. So they discard what is in their hands and advance, and send ten horsemen as a vanguard. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I indeed know their names, and the names of their fathers, and the colours of their horses; they are the best horsemen on the face of the earth on that day,” or he said: “They are among the best horsemen on the face of the earth on that day.”
items.ma-3644: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, he said: Ibn Masʿūd said: I used not to be kept away from the private conversation, nor from such-and-such, nor from such-and-such. Ibn ʿAwn said: He forgot one, and I forgot one. He said: I came to him, and with him was Mālik ibn Murārah al-Rahāwī, and I caught the end of his speech, while he was saying: O Messenger of Allah, I have been allotted of beauty what you see, and I would not like any of the people to surpass me by two shoe-straps or more; is that not transgression? He said: “No, that is not transgression; rather transgression is [the act of] one who is insolent toward — he said: or he said: foolish toward — the truth, and looks down on people.”
items.ma-3645: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAjlān, he said: ʿAwn narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: When a ḥadīth is narrated to you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, think of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [as] the most modest, the most guided, and the most God-fearing.
items.ma-3646: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Sufyān, Sulaymān narrated to me, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I prayed with the Prophet ﷺ one night, and he kept standing until I intended an evil thing. We said: What did you intend? He said: I intended to sit down and leave him.
items.ma-3647: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, Zubayd narrated to me, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Reviling a Muslim is fusūq, and fighting him is kufr.” He said: I said to Abū Wāʾil: Did you hear it from ʿAbd Allāh? He said: Yes.
items.ma-3648: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, Manṣūr narrated to me, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is none of you but has had assigned to him his companion from the jinn and his companion from the angels.” They said: And you, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “And me, but Allah helped me against him, so he commands me only with what is right.”
items.ma-3649: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: Abū al-Zubayr informed me that Mujāhid informed him that Abū ʿUbaydah informed him, from his father, he said: We were sitting in Masjid al-Khayf on the night of ʿArafah that is before the day of ʿArafah, when we heard the rustle of a snake. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Kill it.” He said: So we stood up. He said: It entered a crack in a hole, and a palm frond was brought and a fire was kindled in it, and we took a stick and dug away part of the hole, but did not find it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Leave it; Allah protected it from your evil, as He protected you from its evil.”
items.ma-3650: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Ismāʿīl — he is Ibn Abī Khālid — narrated to us, Qays narrated to me, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: We used to fight alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and we had no women, so we said: O Messenger of Allah, shall we not castrate ourselves?! And he forbade us from that.
items.ma-3651: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Qays narrated to me, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “There is no envy except in two: a man whom Allah has given wealth, and He has empowered him to spend it away in what is right; and a man whom Allah has given wisdom, so he judges by it and teaches it to the people.”
items.ma-3652: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, my father narrated to me, from Abū Yaʿlā, from Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he drew a square line, and drew a line in the middle of the square line, and lines beside the line in the middle of the square line, and a line outside the square line. He said: “Do you know what this is?” They said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: “This is the human being: the middle line; and these lines beside him are the afflictions, biting him from every place: if this one misses him, that one strikes him; and the square line is the term that encompasses him; and the outer line is hope.”
items.ma-3653: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from al-Taymī, from Abū ʿUthmān, from Ibn Masʿūd: that a man kissed a woman, and came to the Prophet ﷺ asking him about its kaffārah, so Allah ﷿ revealed: {Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night; indeed, the good deeds remove the evil deeds} [Hūd: 114]. He said: O Messenger of Allah, is this for me? He said: “For whoever of my ummah does such.”
items.ma-3654: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from al-Taymī, from Abū ʿUthmān, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Let not the adhān of Bilāl prevent any of you from his suḥūr, for he calls the adhān — or he said: he calls out — so that the one among you who is standing in prayer may return, and the one among you who is asleep may awaken. It is not that he says thus” — and he joined his hand and raised it — “but until he says thus.” And Yaḥyā separated between the two index fingers. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: This ḥadīth I did not hear from anyone.
items.ma-3655: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn ʿAtīq narrated to me, from Ṭalq ibn Ḥabīb, from al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Beware: the mutanaṭṭiʿūn have perished,” three times. Yaḥyā said: In a long ḥadīth.
items.ma-3656: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, he said: Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to me, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from his father: that the Prophet ﷺ, in the two rakʿahs, was as if he were on heated stones. I said: Until he stands? He said: Until he stands.
items.ma-3657: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Jāmiʿ ibn Shaddād narrated to me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAlqamah, he said: I heard Ibn Masʿūd say: The Prophet ﷺ returned from al-Ḥudaybiyah at night, and we camped on soft sandy ground, and he said: “Who will guard us?” Bilāl said: I. He said: “Then you will sleep.” He said: No. But he slept until the sun rose. So so-and-so and so-and-so woke up, among them ʿUmar, and he said: Speak out! Then the Prophet ﷺ woke up and said: “Do as you used to do.” When they had done so, he said: “Do thus, for whoever of you sleeps or forgets.”
