items.ma-3658: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, Zubayd narrated to me, from Ibrāhīm, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “He is not of us who strikes the cheeks, tears the openings of garments, and calls with the call of the Jāhiliyyah.”
items.ma-3659: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, ʿAmr ibn Murrah narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salamah, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: Your Prophet ﷺ was given the keys to everything except five: {Indeed, with Allah is the knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs; and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed Allah is al-ʿAlīm, al-Khabīr} [Luqmān: 34].
items.ma-3660: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Zuhayr, he said: Abū Isḥāq narrated to me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from al-Aswad and ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say the takbīr at every lowering and raising, standing and sitting, and he would give the salām on his right and on his left until the whiteness of his cheeks — or his cheek — was seen; and I saw Abū Bakr and ʿUmar do that.
items.ma-3661: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ in a tent, about forty of us, and he said: “Would you be pleased to be a quarter of the people of Paradise?” We said: Yes. He said: “Would you be pleased to be a third of the people of Paradise?” We said: Yes. He said: “By the One in whose Yad is my soul, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise; and that is because none enters Paradise except a Muslim soul, and you, among shirk, are only like a white hair in the skin of a black ox, or a black one in the skin of a red ox.”
items.ma-3662: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, Abū Isḥāq narrated to me, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me while I was praying, and said: “Ask, you will be given, O son of Umm ʿAbd.” Abū Bakr and ʿUmar ﵄ hurried to me; ʿUmar said: Abū Bakr never raced me to anything except that Abū Bakr got ahead of me to it. They asked him about his saying, and he said: It is from my supplication that I hardly ever leave: O Allah, I ask You for bliss that does not perish, and a coolness of the eye that does not run out, and the companionship of the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ in the highest Paradise, the Paradise of eternity.
items.ma-3663: I heard Yaḥyā, he said: I heard Sulaymān, he said: I heard Zayd ibn Wahb, he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: “Indeed you will see after me favouritism, and matters that you will disapprove of.” He said: We said: And what do you command us? He said: “Give them their right, and ask Allah for your right.”
items.ma-3664: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Mujālid, from ʿĀmir, from al-Aswad ibn Yazīd, he said: The iqāmah for the prayer was given in the mosque, and we came walking with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd. When the people bowed, ʿAbd Allāh bowed and we bowed with him while we were walking, and a man passed in front of him and said: Peace be upon you, O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. ʿAbd Allāh said, while bowing: Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth. When he finished, some of the people asked him: Why did you say, when the man greeted you: Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth? He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed among the signs of the Hour is when the greeting is based on acquaintance.”
items.ma-3665: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Mālik ibn Mighwal informed us, from al-Zubayr ibn ʿAdī, from Ṭalḥah, from Murrah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken by night, he was brought to Sidrat al-Muntahā, which is in the sixth heaven. To it ends what is taken up from the earth, and it is received from there; and to it ends what is sent down from above it, and it is received from there. He said: {When there covered the Lote Tree that which covered} [al-Najm: 16]. He said: Moths of gold. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was given three: he was given the five prayers, and he was given the closing verses of Sūrat al-Baqarah, and the muqḥimāt were forgiven for those of his ummah who do not associate anything with Allah.
items.ma-3666: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Sāʾib, from Zādhān, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah has angels roaming on the earth, who convey to me the peace from my ummah.”
items.ma-3667: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Paradise is nearer to one of you than the strap of his sandal, and the Fire is likewise.”
items.ma-3668: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A woman must not have bodily contact with another woman, so as to describe her to her husband as if he were looking at her.”
items.ma-3669: Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿAmr ibn Qays, from ʿĀṣim, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Perform the Ḥajj and the ʿumrah in succession, for they remove poverty and sins as the bellows remove the dross of iron, gold and silver; and the accepted Ḥajj has no reward short of Paradise.”
items.ma-3670: Abū Dāwūd al-Ḥafarī ʿUmar ibn Saʿd narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muhājir, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, then his face changed; then he said: something like this, or close to this.
items.ma-3671: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Abān ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from al-Ṣabbāḥ ibn Muḥammad, from Murrah al-Hamdānī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said one day: “Be modest before Allah ﷿ with true modesty.” He said: We said: O Messenger of Allah, we are modest, and praise be to Allah. He said: “It is not that; rather, whoever is modest before Allah with true modesty, let him guard the head and what it holds, and guard the belly and what it contains, and let him remember death and decay; and whoever desires the Hereafter leaves the adornment of the world. So whoever does that has been modest before Allah ﷿ with true modesty.”
items.ma-3672: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Abān ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from al-Ṣabbāḥ ibn Muḥammad, from Murrah al-Hamdānī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah has apportioned your character among you as He has apportioned your provisions among you; and indeed Allah ﷿ gives the world to whomever He Yuḥibbu and to whomever He lā Yuḥibbu, and does not give the religion except to whomever Aḥabba; so whomever Allah gives the religion, He has Aḥabbahu. By the One in whose Yad is my soul, a servant does not become Muslim until his heart and his tongue are sound, and does not believe until his neighbour is safe from his harms.” They said: And what are his harms, O Prophet of Allah? He said: “His tyranny and his wrongdoing. And a servant does not earn wealth from what is unlawful and spend from it so that it is blessed for him, nor give it as ṣadaqah so that it is accepted from him, nor leave it behind his back, except that it will be his provision to the Fire. Indeed Allah ﷿ does not erase evil with evil, but He erases evil with good; indeed the foul does not erase the foul.”
items.ma-3673: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When the remaining third of the night comes, Allah ﷿ Yahbiṭu ilā the lowest heaven; then the gates of the heaven are opened; then He Yabsuṭu Yadahu and says: Is there any asker, that his request be granted? And He continues like that until the dawn rises.”
items.ma-3674: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The first thing to be judged between the people on the Day of Resurrection will be concerning blood.”
items.ma-3675: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ḥakīm ibn Jubayr, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever asks while he has what suffices him, it will come on the Day of Resurrection as scratches — or lacerations — on his face.” They said: O Messenger of Allah, and what is his sufficiency? He said: “Fifty dirhams, or their equivalent in gold.”
items.ma-3676: Muḥammad ibn al-Sammāk narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from al-Musayyab ibn Rāfiʿ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not buy fish in the water, for it is gharar.”
items.ma-3677: ʿAmmār ibn Muḥammad, the son of the sister of Sufyān al-Thawrī, narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ will send on the Day of Resurrection a caller who will call: O Ādam, Allah commands you to send a contingent from your offspring to the Fire. Ādam will say: O Rabb, from how many? It will be said to him: From every hundred, ninety-nine.” A man from among the people said: Who then is the one among us who is saved after this, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “Do you know what you are among the people? You are among the people only like the mark on the chest of a camel.”
items.ma-3678: ʿAbīdah narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muslim Abū Isḥāq al-Hajarī …, and he mentioned its meaning, and said: “Then Ādam will say: O Rabb, how many shall I send?”
items.ma-3679: ʿAmmār ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Let each of you shield his face from the Fire, even with half a date.”
items.ma-3680: ʿAmmār ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from al-Hajarī, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When the servant of one of you brings his food, let him begin with him and feed him, or let him sit him down with him, for he has taken charge of its heat and its smoke.”
items.ma-3681: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from ʿAlqamah, he said: Ibn Masʿūd said: Shall I not pray for you the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: So he prayed, and did not raise his hands except once.
items.ma-3682: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Aswad ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Masʿūd: that the Prophet ﷺ prostrated [at the recitation of] al-Najm, and the Muslims prostrated, except a man from Quraysh who took a handful of dust and raised it to his forehead and prostrated upon it. ʿAbd Allāh said: I saw him afterwards killed as a disbeliever.
items.ma-3683: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: When {When the help of Allah and the conquest come} was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would say often, when he recited it and bowed: “Glory be to You, O Allah, our Rabb, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me; indeed You are al-Tawwāb al-Raḥīm,” three times.
items.ma-3684: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibrāhīm ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Your permission to come in to me is that you lift the curtain and that you listen to my siwād, until I forbid you.” Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: My father said: Siwādī: my secret. He said: He permitted him to hear his secret.
items.ma-3685: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Prophet ﷺ went out for his need, and said to me: “Find me three stones.” He said: So I brought him two stones and a piece of dung. He said: He took the two stones and threw away the dung, and said: “It is filth.”
items.ma-3686: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to censure for us the night-talk after ʿIshāʾ.
items.ma-3687: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from ʿĪsā ibn ʿĀṣim, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Ṭiyarah is shirk,” and there is none of us but — but Allah removes it through reliance.
items.ma-3688: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I was walking with the Prophet ﷺ in a field in al-Madīnah, and he was leaning on a palm stalk. He said: He passed by some of the Jews, and some of them said to others: Ask him about the spirit. Some of them said: Do not ask him. Then they asked him about the spirit, and said: O Muḥammad, what is the spirit? So he stood, leaning on the palm stalk. He said: I thought that revelation was being sent to him, and he said: {And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is of the command of my Rabb, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little} [al-Isrāʾ: 85]. He said: Some of them said: We told you: Do not ask him.
items.ma-3689: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Beware: I declare myself free before every khalīl of his khullah; and had I taken a khalīl, I would have taken Abū Bakr as a khalīl; your companion is the Khalīl of Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-3690: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Jābir, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to have captives brought to him, and he would give them to the people of a household all together, disliking that he should separate between them.
items.ma-3691: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Qays, from al-Hudhayl ibn Shuraḥbīl, he said: A man came to Abū Mūsā and Salmān ibn Rabīʿah and asked them about a daughter, a son's daughter, and a full sister. They said: To the daughter a half, and to the sister a half; and go to Ibn Masʿūd, for he will follow us. He said: So he went to Ibn Masʿūd and asked him, and told him what they had said, and Ibn Masʿūd said: I would have gone astray then, and I would not be among the guided! I will judge by what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged: to the daughter a half, to the son's daughter a sixth, completing the two-thirds, and what remains to the sister.
items.ma-3692: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh: that the Prophet ﷺ used to say: “O Allah, I ask You for guidance, taqwā, chastity, and sufficiency.”
items.ma-3693: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAmmār ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Duhnī, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd al-Ashjaʿī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Ibn Sumayyah was never presented with two matters except that he chose the more rightly guided of the two.”
items.ma-3694: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gathered us, and we were forty. ʿAbd Allāh said: And I was among the last of those who came to him, and he said: “You will gain, and be given victory, and conquest will be opened for you; so whoever of you reaches that, let him fear Allah, enjoin the good and forbid the wrong; and whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
items.ma-3695: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, he said: I was sitting with ʿAbd Allāh and Abū Mūsā, and they said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed before the Hour there will be days in which ignorance descends, knowledge is raised, and al-harj increases.” He said: We said: And what is al-harj? He said: “Killing.”
items.ma-3696: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Bashīr ibn Salmān narrated to me, from Sayyār Abū Ḥamzah, from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever is visited by a need and lays it before the people, it is likely that his need will not be eased; and whoever lays it before Allah, Allāh Atāhu with immediate sustenance, or with delayed death.”
items.ma-3697: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Khumayr ibn Mālik, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: I recited seventy sūrahs from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while Zayd ibn Thābit still had a forelock in the school.
items.ma-3698: ʿAmr ibn Muḥammad Abū Saʿīd — meaning al-ʿAnqazī: Isrāʾīl and Aswad ibn ʿĀmir informed us; Isrāʾīl narrated to us; and Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Mukhāriq, from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: I witnessed from al-Miqdād — Abū Nuʿaym said: ibn al-Aswad — a scene that for me to be its companion is more beloved to me than whatever is set equal to it: he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was supplicating against the polytheists, and said: By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we will not say as Banū Isrāʾīl said to Mūsā: {Go, you and your Rabb, and fight; indeed we are sitting right here} [al-Māʾidah: 24]; but we will fight on your right, and on your left, and in front of you, and behind you. And I saw the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shine, and he was pleased by that. Aswad said: I saw the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shining because of that, and that pleased him. Abū Nuʿaym said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his face shone, and that pleased him.
items.ma-3699: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh: that the Prophet ﷺ used to give the salām on his right and on his left: “Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah; peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah,” until the whiteness of his cheek was seen.
items.ma-3700:
Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Misʿar, from ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad, from al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Yashkurī, from al-Maʿrūr ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Umm Ḥabībah, the daughter of Abū Sufyān, said: O Allah, let me enjoy my husband the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and my father Abū Sufyān, and my brother Muʿāwiyah. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: “You have asked Allah for fixed terms, counted days, and apportioned provisions; nothing will be hastened before its due time, or delayed beyond its due time. And had you asked Allah to protect you from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave, it would have been better, or more excellent.”
He said: And monkeys were mentioned in his presence — Misʿar said: I think he said: and pigs — that they were among those who had been transformed. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah did not transform anything and leave it offspring or posterity; and monkeys, or pigs, existed before that.”
items.ma-3701: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh: that some people came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: A companion of ours is ailing; shall we cauterize him? He said: He was silent. Then they said: Shall we cauterize him? And he was silent. Then he said: “Cauterize him, and apply heated stones to him well.”
items.ma-3702:
Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Jābir, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Among what I have forgotten, I have not forgotten that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give the salām on his right and on his left: Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah, until the whiteness of his cheeks was seen — or we saw.
Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Sāʾib, from Zādhān, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah has angels roaming on the earth, who convey to me the peace from my ummah.”
items.ma-3703: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “It is not fitting for anyone to say: I am better than Yūnus ibn Mattā.”
items.ma-3704: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from al-Masʿūdī, from ʿUthmān al-Thaqafī — or al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd — al-Masʿūdī doubted — from ʿAbdah al-Nahdī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah has not forbidden a sacred thing except that He knew that someone among you would look into it. Beware, I am holding on to your waists lest you fall into the Fire as moths fall, or flies.”
items.ma-3705: Abū Qaṭan narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbdah al-Nahdī …, and he mentioned it; and likewise Yazīd and Abū Kāmil said: from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd. Rawḥ said: Al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, Abū al-Mughīrah narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, and he said: moths, or flies.
items.ma-3706: Yazīd narrated to us, Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Qays, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: We used to fight with the Prophet ﷺ while we were young men and had no women, so we said: O Messenger of Allah, shall we not castrate ourselves? And he forbade us from that.
items.ma-3707: Yazīd narrated to us, al-ʿAwwām informed us, Abū Isḥāq al-Shaybānī narrated to me, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The millstone of Islam will turn at the head of thirty-five, or thirty-six, or thirty-seven; if they perish, it is the path of one who has perished, and if they remain, their religion will stand for them for seventy years.”
items.ma-3708: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī informed us, ʿĀṣim narrated to me, from Abū Wāʾil, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said, when Ibn al-Nawwāḥah was killed: This one and Ibn Uthāl had come to the Prophet ﷺ as two messengers of Musaylimah the Liar, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: “Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of Allah?” They said: We bear witness that Musaylimah is the Messenger of Allah!! He said: “Were I to kill a messenger, I would have struck your necks.” He said: So it became a sunnah that a messenger is not killed. As for Ibn Uthāl, Allah ʿazza wa-jalla sufficed us against him; and as for this one, that [state] did not cease in him until Allah gave power over him just now.
items.ma-3709: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ lay down on a mat, and it left a mark on his side. When he woke, I began to wipe his side, and said: O Messenger of Allah, would you not have informed us, so that we could spread something over the mat for you? The Messenger of Allah ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam said: “What have I to do with the world? What am I and the world? My likeness and the likeness of the world is only like a rider who took shade beneath a tree, then went on in the evening and left it.”
items.ma-3710: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī informed us, from Jāmiʿ ibn Shaddād, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAlqamah al-Thaqafī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: When we returned from the expedition of al-Ḥudaybiyah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Who will guard us tonight?” ʿAbd Allāh said: I said: I. He said: “You will sleep.” Then he repeated: “Who will guard us tonight?” I said: I; until he had repeated it several times; I said: I, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “Then you.” He said: So I guarded them, until when it was the face of the morning, the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ overtook me: “You will sleep,” and I slept, and nothing woke us except the heat of the sun on our backs. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, and did as he used to do, of the wuḍūʾ and the two rakʿahs of Fajr, then prayed the Ṣubḥ with us. When he finished, he said: “Indeed Allah ﷿, had He willed that you not sleep through it, you would not have slept; but He willed that you be [a precedent] for those after you; so thus [it is] for whoever sleeps or forgets.” He said: Then the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the camels of the people scattered, and the people went out in search of them, and they came with their camels, except the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ʿAbd Allāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “Take [the way] here.” So I took the way he told me, and found her rein twisted around a tree, which nothing but a hand could have untied. He said: I came with her to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, by the One who sent you with the truth as a prophet, I found her rein twisted around a tree, which nothing but a hand could have untied. He said: And Sūrat al-Fatḥ was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: {Indeed, We have given you a clear conquest}.
items.ma-3711: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥārith al-Jābir, from Abū Mājid, he said: A man brought to Ibn Masʿūd a son of his brother; and he said: This is my brother's son, and he has drunk. ʿAbd Allāh said: I know the first ḥadd that was in Islam: a woman stole, and her hand was cut off, and the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed greatly for that; then he said: {And let them pardon and overlook. Would you not love that Allah forgive you? And Allah is al-Ghafūr, al-Raḥīm} [al-Nūr: 22].
items.ma-3712: Yazīd narrated to us, Fuḍayl ibn Marzūq informed us, Abū Salamah al-Juhanī narrated to us, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “No one is ever afflicted with worry or grief and says: O Allah, I am Your servant, the son of Your servant, the son of Your maidservant; my forelock is in Your Yad; Your judgment is carried out upon me; Your decree concerning me is just. I ask You by every Name that is Yours, by which You named Yourself, or taught to any of Your creation, or sent down in Your Book, or kept exclusively to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen with You, that You make the Qurʾān the spring of my heart, the light of my chest, the clearing away of my grief, and the departure of my worry — except that Allah removes his worry and his grief, and replaces it with joy.” He said: It was said: O Messenger of Allah, shall we not learn it? He said: “Yes; it is fitting for whoever hears it to learn it.”
items.ma-3713: Yazīd narrated to us, Sharīk ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed us, from ʿAlī ibn Badhīmah, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When Banū Isrāʾīl fell into disobedience, their scholars forbade them, but they did not desist; so they sat with them in their gatherings — Yazīd said: I think he said: and their markets — and ate with them and drank with them, so Allah struck the hearts of some of them against others, and cursed them upon the tongue of Dāwūd and ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, that being because they disobeyed and used to transgress.” And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been reclining, so he sat up, and said: “No, by the One in whose Yad is my soul, until you bend them back to the truth firmly.”
items.ma-3714: Yazīd narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah informed us, from Thābit al-Bunānī, from Anas ibn Mālik, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The last to enter Paradise is a man who walks on the Ṣirāṭ; he stumbles once, and walks once, and the Fire scorches him once. When he has crossed the Ṣirāṭ, he turns to it and says: Tabāraka the One who saved me from you; Allah has given me what He has not given to anyone of the first and the last. He said: Then a tree is raised for him, and he looks at it, and says: O Rabb, bring me near this tree, so that I may take shade in its shade and drink from its water. He says: O My servant, perhaps if I bring you near it you will ask Me for something other than it. He says: No, O Rabb. And he makes a covenant with Allah that he will not ask Him for anything other than it; and the Rabb ﷿ knows that he will ask Him, because he sees what he has no patience against — meaning against it. So He brings him near it. Then a tree is raised for him, and it is more beautiful than it, and he says: O Rabb, bring me near this tree, so that I may take shade in its shade and drink from its water. He says: O My servant, did you not make a covenant with Me — meaning that you would not ask Me for anything other than it! He says: O Rabb, this one; I will not ask You for anything other than it. And he makes a covenant with Him; and the Rabb knows that he will ask Him for something other than it. So He brings him near it. Then a tree is raised for him at the gate of Paradise, more beautiful than it, and he says: Rabb, bring me near this tree; I will take shade in its shade and drink from its water. He says: O My servant, did you not make a covenant with Me that you would not ask Me for anything other than it?! He says: O Rabb, this tree; I will not ask You for anything other than it. And he makes a covenant with Him; and the Rabb knows that he will ask Him for something other than it, because he sees what he has no patience against. So He brings him near it, and he hears the voices of the people of Paradise, and says: O Rabb, Paradise, Paradise! He says: O My servant, did you not make a covenant with Me that you would not ask Me for anything other than it?! He says: O Rabb, admit me into Paradise. He said: Then He ﷿ says: What will cut Me off from you, O My servant? Would it please you that I give you of Paradise the world and its like with it? He said: He says: Are You mocking me, O my Rabb, when You are Rabb al-ʿIzzah?” He said: ʿAbd Allāh laughed until his molars showed, and then said: Will you not ask me why I laughed? They said to him: Why did you laugh? He said: Because of the laughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: “Will you not ask me why I laughed?” They said: Why did you laugh, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “Because of the Ḍaḥik of the Rabb, when he said: Are You mocking me, when You are Rabb al-ʿIzzah?!”
items.ma-3715: Yazīd narrated to us, Shuʿbah ibn al-Ḥajjāj informed me, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from Abū Saʿd, from Abū Kanūd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us from the gold ring, or the gold band.
items.ma-3716: Yazīd narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah informed us, from Zubayd, from Murrah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “They kept us from the middle prayer until the sun set; may Allah fill their bellies and their graves with fire.”
items.ma-3717: Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Abū ʿUthmān, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Let not the adhān of Bilāl prevent any of you from his suḥūr, for he only calls out (or he said: gives the adhān) so that your one who stands may return and your sleeper may be awakened. It is not that he says thus, but [it is] until he says thus.” And Ibn Abī ʿAdī Abū ʿAmr joined his fingers, and lowered them, and opened what was between his two index fingers, meaning the dawn.
items.ma-3718:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “A person is with the one he loves.”
[Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Some people asked the Prophet ﷺ about a companion of theirs who cauterises himself. He said: So he was silent, then said on the third time: “Apply hot stones to him; burn him.” He said: And he disliked that.]
items.ma-3719: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Prophet ﷺ was among those who often said: Glory be to You, our Rabb, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me. He said: So when {When the victory of Allah and the conquest come} was revealed, he said: “Glory be to You, our Rabb, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me. Indeed You are al-Tawwāb al-Raḥīm.”
items.ma-3720: Muḥammad narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū Isḥāq narrating, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: He taught us the khuṭbah of need: Praise be to Allah; we seek His help and we seek His forgiveness, and we seek refuge with Allah from the evils of ourselves. Whomever Allah guides, there is none to lead him astray, and whomever He leads astray, there is none to guide him. And I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. Then he would recite three verses: {O you who have believed, fear Allah with the fear due to Him, and do not die except as Muslims} [Āl ʿImrān: 102], {O mankind, fear your Rabb, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed Allah is ever over you an observer} [al-Nisāʾ: 1], {O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak a sound word. He will amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment} [al-Aḥzāb: 70 - 71]. Then you mention your need.
items.ma-3721: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq informed us, from Abū ʿUbaydah and Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, he said: And this is the ḥadīth of Abū ʿUbaydah, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught us two khuṭbahs: the khuṭbah of need and the khuṭbah of prayer: Praise be to Allah, or: Indeed, praise belongs to Allah; we seek His help … So he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-3722: Muḥammad narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was prostrating, with some people of Quraysh around him, ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ came with the afterbirth of a slaughtered camel and threw it onto the back of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he did not raise his head. Then Fāṭimah came and took it from his back, and she invoked against the one who had done that. He said: So he said: “O Allah, upon You [is] the assembly of Quraysh: Abū Jahl ibn Hishām, ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabīʿah, ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ, and Umayyah ibn Khalaf” - or “Ubayy ibn Khalaf”, Shuʿbah being the one in doubt -. He said: I indeed saw them killed on the day of Badr, and they were thrown into a well, except that Umayyah or Ubayy, his limbs were severed, so he was not thrown into the well.
items.ma-3723: Khalaf narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us … So he mentioned the ḥadīth, except that he said: ʿAmr ibn Hishām and Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and he added: and ʿUmārah ibn al-Walīd.
items.ma-3724: Muḥammad, who is Ibn Jaʿfar, narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from al-Nazzāl ibn Sabrah, from ʿAbd Allāh, that he said: I heard a man reciting a verse, and I had heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [a reading] other than it, so I brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed, or I recognised dislike in the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Each of you two is doing well. Those before you differed over it, so it destroyed them.” Shuʿbah said: And Misʿar narrated to me from him, and he raised it to ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ: “So do not differ.”
items.ma-3725: Muḥammad narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, he said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrating, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that he said: Two transactions in one transaction are not valid, and indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “May Allah curse the one who consumes ribā, the one who feeds it, its witness and its writer.”
items.ma-3726: Muḥammad narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Simāk, he said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrating, from his father - Shuʿbah said: And I think he had raised it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ - he said: “The likeness of the one who helps his kinsfolk in other than the truth is the likeness of a camel that has fallen into a well, so it pulls with its tail.”
items.ma-3727: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ; that he said: “A man continues to speak the truth and to seek out the truth, until he is written as a ṣiddīq; and he continues to lie and to seek out lying, until he is written as a great liar.”
items.ma-3728: Muḥammad narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, from Hunayy ibn Nuwayrah, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ; that he said: “The most restrained of people in the manner of killing are the people of īmān.”
items.ma-3729: Surayj ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, Mughīrah informed us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed the most restrained of people in the manner of killing are the people of īmān.”
items.ma-3730: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Ribʿī, from al-Barāʾ ibn Nājiyah, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The millstone of Islam will turn at thirty-five, or thirty-six, or thirty-seven. If they perish, [it is] the way of one who has perished; and if their religion stands for them, it will stand for them seventy years.” He said: I said: Is it from what has passed or from what remains? He said: “From what remains.”
items.ma-3731: Isḥāq narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ribʿī ibn Ḥirāsh, from al-Barāʾ ibn Nājiyah al-Kāhilī, from Ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ … the like of it, except that he said: So ʿUmar said to him: O Messenger of Allah, [is it] what has passed, or what remains? He said: “What remains.”
items.ma-3732: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from al-Ḥasan, meaning Ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibrāhīm ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have permitted you to lift the curtain and to listen to my sawād, until I forbid you.”
items.ma-3733: Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn ʿIyāḍ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The most beloved of the ʿirāq to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the foreleg, the foreleg of the sheep, and he had been poisoned in the foreleg, and he used to consider that the Jews were the ones who had poisoned him.
items.ma-3734: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Yaḥyā al-Jābir Abū al-Ḥārith al-Taymī narrated to us, that Abū Mājid, a man from Banū Ḥanīfah, narrated to him, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: We asked our Prophet ﷺ about walking with the funeral procession? He said: “Walking is [at a pace] below the khabab. If it is good, it is hastened to - or he said: it is hurried on to - and if it is other than that, then away with the people of the Fire. The funeral procession is followed, and does not follow; one who goes ahead of it is not of it.”
items.ma-3735: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrating, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The Hour will not be established except upon the worst of people.”
items.ma-3736: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from al-Aswad and ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ say the takbīr at every raising and lowering, and standing and sitting, and he would give the salām to his right and to his left: “Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah,” until I would see the whiteness of his cheek; and I saw Abū Bakr and ʿUmar doing that.
items.ma-3737: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Simāk, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who consumes ribā, the one who feeds it, its two witnesses and its writer.
items.ma-3738: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Jāmiʿ ibn Abī Rāshid, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach us the tashahhud as he used to teach us a sūrah of the Qurʾān.
items.ma-3739: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, from Sharīk, from Thuwayr ibn Abī Fākhitah, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the talbiyah until he threw [pebbles at] Jamrat al-ʿAqabah.
items.ma-3740: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh, regarding [Allah's] saying: {The heart did not lie [about] what it saw}, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw Jibrīl in a ḥullah of rafraf, having filled what is between the heaven and the earth.
items.ma-3741: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made me recite: Indeed I, I am al-Razzāq, Dhū al-Quwwah al-Matīn.
items.ma-3742: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Prophet ﷺ, when he placed his side on his bed, would say: “Protect me from Your punishment on the day You gather Your servants.”
items.ma-3743: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I had indeed intended to command a man to lead the people in prayer, then to command some people who do not pray with us, so that their houses would be burned down upon them.”
items.ma-3744: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, and Abū Aḥmad: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said - Abū Aḥmad said: from Ibn Masʿūd, he said -: It used to please the Prophet ﷺ to supplicate three times and to seek forgiveness three times.
items.ma-3745: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Since {When the victory of Allah and the conquest come} was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he used to say often, when he recited it and then bowed with it, to say: “Glory be to You, our Rabb, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me. Indeed You are al-Tawwāb al-Raḥīm,” three times.
items.ma-3746: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd and Yūnus narrated to us, they said: Dāwūd - meaning Ibn Abī al-Furāt - narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Zayd, from Abū al-Aʿyan al-ʿAbdī, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ al-Jushamī, he said: While Ibn Masʿūd was delivering a khuṭbah one day, there was a snake walking on the wall, so he cut off his khuṭbah, then struck it with his rod, or with a reed - Yūnus said: with his rod - until he killed it. Then he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever kills a snake, it is as if he had killed a polytheist man whose blood has become lawful.”
items.ma-3747: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd and Yūnus narrated to us, they said: Dāwūd narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Zayd, from Abū al-Aʿyan al-ʿAbdī, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ al-Jushamī, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: We asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the monkeys and the swine, are they from the offspring of the Jews? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah has never cursed a people and then transformed them, so that they had offspring when He destroyed them; but this is a creation that already existed. So when Ghaḍiba Allāh ʿalā the Jews, He transformed them and made them like them.”
items.ma-3748: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw Jibrīl in his form, and he had six hundred wings, each wing of which had blocked the horizon; there fell from his wing variegated things, pearls and rubies, of which Allah is ʿAlīm.
items.ma-3749: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, regarding His saying: {And Allah took Ibrāhīm as a khalīl} [al-Nisāʾ: 125], he said: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr informed me, from Khālid ibn Ribʿī, from Ibn Masʿūd, that he said: Indeed Allah took your companion as a khalīl, meaning Muḥammad ﷺ.
items.ma-3750: Abū al-Walīd narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from Khālid ibn Ribʿī al-Asadī, he said: I heard Ibn Masʿūd say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed your companion is the khalīl of Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-3751: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr narrated to us, from Khālid ibn Ribʿī al-Asadī, that he heard Ibn Masʿūd say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed your companion is the khalīl of Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-3752: Muʿāwiyah ibn Hishām narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Khālid ibn Ribʿī, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed your companion is the khalīl of Allah.”
items.ma-3753: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from Khālid ibn Ribʿī, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: Indeed your companion is the khalīl of Allah ﷿.
items.ma-3754: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabīʿ, from his father, from Ibn Masʿūd; that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Ribā, even if it increases, its outcome comes to be [a matter of] paucity.”
items.ma-3755: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Aswad, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made me recite: {And We have certainly made the Qurʾān easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?} A man said: O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: (muddakir) or (mudhdhakir)? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made me recite: (muddakir).
items.ma-3756: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabīʿ, from al-Qāsim ibn Ḥassān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Horses are of three [kinds]: a horse for al-Raḥmān, a horse for the human being, and a horse for Shayṭān. As for the horse of al-Raḥmān: it is the one that is tied in the way of Allah, so its fodder, its dung and its urine - and he mentioned what Allah willed. And as for the horse of Shayṭān: it is the one that is gambled or wagered upon. And as for the horse of the human being: it is the horse that the human being ties up, seeking its offspring, and it covers [him] against poverty.”
items.ma-3757: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, al-Rukayn narrated to us, from Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī, from a man of the Anṣār, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Horses are of three [kinds] …” So he mentioned the ḥadīth.
items.ma-3758: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, Manṣūr narrated to us, from Ribʿī, from al-Barāʾ ibn Nājiyah al-Kāhilī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed the millstone of Islam will shift at thirty-five, or thirty-six, or thirty-seven. If it perishes, then [it is] like the way of what has perished; and if their religion stands for them, it will stand for them seventy years.” He said: ʿUmar said: O Messenger of Allah, [is it] by what has passed or by what remains? He said: “Rather, by what remains.”
items.ma-3759: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, he said: I heard Isrāʾīl ibn Yūnus, from al-Walīd ibn Abī Hishām, a mawlā of Hamdān, from Zayd ibn Abī Zāʾidah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions: “Let none convey to me anything about any of my Companions, for I love to come out to you while I am sound of heart.” He said: And some wealth came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he distributed it. He said: So I passed by two men, and one of them was saying to his companion: By Allah, Muḥammad did not intend by his distribution Wajh Allāh, nor the Home of the Hereafter. So I held firm until I heard what they both said. Then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, you said to us: “Let none convey to me anything about any of my Companions,” and I passed by so-and-so and so-and-so, and they were saying such and such. He said: So the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned red, and it was hard upon him. Then he said: “Leave us [alone] from you; Mūsā was harmed more than that, and he was patient.”
items.ma-3760: Abū al-Naḍr and Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, they said: Shaybān narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer, then went out to the mosque, and behold, the people were waiting for the prayer. He said: “Indeed, there is none among the people of these religions who remembers Allah at this hour except you.” He said: And He sent down these verses: {They are not alike among the People of the Book} until he reached: {And whatever good you do, you will never be denied it; and Allah is ʿAlīm of the God-fearing} [Āl ʿImrān: 113 - 115].
items.ma-3761: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: Ibn al-Nawwāḥah and Ibn Uthāl, the two messengers of Musaylimah, came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said to them: “Do you both bear witness that I am the Messenger of Allah?” They said: We bear witness that Musaylimah is the Messenger of Allah!! The Prophet ﷺ said: “I believe in Allah and His messengers. Were I to kill a messenger, I would have killed you both.” ʿAbd Allāh said: He said: So the sunnah went forth that messengers are not killed.
items.ma-3762: Muʿāwiyah ibn Hishām narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We used to see the signs in the time of the Prophet ﷺ as blessings, and you see them as a cause of fear.
items.ma-3763: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh, that he said: The Prophet ﷺ stopped at a halting place and went off for his need, then he came [back], and a man had lit a fire upon a village of ants, either on the ground or in a tree. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Which of you did this?” A man from the people said: I [did], O Messenger of Allah. He said: “Extinguish it, extinguish it.”
items.ma-3764: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAmr ibn Jaʿdah, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, that a man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him about Laylat al-Qadr. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Which of you remembers the night of the Ṣahbāwāt?” ʿAbd Allāh said: I, by Allah, remember it, O Messenger of Allah, may my father and my mother be a ransom for you; and in my hands were some dates with which I was eating the suḥūr, shielding myself from the dawn with the rear part of my saddle, and that was when the moon rose.
items.ma-3765: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken, the Anṣār said: From us a commander and from you a commander. He said: So ʿUmar came to them and said: O assembly of the Anṣār, do you not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Abū Bakr to lead the people [in prayer]? So which of you is pleased in his soul to go ahead of Abū Bakr? They said: We seek refuge with Allah from going ahead of Abū Bakr.
items.ma-3766: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from Sulaymān, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he prolonged the standing until I intended an evil matter. He said: We said: And what was it? He said: I intended to sit.
items.ma-3767: Abū Saʿīd, a mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥubulī, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, which wrongdoing is greatest? He said: “A cubit of land that he takes away from the right of his brother, for there is no pebble of the earth that he takes except that he will be encircled with it on the Day of Resurrection down to the bottom of the earth, and none knows its bottom except the One who created it.”
items.ma-3768: Abū Saʿīd, who is a mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, Dāwūd ibn Abī al-Furāt narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Abū al-Aʿyan al-ʿAbdī, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ al-Jushamī, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: We asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the monkeys and the swine, are they from the offspring of the Jews? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah has never cursed a people and then transformed them, while they had offspring until He destroyed them; but Allah ﷿ Ghaḍiba ʿalā the Jews, so He transformed them and made them like them.”
items.ma-3769: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: It used to please the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to supplicate three times and to seek forgiveness three times.
items.ma-3771: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made me recite: Indeed I, I am al-Razzāq, Dhū al-Quwwah al-Matīn.
items.ma-3772: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from Khālid ibn Yazīd, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUbayd ibn Rifāʿah, that Abū Muḥammad informed him - and he was one of the companions of Ibn Masʿūd - [that] he narrated to him from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that the shuhadāʾ were mentioned in his presence, and he said: “Indeed most of the shuhadāʾ of my ummah are the people of the beds, and many a one slain between the two ranks, Allah knows best his intention.”
items.ma-3773: Ḥasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥubulī, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, which wrongdoing is most wrongful? He said: “A cubit of land that the Muslim man takes away from the right of his brother, for there is no pebble of the earth that anyone takes except that he will be encircled with it on the Day of Resurrection down to the bottom of the earth, and none knows its bottom except Allah ﷿, who created it.”
items.ma-3774: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, al-Rukayn narrated to us, from al-Qāsim ibn Ḥassān, from his paternal uncle ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥarmalah, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to dislike ten qualities: yellowness, changing grey hair, wearing a ring of gold, dragging the izār, displaying adornment in other than its place, casting the dice, removing the water from its place, spoiling a child, not forbidding it, tying amulets, and the ruqyahs except with the Muʿawwidhāt.
items.ma-3775: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ faced the House and invoked against seven men of Quraysh, among them Abū Jahl, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabīʿah, and ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ. So I swear by Allah: I indeed saw them lying slain at Badr, and the sun had changed them, and it was a hot day.
items.ma-3776: Abū al-Mundhir narrated to us, ʿĪsā ibn Dīnār al-Khuzāʿī narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, that he heard ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith al-Khuzāʿī say: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd say: I did not fast twenty-nine [days] with the Messenger of Allah صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ more than I fasted thirty with him.
items.ma-3777: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿd or Saʿīd ibn ʿIyāḍ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The most beloved of the ʿirāq to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the foreleg of the sheep, and he used to consider that he had been poisoned in the foreleg of the sheep, and we used to consider that it was the Jews who had poisoned him.
items.ma-3778: Aswad narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿd ibn ʿIyāḍ, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: Indeed, part of eloquence is sorcery. He said: And we used to consider that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been poisoned in the foreleg of a sheep, the Jews having poisoned him.
items.ma-3779: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sufyān ibn Saʿīd al-Thawrī narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from his father, from Ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “There is none of you except that his companion from the angels and from the jinn is with him.” They said: And you also, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “And I, except that Allah helped me against him, so he submitted, and he commands me only to good.”
items.ma-3780: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq al-Shaybānī narrated to us, he said: I came to Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, and I had on me two darbān, and a love from him was cast upon me; and with him were some youths, and they said to me: Ask him about {and he was at a distance of two bows or nearer} [al-Najm: 9]? So he asked him, and he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd narrated to us: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw Jibrīl ﵇ and he had six hundred wings.
items.ma-3781: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbī, from Masrūq, he said: We were sitting with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd while he was making us recite the Qurʾān, and a man said to him: O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, did you ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ how many caliphs this ummah will have as rulers? ʿAbd Allāh said: No one has asked me about it since I came to Iraq before you. Then he said: Yes, we did ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “Twelve, like the number of the chiefs of Banū Isrāʾīl.”
items.ma-3782: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from Qays ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Ḥanash al-Ṣanʿānī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that he was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Night of the Jinn, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: “O ʿAbd Allāh, do you have water with you?” He said: I have nabīdh in a small waterskin. He said: “Pour it over me,” and he performed wuḍūʾ. He said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “O ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, a drink and a purifier.”
items.ma-3783: Ḥasan, Abū al-Naḍr and Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, they said: Sharīk narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade two transactions in one single transaction. Aswad said: Sharīk said: Simāk said: A man sells a sale and says: It is with deferral for such and such, and it is in cash for such and such.
items.ma-3784: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us - [ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad said:] and I myself heard it from Ibn Abī Shaybah -, Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Islam began as a stranger, and it will return as it began, so ṭūbā for the strangers.” It was said: And who are the strangers? He said: “Those who are drawn away from the tribes.”
items.ma-3785: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah informed us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, that a man had never done any good at all except tawḥīd, and when death came to him, he said to his family: When I die, take me and burn me until you leave me as charcoal, then grind me, then scatter me in the sea on a windy day. He said: So they did that to him. He said: And behold, he was in Qabḍat Allāh. He said: Allah ﷿ said to him: What made you do what you did? He said: Fear of You. He said: So Allah forgave him.
items.ma-3786: Yaḥyā said: And Ḥammād narrated it to us, from Thābit, from Abū Rāfiʿ, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ … the like of it.
items.ma-3787: ʿĀrim ibn al-Faḍl narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Zayd narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam al-Bunānī narrated to us, from ʿUthmān, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah and al-Aswad, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The two sons of Mulaykah came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Indeed our mother used to honour the husband and show kindness to the child - he said: and he mentioned the guest - except that she had buried a girl alive in the Jāhiliyyah. He said: “Your mother is in the Fire.” So they turned away, and evil could be seen in their faces. Then he commanded about them, and they were brought back, and they returned with joy seen in their faces, hoping that something had occurred. Then he said: “My mother is with your mother.” A man from the hypocrites said: And what will this one avail his mother at all, while we tread upon his heels? Then a man from the Anṣār - and I never saw a man who asked more questions than he - said: O Messenger of Allah, did your Rabb promise you concerning her, or concerning them both? He said: So he thought that it was from something he had heard, and he said: “I did not ask my Rabb, and He did not make me hope for it; and I will indeed stand the praised station on the Day of Resurrection.” The Anṣārī said: And what is that praised station? He said: “That is when you are brought naked, barefoot, and uncircumcised, and the first to be clothed will be Ibrāhīm; he says: Clothe my khalīl. So two white rayṭahs are brought, and let him wear them, then he sits and faces the ʿArsh. Then my clothing is brought to me, and I wear it, and I stand at his right, at a station that none stands in other than me, for which the first and the last envy me.” He said: “And a river will be opened from al-Kawthar to the Ḥawḍ.” The hypocrites said: Water has never flowed except over mud or pebbles. He said: O Messenger of Allah, over mud or pebbles? He said: “Its mud is musk, and its pebbles are pearls.” The hypocrite said: I have not heard the like of today; seldom does water ever flow over mud or pebbles except that it has vegetation. The Anṣārī said: O Messenger of Allah, does it have vegetation? He said: “Yes, rods of gold.” The hypocrite said: I have not heard the like of today; seldom does a rod grow except that it puts forth leaves, or it has fruit. The Anṣārī said: O Messenger of Allah, is there any fruit? He said: “Yes, colours of jewels, and its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey; whoever drinks a drink from it will not be thirsty after it, and whoever is deprived of it will not be quenched after it.”
items.ma-3788: ʿĀrim and ʿAffān narrated to us, they said: Muʿtamir narrated to us, he said: My father said: Abū Tamīmah narrated to me, from ʿAmr - perhaps he said: al-Bikālī - ʿAmr narrating it from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd. ʿAmr said: Indeed ʿAbd Allāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked me to follow him. He said: So we set out until I came to such-and-such a place, and he drew a line for me and said to me: “Be within this; do not go out of it, for if you go out you will perish.” He said: So I was in it. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on, a throw or a little further, or as he said. Then he mentioned hanīn, as if they were the Zuṭṭ. (ʿAffān said: Or as ʿAffān said: if Allah wills): No clothes were upon them, and I did not see their private parts; [they were] tall, with little flesh. He said: So they came and began to ride the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: And the Prophet of Allah ﷺ began to recite to them. He said: And they began to come to me and circle around me, and to come across to me. ʿAbd Allāh said: So I was filled with terror of them, a severe terror. He said: So I sat, or as he said. He said: When the pillar of dawn split, they began to go away, or as he said. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, heavy and in pain, or nearly in pain, from their having ridden him. He said: “Indeed I find myself heavy,” or as he said. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed his head in my lap, or as he said. He said: Then hanīn came, upon them tall white garments, or as he said, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had dozed off. ʿAbd Allāh said: So I was terrified more than I was terrified the first time. (ʿĀrim said in his ḥadīth): He said: So some of them said to others: This servant has indeed been given good, or as they said: his two eyes are asleep - or he said: his eye - or as they said: and his heart is awake. Then he said: (ʿĀrim and ʿAffān said): Some of them said to others: Come, let us strike a parable for him, or as they said. Some of them said to others: Strike a parable for him and we will interpret, or we strike and you interpret. So some of them said to others: His likeness is like that of a master who built a fortified building, then sent food to the people, or as he said. So whoever did not come to his food - or he said: did not follow him - he punished with a severe punishment. Or as they said. The others said: As for the master: he is the Rabb of the worlds; and as for the building: it is Islam; and the food: Paradise; and he is the caller, so whoever follows him will be in Paradise. (ʿĀrim said in his ḥadīth): Or as they said, and whoever does not follow him is punished. Or as he said. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke up and said: “What did you see, O Ibn Umm ʿAbd?” ʿAbd Allāh said: I saw such and such. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Nothing of what they said was hidden from me.” The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: “They are a group of the angels, or he said: They are from the angels, or as Allah willed.”
items.ma-3789: ʿĀrim narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muslim al-Qasmalī narrated to us, Sulaymān al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Yaḥyā ibn Jaʿdah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He will not enter the Fire who has in his heart the weight of a grain of īmān, and he will not enter Paradise who has in his heart the weight of a grain of arrogance.” A man said: O Messenger of Allah, I am pleased that my garment be washed, my head be oiled, and the strap of my sandal be new - and he mentioned things, until he mentioned the strap of his whip - is that from arrogance, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “No, that is beauty. Indeed Allah is Jamīl, Yuḥibbu al-Jamāl; but arrogance is [for] one who disdains the truth and holds people in contempt.”
items.ma-3790:
Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Zakariyyā narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, after me there will take charge of your affair men who extinguish the sunnah, bring about an innovation, and delay the prayer from its times.” Ibn Masʿūd said: O Messenger of Allah, how [will it be] with me if I reach them? He said: “There is no obedience, O Ibn Umm ʿAbd, to one who disobeys Allah.” He said it three times.
[ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad said:] And I myself heard from Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ the like of it.
items.ma-3791: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Hāshimī narrated to us, Ismāʿīl informed us, ʿAmr, meaning Ibn Abī ʿAmr, informed me, from ʿUbayd Allāh and Ḥamzah, the two sons of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that the Prophet ﷺ used to eat meat, then stand for the prayer without touching water.
items.ma-3792: Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from ʿAmr, meaning Ibn Abī ʿAmr, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eat meat, then stand for the prayer, and he did not touch a drop of water.
items.ma-3793: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn Bilāl narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr, from Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eat meat, then stand for the prayer, and not touch water.
items.ma-3794: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Saʿd set out to perform ʿumrah, and stayed with Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and Umayyah, whenever he set out for al-Shām and passed by al-Madīnah, would stay with Saʿd. Umayyah said to Saʿd: Wait, until when midday comes and the people are heedless, go and perform ṭawāf. While Saʿd was performing ṭawāf, Abū Jahl came to him and said: Who is this performing ṭawāf of the Kaʿbah in safety? Saʿd said: I am Saʿd. Abū Jahl said: You perform ṭawāf of the Kaʿbah in safety, while you have given shelter to Muḥammad? They exchanged harsh words, and Umayyah said to Saʿd: Do not raise your voice against Abū al-Ḥakam, for he is the master of the people of the valley. Saʿd said to him: By Allah, if you prevent me from performing ṭawāf of the House, I will cut off your trade route to al-Shām. Umayyah kept saying: Do not raise your voice against Abū al-Ḥakam, and kept restraining him. Saʿd became angry and said: Leave us from you, for I heard Muḥammad claim that he is your killer. He said: Me? He said: Yes. He said: By Allah, Muḥammad does not lie. When they went out, he returned to his wife and said: Do you not know what the Yathribī said to me? And he told her of it. When the cry came and they went out to Badr, his wife said: Do you not remember what your brother the Yathribī said? So he wanted not to go out, and Abū Jahl said to him: You are among the nobles of the valley, so travel with us a day or two. So he travelled with them, and Allah ﷿ killed him.
items.ma-3795: Khalaf ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Saʿd ibn Muʿādh set out to perform ʿumrah, and stayed with Umayyah ibn Khalaf ibn Ṣafwān, and Umayyah, whenever he set out for al-Shām and passed by al-Madīnah, would stay with Saʿd … So he mentioned the ḥadīth, except that he said: So he returned to Umm Ṣafwān and said: Do you not know what my brother the Yathribī said? She said: And what did he say? He said: He claimed that he heard Muḥammad claim that he is my killer. She said: By Allah, Muḥammad does not lie. And when they went out to Badr … and he related it on.
items.ma-3796: Ḥujayn ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that when he slept, he would place his right hand under his cheek and say: “O Allah, protect me from Your punishment on the day You gather Your servants.”
items.ma-3797: Ḥujayn ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, that he was in the mosque supplicating, and the Prophet ﷺ entered while he was supplicating, and said: “Ask, you will be given,” and he was saying: O Allah, I ask You for īmān that does not turn back, and bliss that does not run out, and the companionship of the Prophet ﷺ Muḥammad in the highest chambers of Paradise, the Paradise of eternity.
items.ma-3798: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Ḥaṣīn, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever sees me in the dream has indeed seen me in wakefulness, for Shayṭān does not take on a likeness in my form.”
items.ma-3799: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ … the like of it.
items.ma-3800: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from his father, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, every prophet has allies among the prophets, and indeed my ally among them is my father and the khalīl of my Rabb, Ibrāhīm.” He said: Then he recited: {Indeed, the most worthy of people of Ibrāhīm} to the end of the verse [Āl ʿImrān: 68].
items.ma-3801: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr and Muʾammal narrated to us, they said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was in a red tent (ʿAbd al-Malik said: of leather) with about forty men, and he said: “Indeed, you will have [conquests] opened for you, you will be given victory, and you will gain; so whoever of you reaches that, let him fear Allah, enjoin the maʿrūf and forbid the munkar, and maintain his ties of kinship. Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in the Fire. And the likeness of the one who helps his people in other than the truth is like a camel that has fallen into a well, so it pulls [itself] out of it with its tail.”
items.ma-3802: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from his father, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is none of you except that his companion from the jinn and his companion from the angels has been assigned to him.” They said: And you, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “And me; but Allah helped me against him, so he submitted, and he commands me only to good.”
items.ma-3803: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Hammām, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I heard a man reciting Ḥā Mīm of the thirty - meaning (al-Aḥqāf) - and he recited a ḥarf, and another man recited a ḥarf that his companion had not recited, and I recited ḥarfs that my two companions had not recited. So we went to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and he said: “Do not differ, for those before you perished only through their differing.” Then he said: “Look for the man among you who is the best reciter, and take his recitation.”
items.ma-3804: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from Abū Saʿd, from Abū al-Kanūd, he said: I obtained a ring of gold on one of the military expeditions, and I wore it. Then I came to ʿAbd Allāh, and he took it, put it between his jaws and chewed it, and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade wearing a ring of gold - or he said: a circlet of gold.
items.ma-3805: Yazīd narrated to us, Shuʿbah informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated in al-Najm, and none of the people remained except that he prostrated, except an old man who took a handful of pebbles and raised it to his forehead and said: This is enough for me. ʿAbd Allāh said: I indeed saw him killed as a kāfir.
items.ma-3806: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: We talked much in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one night, then we went to him in the morning, and he said: “The prophets were presented to me last night with their nations, and a prophet would pass with three [people] with him, and a prophet with a company with him, and a prophet with a few men with him, and a prophet with no one with him, until Mūsā passed by me with a throng of Banū Isrāʾīl, and they pleased me, and I said: Who are these? It was said to me: This is your brother Mūsā, with Banū Isrāʾīl with him.” He said: “I said: And where is my ummah? It was said to me: Look to your right. So I looked, and behold, the hillocks were blocked with the faces of men. Then it was said to me: Look to your left. So I looked, and behold, the horizon was blocked with the faces of men. It was said to me: Are you pleased? I said: I am pleased, O Rabb, I am pleased, O Rabb. He said: It was said to me: Indeed with these are seventy thousand who enter Paradise without reckoning.” Then the Prophet ﷺ said: “My father and my mother be a ransom for you. If you are able to be among the seventy thousand, then do so; and if you fall short, then be among the people of the hillocks; and if you fall short, then be among the people of the horizon, for I saw people there mingling in confusion.” Then ʿUkkāshah ibn Miḥṣan stood and said: Supplicate to Allah for me, O Messenger of Allah, that He make me one of the seventy. So he supplicated for him. Then another man stood and said: Supplicate to Allah, O Messenger of Allah, that He make me one of them. He said: “ʿUkkāshah has preceded you with it.” He said: Then we talked, and we said: Who do you think these seventy thousand are? A people who were born in Islam and did not associate anything with Allah until they died? That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “They are those who do not cauterise, do not seek ruqyah, and do not take bad omens, and upon their Rabb they rely.”
items.ma-3807: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and they did not find water, so a basin of water was brought, and the Prophet ﷺ put his hand in it and spread apart his fingers. He said: So I saw the water gushing forth from between the fingers of the Prophet ﷺ, [then he said]: “Come to the wuḍūʾ, and the blessing is from Allah.” al-Aʿmash said: And Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd informed me, he said: I said to Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh: How many were the people that day? He said: We were one thousand five hundred.
items.ma-3808: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: A man said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: How [can it be] for me to know when I have done well and when I have done wrong? The Prophet ﷺ said: “If you hear your neighbours say: You have done well, then you have done well; and if you hear them say: You have done wrong, then you have done wrong.”
items.ma-3809: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from Simāk, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “May Allah curse the one who consumes ribā, the one who feeds it, its two witnesses and its writer.” He said: And he said: “Ribā and zinā do not appear among a people except that they bring down upon themselves the punishment of Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-3810: Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Fazārah, from Abū Zayd, a mawlā of ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on the night he met the jinn, and he said: “Do you have water with you?” I said: No. He said: “What is this in the waterskin?” I said: Nabīdh. He said: “Show it to me: a good date and purifying water.” So he performed wuḍūʾ with it, then prayed with us.
items.ma-3811: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Abū Bakr informed us, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Wāʾil, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever sets up a rival to Allah, Allah will place him in the Fire,” and he said: And another [matter] I say, which I did not hear from him: Whoever dies not setting up a rival to Allah, Allah will admit him to Paradise. And these prayers are kaffārāt for what is between them, so long as the killing is avoided.
items.ma-3812: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Abū Bakr informed us, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed I am your forerunner at the Ḥawḍ, and indeed I will be contended with over men, and I will be overcome regarding them, and I will say: O Rabb, my Companions! And it will be said: You do not know what they innovated after you.”
items.ma-3813: Rawḥ narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Salām, from Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast on the journey and to break the fast, and to pray two rakʿahs, not leaving them; he says: not adding to them, meaning the obligatory [prayer].
items.ma-3814: Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us, my father narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿĀṣim narrating, from Zirr, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
items.ma-3815: Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us, my father narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr narrating, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not return after me as kuffār, some of you striking the necks of others.”
