items.ma-3816: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Prophet ﷺ said to a people who stay behind from the Jumuʿah: “I had indeed intended to command a man to lead the people in prayer, then to burn down, upon men who stay behind from the Jumuʿah, their houses.” Zuhayr said: Abū Isḥāq narrated to us that he heard it from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ.
items.ma-3817: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, al-Ashjaʿī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh and Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, they said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, before the Hour there will be days in which knowledge is lifted, and ignorance descends, and al-harj becomes abundant in them.” He said: And al-harj is killing.
items.ma-3818: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, ʿImrān narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿAbd Rabbih, from Abū ʿIyāḍ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Beware of the belittled sins, for they gather upon a man until they destroy him.” And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck a parable for them: like a people who alighted in a desolate land, and the people's cooking was at hand, so a man would go off and come with a stick, and [another] man would come with a stick, until they had gathered a great mass, and they kindled a fire and cooked what they threw into it.
items.ma-3819: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was shown the nations at the season, and his ummah was slow in coming to him. He said: “So my ummah was shown to me, and their multitude pleased me; they had filled the plain and the mountain. It was said to me: Indeed with these are seventy thousand who enter Paradise without reckoning; they are those who do not cauterise, do not seek ruqyah, do not take bad omens, and upon their Rabb they rely.” ʿUkkāshah said: O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah that He make me one of them. So he supplicated for him. Then [another] stood - meaning another - and said: O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah that He make me one of them. He said: “ʿUkkāshah has preceded you with it.”
items.ma-3820: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: How do you recognise those of your ummah who have not seen you? He said: “Indeed they are white-browed, white-limbed, piebald, from the traces of wuḍūʾ.”
items.ma-3821: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When it is the remaining third of the night, [He] Yahbiṭu ilā al-samāʾ al-dunyā, then opens the gates of heaven, then Yabsuṭu Yadahu and says: Is there any asker, that his request be granted? And He continues like that until the dawn shines forth.”
items.ma-3822: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Abān ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Bajalī narrated to us, from Karīm ibn Abī Ḥāzim, from his grandmother Salmā bint Jābir, that her husband became a shahīd, so she came to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and said: I am a woman whose husband has become a shahīd, and men have proposed to me, and I refused to marry until I meet him; do you hope for me, if he and I are brought together, that I will be among his wives? He said: Yes. A man said to him: We have not seen you do this since we have been sitting with you! He said: Indeed I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed the quickest of my ummah to join me in Paradise is a woman from Aḥmas.”
items.ma-3823: Muḥāḍir Abū al-Muwarriʿ narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from ʿAwsajah ibn al-Rammāḥ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Hudhayl, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: “O Allah, You have made good my creation, so make good my character.”
items.ma-3824: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from his father, he said: I came to Abū Jahl, and he had been wounded and his leg had been cut off. He said: So I began to strike him with my sword, but it did nothing to him - it was said to Sharīk: In the ḥadīth: and he was warding off with his sword? He said: Yes -. He said: I did not cease until I took his sword and struck him with it until I killed him. He said: Then I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Abū Jahl has been killed - and perhaps Sharīk said: I have killed Abū Jahl -. He said: “Did you see him?” I said: Yes. He said: “By Allah?” twice? I said: Yes. He said: “Then go, so that I may look at him.” So he went and came to him, and the sun had changed something of him. So he commanded concerning him and his companions, and they were dragged until they were thrown into the well. He said: And the people of the well were followed with a curse. And he said: “This was the Pharaoh of this ummah.”
items.ma-3825: Aswad narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “This is the Pharaoh of my ummah.”
items.ma-3826: Ṭalq ibn Ghannām ibn Ṭalq narrated to us, Zakariyyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd narrated to us, from his father, he said: An old man from Banū Asad narrated to me - either he said: Shaqīq, or he said: Zirr - from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I witnessed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ supplicating for this clan of al-Nakhaʿ, or he said: praising them, until I wished that I were a man from them.
items.ma-3827: Abū Salamah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad informed us, from ʿAmr, meaning Ibn Abī ʿAmr, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ eat meat, then stand for the prayer, and he did not touch a drop of water.
items.ma-3828: Abū al-Jawwāb narrated to us, ʿAmmār ibn Ruzayq narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to seek refuge from Shayṭān, from his prodding, his blowing and his puffing. He said: And his prodding is madness, his blowing is poetry, and his puffing is pride.
items.ma-3829: Khalaf ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah narrated to us, from Zubayd, from Murrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The polytheists detained the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the ʿAṣr prayer until the sun turned yellow or red, and he said: “They have occupied us from the middle prayer. May Allah fill their insides - or may Allah stuff their insides - and their graves with fire.”
items.ma-3830: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us, [ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad said:] and I myself heard it from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Prophet ﷺ used to say: “O Allah, I seek refuge with You from Shayṭān, from his prodding, his blowing and his puffing.” So his prodding is madness, his blowing is poetry, and his puffing is arrogance.
items.ma-3831: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A people will come forth at the end of time, foolish of mind, young - or he said: youthful - of age. They speak from the best of the speech of people. They recite the Qurʾān with their tongues, [and] it does not pass their collarbones. They pass out of Islam as the arrow passes through the quarry. So whoever reaches them, let him kill them, for in killing them there is a great reward with Allah for whoever kills them.”
items.ma-3832: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The first to display their Islam were seven: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿAmmār, his mother Sumayyah, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl, and al-Miqdād. As for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Allah protected him through his uncle Abū Ṭālib; and as for Abū Bakr, Allah protected him through his people; and as for the rest of them, the polytheists seized them, clothed them in coats of iron mail, and scorched them in the sun, and there was no one among them who did not accede to them in what they wanted, except Bilāl, for his soul was cheap to him for the sake of Allah, and he was held cheap by his people. So they gave him to the boys, and they began to take him around the mountain paths of Makkah, while he was saying: Aḥad, Aḥad.
items.ma-3833: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUbayd Allāh narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, that ʿAbd Allāh narrated to them that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: “Your permission [to come] to me is that you lift the curtain and that you hear my sawād, until I forbid you.”
items.ma-3834: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, he said: Sulaymān said: I heard them mention, from Ibrāhīm ibn Suwayd, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Your permission [to come] to me is that you uncover the screen.”
items.ma-3835: Abū Qaṭan narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped at a halting place, and a person went off to a thicket and took out from it the eggs of a ḥummarah, and the ḥummarah came, fluttering over the head of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the heads of his Companions. He said: “Which of you has bereaved this one?” A man from the people said: I took some eggs of hers. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Return it.”
items.ma-3836: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī informed us, from al-Qāsim and al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped at a halting place … So he mentioned the like of it, and he said: “Return it, as mercy for her.”
items.ma-3837: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Hāshimī narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh informed us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from Ibn Muʿayz al-Saʿdī, he said: I went out to water a horse of mine before dawn, and I passed by the mosque of Banū Ḥanīfah, and they were saying: Indeed Musaylimah is the Messenger of Allah. So I came to ʿAbd Allāh and informed him, and he sent the police, and they brought them, and he asked them to repent, so they repented and he released them, and he struck the neck of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Nawwāḥah. They said: You seized a people in one matter, and you killed some of them and left some? He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when this one and Ibn Uthāl ibn Ḥajar came to him, and he said: “Do you both bear witness that I am the Messenger of Allah?” They said: We bear witness that Musaylimah is the Messenger of Allah. The Prophet ﷺ said: “I believe in Allah and His messengers, and were I to kill a delegation, I would have killed you both.” For that reason I killed him.
items.ma-3838: Muḥammad ibn Sābiq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Respond to the one who invites, do not reject the gift, and do not strike the Muslims.”
items.ma-3839: Muḥammad ibn Sābiq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The believer is not a taunter, nor a curser, nor the obscene, vulgar one.” And Ibn Sābiq once said: “…the taunter, nor the curser.”
items.ma-3840: Muḥammad ibn Sābiq narrated to us, ʿĪsā ibn Dīnār narrated to us, my father narrated to me, that he heard ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith say: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd say: I did not fast twenty-nine [days] with the Prophet ﷺ more than I fasted thirty with him.
items.ma-3841: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq, he said: I was sitting with ʿAbd Allāh and Abū Mūsā, and they were conversing, and they said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Before the Hour there are days in which knowledge is lifted, and ignorance descends in them, and al-harj appears in them” - and al-harj is killing.
items.ma-3842: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: When the Prophet ﷺ was taken, the Anṣār said: From us a commander and from you a commander. So ʿUmar came to them and said: O assembly of the Anṣār, do you not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Abū Bakr to lead the people [in prayer]? They said: Yes. He said: So which of you is pleased in his soul to go ahead of Abū Bakr? The Anṣār said: We seek refuge with Allah from going ahead of Abū Bakr.
items.ma-3843: Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: A black slave caught up with the Prophet ﷺ and died, and the Prophet ﷺ was informed. He said: “Look whether he left anything.” They said: He left two dīnārs. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Two brandings.”
items.ma-3844: Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed, among the worst of people are those whom the Hour overtakes while they are alive, and those who take the graves as mosques.”
items.ma-3845: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀbis, he said: A man from Hamdān, from the companions of ʿAbd Allāh, narrated to us, and he did not name him to us, he said: When ʿAbd Allāh wanted to go to al-Madīnah, he gathered his companions and said: By Allah, I hope that there has come to be among you today some of the best of what has come to be among the armies of the Muslims of religion, understanding, and knowledge of the Qurʾān. Indeed this Qurʾān was sent down in ḥurūf. By Allah, two men would dispute more intensely than they had ever disputed over anything, and when the reciter said: This one made me recite, he would say: You have done well; and when the other said it, he would say: Each of you two has done well. So he made us recite: Indeed truthfulness guides to righteousness, and righteousness guides to Paradise, and lying guides to wickedness, and wickedness guides to the Fire, and take lesson from that in the saying of one of you to his companion: He lied and acted wickedly, and in his saying, when he declares him truthful: You spoke the truth and acted righteously. Indeed this Qurʾān does not differ, is not worn out, and does not become worthless through much repetition. So whoever recites it according to a ḥarf, let him not leave it out of aversion to it; and whoever recites it according to any of those ḥurūf which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught, let him not leave it out of aversion to it, for whoever denies a verse of it denies all of it. It is only like the saying of one of you to his companion: Hurry, and ḥayya halā. By Allah, if I knew a man more knowledgeable than I of what Allah sent down upon Muḥammad ﷺ, I would seek him out, so as to add his knowledge to my knowledge. There will be a people who will let the prayer die, so pray the prayer at its time, and make your prayer with them a voluntary one. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to be reviewed with the Qurʾān every Ramaḍān, and I was reviewed in the year in which he was taken twice, and he informed me that I was doing well, and I recited seventy sūrahs from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-3846: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from Khumayr ibn Mālik, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I recited seventy sūrahs from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and indeed Zayd ibn Thābit had a forelock in the writing school.
items.ma-3847: Hāshim narrated to us, Shaybān narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim; and ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in Jahannam.” One of them said: in the Fire.
items.ma-3848: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿAyyāsh al-ʿĀmirī, from al-Aswad ibn Hilāl, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, among the signs of the Hour is that a man gives the salām to a man; he gives him the salām only for acquaintance.”
items.ma-3849: Hāshim and Ḥusayn narrated to us, in meaning, they said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us; and Abū Aḥmad: Isrāʾīl narrated to me, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ and al-Aswad ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ give the salām to his right: Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah, until the whiteness of his right cheek appeared, and to his left likewise.
items.ma-3850: Hāshim and Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, they said: Shaybān narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I am your forerunner at the Ḥawḍ, and I will indeed be contended with over men from my Companions, and I will indeed be overcome regarding them; then it will indeed be said to me: Indeed you do not know what they innovated after you.”
items.ma-3851: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ṣilah, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the messenger of Musaylimah came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said to him: “Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of Allah?” So he said something to him, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Were it not that I do not kill messengers - or: if I were to kill any of the messengers - I would have killed you.”
items.ma-3852: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: A man for whom cauterisation had been described was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “Cauterise him, or: apply hot stones to him.”
items.ma-3853: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to recite: {So is there any who will remember?}
items.ma-3854: al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā, from the people of Marw, narrated to us, al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā narrated to us, from Sufyān al-Thawrī, from Simāk, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I obtained from a woman everything except that I did not have intercourse with her? He said: So Allah sent down: {And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night. Indeed, the good deeds remove the evil deeds} [Hūd: 114].
items.ma-3855: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Prophet ﷺ said to a man: “Were it not that you are a messenger, I would have killed you.”
items.ma-3856: Umayyah ibn Khālid narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah has killed Abū Jahl. He said: “Praise be to Allah, who gave victory to His servant and honoured His religion,” and he said once - meaning Umayyah -: “He was true to His servant and honoured His religion.”
items.ma-3857: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, Abū Muʿāwiyah - meaning Shaybān - narrated to us, from Abū al-Yaʿfūr, from Abū al-Ṣalt, from Abū ʿAqrab, he said: I went in the morning to Ibn Masʿūd one morning in Ramaḍān and found him sitting on top of his house, and we heard his voice as he was saying: Allah has been truthful, and His Messenger has conveyed. We said: We heard you say: Allah has been truthful, and His Messenger has conveyed. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Laylat al-Qadr is in the middle of the last seven [nights] of Ramaḍān; the sun rises on that morning clear, with no rays.” So I looked at it and found it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said.
items.ma-3858: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, Abū Yaʿfūr narrated to us, from Abū al-Ṣalt, from Abū ʿAqrab al-Asadī, he said: I went in the morning to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd … So he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-3859: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, Abū ʿAqīl narrated to us, Mujālid narrated to us, from al-Shaʿbī, from Masrūq, he said: We were sitting with ʿAbd Allāh in the mosque as he made us recite, and a man came to him and said: O Ibn Masʿūd, did your Prophet tell you how many caliphs there will be after him? He said: Yes, like the number of the chiefs of Banū Isrāʾīl.
items.ma-3860: Abū al-Naḍr and Ḥasan narrated to us, they said: Shaybān narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast three days from the beginning of each new moon, and seldom would he break the fast on the day of Jumuʿah.
items.ma-3861: Muḥammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us. And ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, from Ibn Abī ʿArūbah, from Qatādah, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on one of his journeys, we heard a caller calling: Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: “Upon the fiṭrah.” Then he said: I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: “He has come out of the Fire.” He said: So we hurried to him, and behold, he was an owner of livestock whom the prayer had overtaken, so he called out for it.
items.ma-3862: Zayd ibn Ḥubāb narrated to us, Ḥusayn narrated to me, ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah narrated to me, he said: I heard Shaqīq ibn Salamah say: I heard Ibn Masʿūd say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I saw Jibrīl at Sidrat al-Muntahā, and he had six hundred wings.” He said: I asked ʿĀṣim about the wings, and he refused to inform me. He said: And some of his companions informed me: that the wing is what is between the east and the west.
items.ma-3863: Zayd ibn al-Ḥubāb narrated to us, Ḥusayn narrated to me, Ḥuṣayn narrated to me, Shaqīq narrated to me, he said: I heard Ibn Masʿūd say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Jibrīl came to me in green, with pearls hung upon him.”
items.ma-3864: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah narrated to us, from al-Walīd ibn Qays, from Isḥāq ibn Abī al-Kahtalah, Muḥammad said: I think it is from Ibn Masʿūd, that he said: Indeed Muḥammad did not see Jibrīl in his form except twice. As for one time, he asked him to show him himself in his form, so he showed him his form, and it blocked the horizon; and as for the other time, he ascended with him when he ascended with him. And His saying: {And he was at the highest horizon. Then he approached and descended. And was at a distance of two bows or nearer. And he revealed to His servant what he revealed} [al-Najm: 7 - 10]. He said: So when Jibrīl sensed his Rabb, he returned to his form and prostrated. And His saying: {And he certainly saw him in another descent. At Sidrat al-Muntahā. Near it is the Garden of the Refuge. When there covered the Sidrah that which covered. The sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress. He certainly saw of the greatest signs of his Rabb} [al-Najm: 13 - 18]. He said: [It was] the creation of Jibrīl ﵇.
items.ma-3865: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Abū Bakr narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Wāʾil, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever sets up a rival to Allah, Allah will place him in the Fire.” He said: And another [matter] I say, which I did not hear from him: And whoever dies not setting up a rival to Allah, Allah ﷿ will admit him to Paradise. And these prayers are kaffārāt for what is between them, so long as the killing is avoided.
items.ma-3866: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Abū Bakr informed us, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “And indeed I am your forerunner at the Ḥawḍ, and indeed I will be contended with over men and be overcome regarding them, and I will say: O Rabb, my Companions! And He says: Indeed you do not know what they innovated after you.”
items.ma-3867: Rawḥ narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Salām, from Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast on the journey and to break the fast, and to pray the two rakʿahs, not leaving them; he says: not adding to them, meaning the obligatory [prayer].
items.ma-3868: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Abān narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The most severe of people in punishment on the Day of Resurrection: a man whom a prophet killed, or who killed a prophet, and an imām of misguidance, and one who makes likenesses among those who make likenesses.”
items.ma-3869: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated to us, Bashīr ibn Salmān narrated to us - he used to stay at the Mosque of al-Maṭmūrah -, from Sayyār Abū Ḥamzah, from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever is struck by need, and brings it down upon the people, his need will not be closed; and whoever brings it down upon Allah ﷿, Allah will hasten wealth for him, either a swift term or swift wealth.”
items.ma-3870: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated to us, Bashīr ibn Salmān narrated to us, from Sayyār, from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, he said: We were sitting with ʿAbd Allāh, and a man came and said: The prayer has been established. So he stood and we stood with him. When we entered the mosque, we saw the people bowing in the front of the mosque, so he said the takbīr and bowed, and we bowed, then we walked, and we did as he had done. A man passed by, hurrying, and said: Upon you be peace, O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. He said: Allah and His Messenger have been truthful. When we had prayed and returned, he went in to his family; we sat, and some of us said to others: Did you not hear his reply to the man: Allah has been truthful, and His messengers have conveyed? Which of you will ask him? Ṭāriq said: I will ask him. So he asked him when he came out, and he mentioned from the Prophet ﷺ: “Indeed, before the Hour there will be the giving of the salām to the select few, the spread of trade, until the woman helps her husband in trade, the severing of the ties of kinship, false testimony, the concealing of the testimony of truth, and the appearance of the pen.”
items.ma-3871: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, ʿĪsā ibn Dīnār narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Ḍirār al-Khuzāʿī, he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd say: I did not fast twenty-nine [days] with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ more than I fasted thirty with him.
items.ma-3872: Yūnus narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, who narrated to him, from his father, that Ibn Masʿūd narrated to him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would, for the most part, turn away from the prayer to his left, toward the chambers.
items.ma-3873: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: That I swear nine times that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was killed is more beloved to me than that I swear once that he was not killed; and that is because Allah made him a prophet, and took him as a shahīd. al-Aʿmash said: So I mentioned that to Ibrāhīm, and he said: They used to consider that the Jews had poisoned him, and Abū Bakr.
items.ma-3874: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, he said: ʿAbd Allāh used to throw the Jamrah from the valley bed. I said: Is it from here that you throw it? He said: From here, by the One other than Whom there is no deity, he upon whom Sūrat al-Baqarah was sent down threw it.
items.ma-3875: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿUmārah, from Wahb ibn Rabīʿah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: I was hiding myself behind the coverings of the Kaʿbah, when three men came: a Thaqafī and his two in-laws from Quraysh, abundant the fat of their bellies, little the understanding of their hearts. They conversed among themselves, and he said: One of them said: Do you think that Allah ﷿ Yasmaʿu what we said? The other said: I think that He Yasmaʿu if we raise [our voices] and does not Yasmaʿu if we lower [them]. The other said: If He Yasmaʿu any of it, then He Yasmaʿuhu all of it. He said: So I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: So Allah ﷿ sent down: {And you were not hiding yourselves lest your hearing testify against you} until: {the losers} [Fuṣṣilat: 22, 23].
items.ma-3876: Wakīʿ narrated to us, ʿUmar ibn Dharr narrated to us, from al-ʿAyzār ibn Jarwal al-Ḥaḍramī, from a man of theirs who was given the kunyah Abū ʿUmayr, that he was a friend of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, and that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd visited him at his home and did not find him. He said: So he asked permission of his family and gave the salām, and asked for something to drink. He said: So the girl was sent to bring him a drink from the neighbours, and she was slow, so he cursed her. ʿAbd Allāh went out, and Abū ʿUmayr came and said: O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, one like you is not [one over whom] jealousy is felt. Why did you not give the salām to the family of your brother, and sit, and take some of the drink? He said: I did. So I sent the servant, and she was slow - either they did not have any with them, or they were reluctant about what they had - and the servant was slow, so I cursed her. And I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed the curse, when it is directed to the one to whom it is directed, if it finds a way against him, or finds a path in him, and if not, it says: O Rabb, I was directed to so-and-so, and I found no way against him, and I found no path in him. Then it is said to it: Return from where you came.” So I feared that the servant was excused, so that the curse would return, and I would be its cause.
items.ma-3877: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taught the openings of good and its comprehensive [matters] - or the comprehensive [matters] of good and its openings - and we did not know what to say in our prayer until he taught us. So he said: Say: “The greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.”
items.ma-3878: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Were I to take anyone as a khalīl, I would have taken Ibn Abī Quḥāfah as a khalīl.”
items.ma-3879: Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, al-Ḥasan narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give the salām to his right and to his left, until the whiteness of his cheek was seen: Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah.
items.ma-3880: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed I declare myself free, before every khalīl, of his khill; and were I to take a khalīl, I would have taken Ibn Abī Quḥāfah as a khalīl, and indeed your companion is the khalīl of Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-3881: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Aʿwar, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: The one who consumes ribā, the one who feeds it, its writer and its two witnesses, if they know it, and the woman who tattoos and the woman who has herself tattooed for beauty, and the one who withholds the ṣadaqah, and the one who turns back as a Bedouin after his emigration: are cursed on the tongue of Muḥammad ﷺ on the Day of Resurrection. He said: So I mentioned that to Ibrāhīm, and he said: ʿAlqamah narrated to me, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: The one who consumes ribā and the one who feeds it are equal.
items.ma-3882: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Khuṣayf, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he lined up a row behind him, and [there was] a row facing the enemy. He said: And all of them were in prayer. He said: And he said the takbīr and they all said the takbīr, and he prayed with the row that adjoined him one rakʿah, while a row was facing the enemy. He said: Then those went away and those came, and he prayed with them one rakʿah. Then those with whom he had prayed stood for the second rakʿah and completed it in their place. Then those went to the places of those in the rows, and those others came and completed a rakʿah.
items.ma-3883: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Jābir, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Prophet ﷺ prayed the Ẓuhr, or the ʿAṣr, [with] five [rakʿahs], then performed the two prostrations of forgetfulness. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “These two prostrations are for whoever of you thinks that he has added or omitted.”
items.ma-3884: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: We used to give the salām to the Prophet ﷺ in the prayer, until we returned from the Najāshī; so we gave him the salām and he did not reply to us, and he said: “Indeed in the prayer there is an occupation.”
items.ma-3885: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, Muṭarrif narrated to us, from Abū al-Jahm, from Abū al-Raḍrāḍ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: I used to give the salām to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the prayer, and he would reply to me. Then one day I gave him the salām and he did not reply to me, and I felt something in myself. When he had finished, I said: O Messenger of Allah, whenever I gave you the salām in the prayer, you replied to me? He said: So he said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ brings about in His affair whatever He wills.”
items.ma-3886: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: Will any one of us be held to account for what he did in the Jāhiliyyah? He said: “Whoever does good in Islam will not be held to account for what he did in the Jāhiliyyah, and whoever does evil in Islam will be seized for the first and the last.”
items.ma-3887: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, al-Thawrī narrated to us, from Jābir, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Among what I forgot of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I did not forget that he used to give the salām to his right: Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah, until the whiteness of his cheek was seen; and to his left: Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah, until the whiteness of his cheek was seen as well.
items.ma-3888: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar and al-Thawrī narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ … like the ḥadīth of Abū al-Ḍuḥā.
items.ma-3889: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “How will it be with you, O ʿAbd Allāh, when there are over you commanders who neglect the sunnah and delay the prayer from its time?” He said: What do you command me, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “You ask me, O Ibn Umm ʿAbd, how you should act? There is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-3890: ʿAffān ibn Muslim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, al-Walīd ibn al-ʿAyzār ibn Ḥurayth informed me, he said: I heard Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī say: The owner of this house narrated to us - and he pointed to the house of ʿAbd Allāh, and did not name him -, he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Which deed is most beloved to Allah? He said: “The prayer at its time.” He said: I said: Then which? He said: “Then dutifulness to parents.” He said: I said: Then which? He said: “Then jihād in the way of Allah.” He said: So he narrated them to me, and had I asked him for more, he would have given me more.
items.ma-3891: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, he said: I heard Abū ʿUbaydah, from his father, he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to say often: “Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me.” So when {When the victory of Allah and the conquest come} was revealed, he said: “Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me. Indeed You are al-Tawwāb.”
items.ma-3892: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr narrated to us, from Khālid ibn Ribʿī al-Asadī, that he heard Ibn Masʿūd say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed your companion is the khalīl of Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-3893: ʿAffān narrated to us, Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū Isḥāq narrating, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, he said: We performed Ḥajj with Ibn Masʿūd in the caliphate of ʿUthmān. He said: When we stood at ʿArafah, and the sun had set, Ibn Masʿūd said: If the Commander of the Believers were to set out now, he would have done right. He said: And I do not know whether the word of Ibn Masʿūd was quicker, or the setting out of ʿUthmān. He said: So the people hurried on, and Ibn Masʿūd did not go beyond the ʿanaq, until we came to Jamʿ, and Ibn Masʿūd prayed the Maghrib with us, then called for his supper, then ate supper, then stood and prayed the last ʿIshāʾ, then slept, until when the first of the dawn rose, he stood and prayed the morning prayer. He said: I said to him: You did not [use to] pray the prayer at this hour! - and he used to pray when it was bright -. He said: Indeed I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on this day, and in this place, pray at this hour.
items.ma-3894:
Khalaf ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Khālid narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Shaqīq ibn Salamah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disparaged to us the night conversation after the ʿIshāʾ.
Khālid said: The meaning of jadaba ilaynā: he means: he found fault with it, he censured it.
items.ma-3895: ʿAffān and Bahz narrated to us, they said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm informed me, he said: I heard Abū ʿUbaydah narrating, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ: He was in the first two rakʿahs as if on hot stones. I said: Until he stands? He said: Until he stands.
items.ma-3896:
ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Abū Isḥāq informed us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, he said: ʿAbd Allāh used to say: Indeed lying is not fitting, whether in earnest or in jest - and ʿAffān said once: in earnest - and a man must not promise a child, then not fulfil it for him.
He said: And indeed Muḥammad said to us: “A man continues to speak the truth until he is written with Allah as a ṣiddīq, and a man continues to lie until he is written with Allah as a great liar.”
items.ma-3897: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Abān ibn Taghlib, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he mentioned the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to say: “Labbayka, O Allah, labbayka; labbayka, there is no partner for You, labbayka. Indeed the praise and the favour are Yours.”
items.ma-3898: ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us - ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad said:] and I myself heard it from ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah -, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: While the Prophet ﷺ was in a tilled field, leaning on a palm-stalk, a group of the Jews stood up to him and asked him about the rūḥ. He was silent, then recited this verse to them: {They ask you about the rūḥ. Say: The rūḥ is of the affair of my Rabb, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little} [al-Isrāʾ: 85].
items.ma-3899: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, Thābit informed us, from Anas ibn Mālik, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The last to enter Paradise is a man; he walks once, and stumbles once, and the Fire scorches him once. When he has passed beyond it, he turns to it and says: Tabāraka the One who delivered me from you; Allah has indeed given me something He has not given to anyone of the first and the last. Then a tree is raised for him, and he says: O Rabb, bring me near this tree, that I may take shade in its shade and drink from its water. Allah says: O son of Ādam, perhaps if I give it to you, you will ask me for something other than it? He says: No, O Rabb, and he pledges to Him that he will not ask Him for anything other than it. He said: And his Rabb ﷿ excuses him, because he sees what he has no patience against. So He brings him near it, and he takes shade in its shade and drinks from its water. Then a tree is raised for him that is better than the first, and he says: O Rabb, this one; let me drink from its water and take shade in its shade; I will not ask You for anything other than it. He says: O son of Ādam, did you not pledge to Me that you would not ask Me for anything other than it? He says: Perhaps if I bring you near it, you will ask me for something other than it? So he pledges to Him that he will not ask Him for anything other than it, and his Rabb ﷿ excuses him, because he sees what he has no patience against. So He brings him near it, and he takes shade in its shade and drinks from its water. Then a tree is raised for him at the gate of Paradise, which is better than the first two, and he says: O Rabb, bring me near this tree, that I may take shade in its shade and drink from its water; I will not ask You for anything other than it. He says: O son of Ādam, did you not pledge to Me that you would not ask Me for anything other than it? He said: Yes, O Rabb, this one; I will not ask You for anything other than it. He says: Perhaps if I bring you near it, you will ask me for something other than it? So he pledges to Him that he will not ask Him for anything other than it, and his Rabb excuses him, because he sees what he has no patience against. So He brings him near it, and when He has brought him near it, he hears the voices of the people of Paradise, and says: O Rabb, admit me into it. He says: O son of Ādam, what will cut me off from you? Will it please you that I give you the world and the like of it with it? He says: O Rabb, are You mocking me, while You are Rabb of the worlds?” Then Ibn Masʿūd laughed and said: Will you not ask me what I am laughing at? They said: What are you laughing at? He said: Thus the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed, and he said: “Will you not ask me what I am laughing at?” They said: What are you laughing at, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “From the Ḍaḥik of my Rabb when he said: Are You mocking me, while You are Rabb of the worlds?! Then He says: I am not mocking you, but I am Qadīr over what I will.”
items.ma-3900: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “For every treacherous one there will be a banner on the Day of Resurrection.”
items.ma-3901: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah informed us, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: On the day of Badr we were three to each camel; Abū Lubābah and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib were the two riding-companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: And it was the turn of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: So they said: We will walk in your place. He said: “You two are not stronger than I, nor am I more free of need of the reward than you two.”
items.ma-3902: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Sulaymān al-Aʿmash informed me, he said: I heard Abū Wāʾil say: I heard ʿAbd Allāh say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a distribution, and a man from the people said: Indeed this is a distribution by which Wajh Allāh ﷿ is not intended!! He said: So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him. He said: So he became angry, until I saw anger in his face, and he said: “May Allah have mercy on Mūsā; he was harmed with more than that, and was patient.”
items.ma-3903: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Zubayd, Manṣūr and Sulaymān informed me that they heard Abū Wāʾil narrating, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Reviling a Muslim is fusūq, and fighting him is kufr.” Zubayd said: I said to Abū Wāʾil twice: Did you hear it from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ? He said: Yes.
items.ma-3904: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Abū Isḥāq informed us, he said: I heard Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to say: “O Allah, I ask You for God-fearingness, guidance, chastity, and wealth.”
items.ma-3905: ʿAffān narrated to us, Masʿūd ibn Saʿd narrated to us, Khuṣayf narrated to us, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote regarding the ṣadaqah of cattle: “When cattle reach thirty, there is in them a tabīʿ of the cattle, a jadhaʿ or a jadhaʿah, until they reach forty. When they reach forty, there is in them a musinnah cow. When the cattle become many, then in every forty of the cattle, a musinnah cow.”
items.ma-3906: ʿAffān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid narrated to us, Sulaymān al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq ibn Salamah, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd addressed us and said: I took from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seventy-odd sūrahs, while Zayd ibn Thābit was a boy with two forelocks, playing with the boys.
items.ma-3907: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah informed me, he said: I heard al-Nazzāl ibn Sabrah say: I heard ʿAbd Allāh say: I heard a man recite a verse other than the way the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had made me recite it, so I took him by the hand until I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: “Each of you two is doing well. Do not differ” - the greater part of my knowledge, and if not, then Misʿar narrated it to me - “for those before you differed over it, and so they perished.”
items.ma-3908: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah narrated to me, he said: I heard al-Nazzāl ibn Sabrah narrating, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I heard a man reciting a verse other than the way the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had made me recite, so I took him by the hand and came with him to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “Each of you has done well.” He said: And he became angry, until anger was recognised in his face. Shuʿbah said: The greater part of my thought is that he said: “Do not differ, for those before you differed over it, and so they perished.”
items.ma-3909: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, he said: I heard Abū al-Aḥwaṣ say: ʿAbd Allāh used to say, from the Prophet ﷺ: “Were I to take a khalīl from my ummah, I would have taken Abū Bakr.”
items.ma-3910: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Zirr, that a man said to Ibn Masʿūd: How do you recognise this ḥarf: {water not yāsin} or {āsin}? He said: Have you recited all of the Qurʾān? He said: I recite the whole of the Mufaṣṣal in one rakʿah. He said: Reciting rapidly like poetry, may you have no father?! I know the pairs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to join together, two pairs at a time, from the beginning of the Mufaṣṣal. And the beginning of Ibn Masʿūd's Mufaṣṣal was: {al-Raḥmān}.
items.ma-3911: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib informed us, from Ibn Udhunān, he said: I lent ʿAlqamah two thousand dirhams; when his allowance came out, I said to him: Repay me. He said: Delay me until next year. I refused him and took it. He said: Then I came to him afterwards, and he said: You have distressed me, and you have denied me. I said: Yes, it is your own doing. He said: And what is my matter? I said: Indeed you narrated to me from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Indeed a loan runs in the course of half a ṣadaqah.” He said: Yes, it is so. He said: Then take it now.
items.ma-3912: ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah narrated to us, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, from Ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “The two eyes commit zinā, the two hands commit zinā, the two feet commit zinā, and the private part commits zinā.”
items.ma-3913: ʿAffān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muslim narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to me, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He will not enter Paradise who has in his heart the weight of a grain of arrogance, and he will not enter the Fire who has in his heart the weight of a mustard grain of īmān.”
items.ma-3914: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah informed us, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: that a man of the people of the Ṣuffah died, and two dīnārs were found in his cloak, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Two brandings.”
items.ma-3915: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr, from Ibn Masʿūd, that he said regarding this verse: {And he certainly saw him in another descent} [al-Najm: 13], the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I saw Jibrīl at Sidrat al-Muntahā, upon him six hundred wings, scattering from his feathers the variegated things: pearls and rubies.”
items.ma-3916: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym informed us, from ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever says: O Allah, Fāṭir of the heavens and the earth, ʿĀlim of the unseen and the witnessed, I make a covenant with You in this worldly life that I bear witness that there is no deity except You alone, no partner for You, and that Muḥammad is Your servant and Your Messenger; for if You entrust me to myself, You bring me near to evil and distance me from good, and I trust only in Your mercy; so make for me with You a covenant that You will fulfil for me on the Day of Resurrection; indeed You do not break the appointment - except that Allah says to His angels on the Day of Resurrection: Indeed My servant has made a covenant with Me, so fulfil it for him; and Allah admits him to Paradise.” Suhayl said: So I informed al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān that ʿAwn had informed [me of] such and such, and he said: There is no girl in our family but she says this in her screened chamber.
items.ma-3917: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Manṣūr informed me, he said: I heard Khaythamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “There is no night conversation except for one of two men: one who prays, or a traveller.”
items.ma-3918: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Abū Isḥāq informed us, he said: I heard al-Aswad narrating, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to recite this word: {So is there any who will take heed?} with the letter dāl.
items.ma-3919: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, Manṣūr narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: When we prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a man among us would say in his prayer: “Peace be upon Allah, peace be upon so-and-so,” singling out [individuals]. Then one day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: “Indeed Allah ﷿ is al-Salām. So when one of you sits in his prayer, let him say: ‘All greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah’ — and when you say that, you have greeted every servant in the heavens and the earth — ‘I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.’ Then let him choose whatever supplication he wishes — or whatever he likes.”
items.ma-3920:
Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: When we sat in the prayer, we used to say: “Peace be upon Allah, peace be upon us from our Rabb, peace be upon Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl, peace be upon so-and-so, peace be upon so-and-so.” So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah is al-Salām. So when you sit in the prayer, say: ‘All greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah’ — for when he says that, it reaches every righteous servant in the heaven and the earth — ‘I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.’ Then let him choose whatever speech he wishes.”
Sulaymān said: Ibrāhīm also narrated it to me, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh … the like of it.
items.ma-3921: Muʾammal narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Aswad, Abū al-Aḥwaṣ and Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to teach us the tashahhud in the prayer: “All greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.”
items.ma-3922: Muʾammal narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us — from ʿAṭāʾ, meaning Ibn al-Sāʾib — from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah ﷿ has not sent down any disease except that He sent down for it a remedy; whoever knew it knew it, and whoever was ignorant of it was ignorant of it.”
items.ma-3923: Muʾammal narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Paradise is nearer to one of you than the strap of his sandal, and the Fire is the same.”
items.ma-3924: Muʾammal narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The moon was split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, until I saw the mountain between the two parts of the moon.
items.ma-3925:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, al-Thawrī informed us, from ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad, from al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Yashkurī, from al-Maʿrūr ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Umm Ḥabībah said: “O Allah, grant me enjoyment of my husband the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and of my father Abū Sufyān, and of my brother Muʿāwiyah.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “You have asked Allah for appointed terms, apportioned provisions, and footsteps that will be reached. Nothing of them is hastened before its due time, and nothing of them is delayed after its due time. And if you had asked Allah to spare you from a punishment in the Fire and a punishment in the grave, it would have been better for you.”
He said: A man said: “O Messenger of Allah, the apes and the pigs, are they of what was transformed?” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah did not transform a people, or destroy a people, and then make for them offspring or a posterity. And indeed the apes and the pigs existed before that.”
items.ma-3926: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, he said: Abū Isḥāq mentioned, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Shayṭān passed by me, so I seized him and strangled him, until I could indeed feel the coolness of his tongue in my hands. He said: ‘You have hurt me, you have hurt me.’”
items.ma-3927: Aswad narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ibn al-Aswad, from ʿAlqamah and al-Aswad: that they were with Ibn Masʿūd, and the prayer became due. ʿAlqamah and al-Aswad stood back, so Ibn Masʿūd took them by their hands and stood one of them on his right and the other on his left. Then they bowed, and they placed their hands on their knees, and he struck their hands. Then he joined his hands together, interlaced [the fingers], and placed them between his thighs, and said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ do it.
items.ma-3928: Ḥusayn narrated it to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Aswad ibn Yazīd and ʿAlqamah ibn Qays … and he mentioned it.
items.ma-3929: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Khumayr ibn Mālik, he said: It was ordered that the copies of the Qurʾān be changed. He said: Ibn Masʿūd said: Whoever among you is able to conceal his copy of the Qurʾān, let him conceal it, for whoever conceals something will come with it on the Day of Resurrection. He said: Then he said: I recited seventy sūrahs from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Shall I leave what I took from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
items.ma-3930: Aswad narrated to us, he said: and Khalaf ibn al-Walīd informed us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ṣilah, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: al-ʿĀqib and al-Sayyid, the two leaders of Najrān, came. He said: They wanted to engage in mutual imprecation with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: One of them said to his companion: “Do not engage in mutual imprecation with him, for by Allah, if he is a prophet and he invokes a curse on us — Khalaf said: and we invoke a curse on each other — we will never succeed, neither we nor our descendants.” He said: So they came to him and said: “We will not engage in mutual imprecation with you, but we will give you what you ask, so send with us a trustworthy man.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “I will surely send a trustworthy man, truly trustworthy, truly trustworthy.” He said: The Companions of Muḥammad looked up eagerly for it. He said: Then he said: “Stand, O Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ.” He said: When he turned his back, he said: “This is the trustworthy one of this ummah.”
items.ma-3931: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, they said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: When the Prophet ﷺ went to sleep — Abū Aḥmad said: when he retired to his bed — he would place his right hand beneath his cheek — Abū Aḥmad said: the right — then say: “O Allah, protect me from Your punishment on the day You gather Your servants.”
items.ma-3932: Wakīʿ narrated it to us … with the same meaning.
items.ma-3933: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik, from Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Anṣārī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give the salutation in his prayer to his right and to his left, until the whiteness of his cheeks could be seen.
items.ma-3934: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Fiṭr narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Zayd ibn Wahb al-Juhanī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, and he is the truthful, the one who is believed: “The creation of one of you is gathered in his mother’s womb for forty nights, then he is a clinging clot for the like of that, then he is a chewed lump for the like of that. Then Allah ﷿ sends to him an angel from among the angels, who says: ‘Write his deeds, his term, and his provision, and write him wretched or happy.’” Then he said: By the One in whose hand is the soul of ʿAbd Allāh, a man will do the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is nothing between him and Paradise except a cubit; then wretchedness overtakes him, so he does the deeds of the people of the Fire, and he dies and enters the Fire. Then he said: By the One in whose hand is the soul of ʿAbd Allāh, a man will do the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is nothing between him and the Fire except a cubit; then happiness overtakes him, so he does the deeds of the people of Paradise, and he dies and enters Paradise.
items.ma-3935: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Sayf narrated to us, he said: I heard Mujāhid say: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sakhbarah Abū Maʿmar narrated to me, he said: I heard Ibn Masʿūd say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me the tashahhud — my palm between his palms — as he would teach me a sūrah of the Qurʾān. He said: “All greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.” And he was among us. Then when he was taken, we said: “Peace be upon the Prophet.”
items.ma-3936: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Abū ʿUmays narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar mention, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, that he said: Whoever it pleases to meet Allah tomorrow as a Muslim, let him be diligent in these prayers wherever they are called, for Allah has legislated for your Prophet the practices of guidance, and they are among the practices of guidance. If you were to pray in your houses as this one who stays behind prays in his house, you would have abandoned the Sunnah of your Prophet, and if you abandoned the Sunnah of your Prophet, you would go astray. There is no man who purifies himself and does the purification well, then sets out for one of these mosques, except that Allah writes for him a good deed for every step he takes, raises him a degree by it, and removes from him a bad deed by it. And if you had seen us, none stayed away from it except a hypocrite whose hypocrisy was known. And a man would be brought, supported between two men, until he was stood in the row.
items.ma-3937:
Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I prayed one night with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he did not cease standing, until I intended an evil thing. We said: “What did you intend?!” He said: I intended to sit down and leave the Prophet ﷺ.
Sulaymān said: Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah also narrated to us … the like of it.
items.ma-3938: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Hāshimī narrated to us, Saʿīd — meaning Ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jumaḥī — narrated to us, from Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, from al-Awdī, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Everyone gentle, soft, easy-going, and near to the people is forbidden to the Fire.”
items.ma-3939: Mūsā ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Zuhayr informed us, from Abū al-Ḥārith Yaḥyā al-Taymī, from Abū Mājid al-Ḥanafī, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We asked our Prophet ﷺ about walking with the funeral procession. He said: “Walking is [at a pace] below the khabab. If it is good, it is hastened to, or it is hastened toward it; and if it is other than that, then away with the people of the Fire. The funeral is followed and does not follow; he is not of us who goes ahead of it.”
items.ma-3940: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAjlān, he said: ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to me, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: When a ḥadīth is narrated to you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then think of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what is most befitting, most guided, and most God-fearing.
items.ma-3941: Rawḥ and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, they said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, Rawḥ said: al-Ḥakam narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, that he performed Ḥajj with ʿAbd Allāh, and he threw seven pebbles at the greatest Jamrah, placing the House on his left and Minā on his right, and he said: This is the standing place of the one upon whom Sūrat al-Baqarah was revealed.
items.ma-3942: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd went down into the middle of the valley, faced the Jamarāt squarely, and placed the mountain above his back, then threw, and said: This is the standing place of the one upon whom Sūrat al-Baqarah was revealed.
items.ma-3943: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: A black slave joined the Prophet ﷺ, then he died, and he was brought to the Prophet ﷺ. He said: “See whether he left anything.” They said: “He left two dīnārs.” He said: “Two brandings.”
items.ma-3944: Asbāṭ and Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, the meaning [being the same], they said: Muṭarrif narrated to us, from Abū al-Jahm, from Abū al-Raḍrāḍ, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I used to give greeting to the Prophet ﷺ while he was in prayer, and he would return it to me. Then one day I greeted him and he did not return anything to me, so I felt it in myself. I said: “O Messenger of Allah, I used to greet you while you were in prayer and you would return it to me, and I greeted you and you did not return anything to me?!” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah brings about in His affair whatever He wills.”
items.ma-3945: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn ʿAṭāʾ narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah informed us, from Qatādah, from ʿAzrah, from al-Ḥasan al-ʿUranī, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, from Masrūq, that a woman came to Ibn Masʿūd and said: “I have been informed that you forbid the wāṣilah.” He said: “Yes.” She said: “Is it something you find in the Book of Allah, or did you hear it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?!” He said: “I find it in the Book of Allah, and from the Messenger of Allah.” She said: “By Allah, I have gone through what is between the two covers of the copy of the Qurʾān, and I did not find in it what you say!” He said: “Did you find in it: {Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you from, abstain from it} [al-Ḥashr: 7]?” She said: “Yes.” He said: “Then I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid the nāmiṣah, the wāshirah, the wāṣilah and the wāshimah, except because of an illness.” The woman said: “Perhaps it is [done] by some of your women?” He said to her: “Enter.” So she entered, then came out and said: “I saw no harm.” He said: “Then I did not preserve the counsel of the righteous servant: {And I do not want to oppose you by [doing] what I forbid you from} [Hūd: 88].”
items.ma-3946: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, he said: Abū Bakr informed us, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever takes away the property of a Muslim man without right will meet Allah ﷿ while He is Ghaḍbān with him.”
items.ma-3947: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Abū Bakr informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “No man will enter Paradise in whose heart is the weight of an atom of arrogance, and no man will enter the Fire in whose heart is the weight of an atom of faith.”
items.ma-3948: Aswad narrated to us, Abū Bakr informed us, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAmr, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed the believer is not one who curses much, nor one who taunts, nor one who is obscene, nor one who is foul-mouthed.”
items.ma-3949: Rawḥ and ʿAffān narrated to us, they said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, ʿAffān said: ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib informed us, from Murrah al-Hamdānī, from Ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “ʿAjiba Rabbunā ﷿ min rajulayn: a man who rose from his bedding and his blanket, from among his family and his neighbourhood, to his prayer, so Rabbunā says: ‘O My angels, look at My servant: he rose from his bed and his bedding, and from among his neighbourhood and his family, to his prayer, out of desire for what is with Me and fear of what is with Me.’ And a man who went out to fight in the way of Allah ﷿, and they were routed, so he knew what was upon him in fleeing and what was for him in returning, so he returned until his blood was shed, out of desire for what is with Me and fear of what is with Me. So Allah ﷿ says to His angels: ‘Look at My servant: he returned out of desire for what is with Me and dread of what is with Me, until his blood was shed.’”
items.ma-3950: Rawḥ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū Isḥāq say: I heard Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrating, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to make this supplication: “O Allah, I ask You for guidance, God-fearing, chastity and sufficiency.”
items.ma-3952: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib informed us, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: Beware of saying: “So-and-so died a shahīd,” or “So-and-so was killed a shahīd,” for a man fights to gain spoils, and fights to be mentioned, and fights so that his position may be seen. So if you must bear witness, then bear witness for the group whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent in a detachment, and they were killed, and they said: “O Allah, convey to our Prophet ﷺ from us that we have met You, and we were pleased with You, and You were pleased with us.”
items.ma-3953: Rawḥ and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, they said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, he said: I heard ʿUmārah ibn ʿUmayr narrating — Ibn Jaʿfar said: or Ibrāhīm, Shuʿbah was in doubt — from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: I prayed two rakʿahs with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Minā, and two rakʿahs with Abū Bakr ﵁, and two rakʿahs with ʿUmar ﵁. Would that my share of the four were two accepted rakʿahs.
items.ma-3954: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Yūnus narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I spent the night reciting to the jinn, [as] companions, at al-Ḥajūn.”
items.ma-3955: Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah and Yaḥyā ibn Ḥammād narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿAwānah informed us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from al-ʿUryān ibn al-Haytham, from Qabīṣah ibn Jābir al-Asadī, he said: I went with an old woman of Banū Asad to Ibn Masʿūd, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursing the women who pluck [facial hair], the women who file their teeth, and the women who tattoo, who change the creation of Allah. Yaḥyā said: and the women who mark, who …
items.ma-3956: Ḥasan narrated to us, Shaybān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from al-ʿUryān ibn al-Haytham, from Qabīṣah ibn Jābir al-Asadī, he said: I went with an old woman to Ibn Masʿūd, and he mentioned an account. Then ʿAbd Allāh said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursing the women who pluck [facial hair], the women who file their teeth, and the women who tattoo, who change the creation of Allah ﷿.
items.ma-3957: Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A Muslim fighting his brother is kufr, and reviling him is fusūq.”
items.ma-3958: Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn, he said: Ibrāhīm narrated to me, from Nahīk ibn Sinān al-Sulamī, that he came to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and said: “I recited the Mufaṣṣal last night in one rakʿah.” He said: “Rapidly, like the rapid [recitation of] poetry, or scattering like the scattering of poor dates? It was only divided so that you would divide it. I know the similar [sūrahs] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pair: twenty sūrahs, al-Raḥmān and al-Najm according to the arrangement of Ibn Masʿūd, every two sūrahs in one rakʿah.” And he mentioned al-Dukhān and ʿAmma yatasāʾalūn in one rakʿah.
items.ma-3959: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Shuʿbah informed us, from al-Aʿmash, he heard Abū Wāʾil narrating, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “For every treacherous one there will be a banner, and it will be said: ‘This is the treachery of so-and-so.’”
items.ma-3960: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, he said: I heard Abū Wāʾil narrating, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “How evil it is for one of you — or: how evil it is for one of them — to say: ‘I have forgotten such-and-such verse,’ rather he was made to forget. Keep refreshing your memory of the Qurʾān, for by the One in whose hand is my soul, it escapes more readily from the hearts of men than camels from their hobbles.”
items.ma-3961: Ṣafwān ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed us, from Mujāhid, from Ibn Sakhbarah, he said: I went out in the morning with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd from Minā to ʿArafāt, and he was reciting the talbiyah. He said: ʿAbd Allāh was a dark-complexioned man with two plaits, and on him was the look of the people of the desert. A rabble of the rabble of the people gathered around him and said: “O Bedouin, this is not a day of talbiyah; it is only a day of takbīr!” He said: Then he turned to me and said: “Have the people become ignorant, or have they forgotten? By the One who sent Muḥammad ﷺ with the truth, I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he did not leave the talbiyah until he threw the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah, except that he would mix it with takbīr or tahlīl.”
items.ma-3962: Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoke against Quraysh except on one day. He was praying while a group of Quraysh were sitting, and the afterbirth of a slaughtered camel was near him. They said: “Who will take this afterbirth and throw it on his back?” He said: ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ said: “I [will],” so he took it and threw it on his back, and he remained in prostration until Fāṭimah, Ṣalawāt Allāh ʿalayhā, came and took it off his back. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, upon You is the assembly of Quraysh. O Allah, upon You is ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah. O Allah, upon You is Shaybah ibn Rabīʿah. O Allah, upon You is Abū Jahl ibn Hishām. O Allah, upon You is ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ. O Allah, upon You is Ubayy ibn Khalaf, or Umayyah ibn Khalaf.” He said: ʿAbd Allāh said: I saw them all killed on the day of Badr, then dragged to the well, except Ubayy, or Umayyah, for he was a huge man, so he fell apart.
items.ma-3963: Azhar ibn Saʿd narrated to us, Ibn ʿAwn informed us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “The best of people are my contemporaries, those who follow me, then those who follow them, then those who follow them.” He said: I do not know whether he said at the third or at the fourth: “Then there will come after them a succession whose testimony precedes the oath of one of them, and his oath precedes his testimony.”
items.ma-3964: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, he said: ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Zirr, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the nations were presented to the Prophet ﷺ. He said: Then his ummah was presented to him, and their great number pleased him. It was said: “With these are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning.”
items.ma-3965: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: On the day of Badr there was one camel for every three men, and the riding companions of the Prophet ﷺ were ʿAlī and Abū Lubābah. He said: When it was the turn of the Prophet ﷺ, the two would say to him: “Ride, so that we walk in your place.” He would say: “You two are not stronger than I, and I am not in less need of the reward than you.”
items.ma-3966: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: It is not Abū ʿUbaydah who mentioned it, but ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from his father, that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd say: The Prophet ﷺ went to the ghāʾiṭ and ordered me to bring him three stones. I found two stones and did not find the third, so I took a piece of dung and brought them to the Prophet ﷺ. He took the two stones and threw away the dung, and said: “This is rikṣ.”
items.ma-3967: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, and he mentioned the tashahhud, the tashahhud of ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ; and Manṣūr, al-Aʿmash and Ḥammād, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ … the like of it.
items.ma-3968: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Aswad ibn Yazīd and ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, that a man came to him and said: “I recited the Mufaṣṣal in one rakʿah.” He said: “Rather you recited rapidly like the rapid [recitation of] poetry, or like the scattering of poor dates. But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not do as you did. He used to recite the similar [sūrahs]: al-Raḥmān and al-Najm in one rakʿah.” He said: Abū Isḥāq mentioned ten rakʿahs, with twenty sūrahs according to the arrangement of ʿAbd Allāh, the last of them: {When the sun is wrapped up} and al-Dukhān.
items.ma-3969: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, he said: I was with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd at Jamʿ, and he prayed the two prayers, each prayer by itself with an adhān and an iqāmah, with the supper between them, and he prayed the Fajr when the dawn shone, or he said: when one said: “The dawn has risen,” and another said: “It has not risen.” Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed these two prayers are shifted from their time in this place; the people are not to arrive at Jamʿ until they have entered the late part of the night, and the Fajr prayer is at this hour.”
items.ma-3970: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam and Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, they said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had me recite: {Indeed it is I who am the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm.}
items.ma-3971: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh, regarding the saying of Allah ﷿: {The heart did not lie [about] what it saw} [al-Najm: 11], he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw Jibrīl in a ḥullah of rafraf, filling what is between the heaven and the earth.
items.ma-3972: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam and Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, they said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from his father and ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah used to say the takbīr at every bowing and prostration, and rising and lowering, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, riḍwān Allāh ʿalayhimā, [did likewise], and they would give the salutation to their right and their left: “Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah.”
items.ma-3973: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam and Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, they said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ and Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “Which deeds are best?” He said: “The prayer at its time, kindness to parents, and jihād in the way of Allah.” And had I asked for more, he would have given me more. Ḥusayn said: and had I asked him for more.
items.ma-3974: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs narrated to us, he dictated it to me from his book, from ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, ʿAlqamah narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught us the prayer. He said the takbīr and raised his hands, then bowed and joined his hands together, placing them between his knees. That reached Saʿd, who said: “My brother has spoken the truth; we used to do that, then we were commanded with this,” and he took hold of his knees. ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb narrated to me … thus.
