items.ma-3975: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed a prayer — I do not know whether he added or reduced — then gave the salutation and performed two prostrations.
items.ma-3976: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn, from Kathīr ibn Mudrik, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh, that he recited the talbiyah on the night of Jamʿ, then said: Here I saw the one upon whom Sūrat al-Baqarah was revealed reciting the talbiyah.
items.ma-3977: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Jābir al-Taymī, from Abū al-Mājid, he said: A man came to ʿAbd Allāh, and he mentioned the account, and he began narrating from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: Indeed the first man whose hand was cut off in Islam — or among the Muslims — was a man who was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and it was said: “O Messenger of Allah, this man stole.” It was as though ashes had been blown into the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Some of them said: “O Messenger of Allah, [it is as if] you are saying: What is wrong with you?” He said: “And what prevents me, when you are the helpers of Shayṭān against your companion? And Allah ﷿ is Pardoning, He loves pardoning, and it is not fitting for the one in charge of a matter, when a ḥadd is brought to him, except that he carries it out.” Then he recited: {And let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.} [al-Nūr: 22]. Yaḥyā said: Sufyān dictated it to us, dictating.
items.ma-3978: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Yaḥyā al-Jābir, from Abū al-Mājid al-Ḥanafī, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We asked our Prophet ﷺ about walking with the funeral procession, and he said: “Walking is [at a pace] below the khabab. If it is good, it is hastened to; and if it is other than that, then away with the people of the Fire. The funeral is followed; he is not of us who goes ahead of it.”
items.ma-3979: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I have seen us when the prayer was not established until the rows were complete for us. So whoever it pleases to meet Allah ﷿ tomorrow as a Muslim, let him be diligent in these prescribed prayers wherever they are called, for they are among the practices of guidance, and Allah ﷿ has legislated for your Prophet ﷺ the practices of guidance.
items.ma-3980: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Wakīʿ narrated to us, from his father, from Abū Isḥāq, from Maʿdīkarib, he said: We came to ʿAbd Allāh and asked him to recite to us {Ṭā Sīn Mīm} of the two hundred. He said: “I do not have it with me, but you should go to the one who took it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt.” He said: So we came to Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt, and he recited it to us.
items.ma-3981: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Abū Bakr narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had me recite a sūrah from the thirties, from Āl Ḥā Mīm — he said: meaning al-Aḥqāf. He said: A sūrah that had more than thirty verses was called one of the thirties. He said: I went to the mosque, and there was a man reciting it differently from how he had me recite it. I said: “Who had you recite?” He said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” He said: I said to another: “Recite it,” and he recited it differently from my recitation and the recitation of my companion. So I went with them to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, these two differ from me in the recitation?” He said: He became angry, and his face changed colour, and he said: “Only disagreement destroyed those before you.” He said: Zirr said: And with him was a man. He said: The man said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commands you that each man among you recite as he was taught, for only disagreement destroyed those before you.” ʿAbd Allāh said: I do not know whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had confided something to him, or whether he knew what was in the soul of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: And the man was ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, ṣalawāt Allāh ʿalayhi.
items.ma-3982: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Bashīr Abū Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Sayyār Abū al-Ḥakam, from Ṭāriq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said to him: “O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, a man greeted you with salām, and you said: ‘Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth’?” He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Before the Hour there will be greeting restricted to particular people, and trade will spread, until the woman helps her husband in trade, and the ties of kinship will be cut.”
items.ma-3983: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Nahshalī narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed five [rakʿahs], the Ẓuhr or the ʿAṣr. When he finished, it was said to him: “O Messenger of Allah, has something been added to the prayer?” He said: “No.” They said: “But you prayed five?” He said: Then he performed the two prostrations of forgetfulness, then said: “I am only a human being; I remember as you remember, and I forget as you forget.”
items.ma-3984: Asbāṭ narrated to us, he said: al-Shaybānī narrated to us, from al-Musayyab ibn Rāfiʿ, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever kills a snake has seven good deeds, whoever kills a gecko has one good deed, and whoever leaves a snake out of fear of its consequence is not of us.”
items.ma-3985: Asbāṭ narrated to us, Ashʿath narrated to us, from Kurdūs, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The assembly of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while with him were Khabbāb, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl and ʿAmmār. They said: “O Muḥammad, are you content with these?” So the Qurʾān was revealed concerning them: {And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered to their Rabb}, up to His saying: {And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers} [al-Anʿām: 51–58].
items.ma-3986: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Qays, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We used to fight with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we had no women. So we said: “O Messenger of Allah, should we not castrate ourselves?” He forbade us from it. Then afterwards we were permitted to marry a woman for a garment for a fixed term. Then ʿAbd Allāh recited: {O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors.} [al-Māʾidah: 87].
items.ma-3987: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that he said: We conversed one night with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until we had prolonged the conversation, then we returned to our families. When morning came, we went early to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “The prophets were presented to me with their nations, and their followers from their nations. A prophet would pass with three of his nation, and a prophet with a small band of his nation, and a prophet with a group of his nation, and a prophet with one man of his nation, and a prophet with none of his nation with him, until Mūsā ibn ʿImrān ﷺ passed by me in a great throng of Banū Isrāʾīl. When I saw them, they impressed me. I said: ‘O Rabb, who are these?’ He said: ‘This is your brother Mūsā ibn ʿImrān and those with him of Banū Isrāʾīl.’ I said: ‘O Rabb, then where is my ummah?’ He said: ‘Look to your right,’ and behold, the hills, the hills of Makkah, were blocked with the faces of men. I said: ‘Who are these, O Rabb?’ He said: ‘Your ummah.’ I said: ‘I am pleased, Rabb.’ He said: ‘Are you pleased?’ I said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Look to your left.’ He said: So I looked, and behold, the horizon was blocked with the faces of men. He said: ‘Are you pleased?’ I said: ‘I am pleased.’ It was said: ‘With these are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise; there is no reckoning for them.’” Then ʿUkkāshah ibn Miḥṣan, one of Banū Asad ibn Khuzaymah, began and said: “O Prophet of Allah, supplicate to Allah that He make me one of them.” He said: “O Allah, make him one of them.” Then another man among them began and said: “O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah that He make me one of them.” He said: “ʿUkkāshah has preceded you in it.”
items.ma-3988: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, Hishām informed us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: We conversed one night … and he mentioned its meaning. And [another narration]: He narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, that Ibn Masʿūd said: We conversed with the Prophet of Allah ﷺ one night … and he mentioned it.
items.ma-3989: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd informed us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan and al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ziyād, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: We conversed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one night until we had prolonged the conversation … and he mentioned it.
items.ma-3990: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Ḥafṣ — meaning Ibn Ghiyāth — narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the killing of a snake at Minā.
items.ma-3991: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad and Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, they said: Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from Ibn Masʿūd, that he was picking a siwāk from the arāk tree, and he had thin legs, and the wind began to blow him over, and the people laughed at him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “What are you laughing at?” They said: “O Prophet of Allah, at the thinness of his legs.” He said: “By the One in whose hand is my soul, they are heavier in the Scale than Uḥud.”
items.ma-3992: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad and ʿAffān narrated to us, the meaning [being the same], they said: Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿAffān said: ʿĀṣim informed us, from Zirr, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had me recite Sūrat al-Aḥqāf, and he had another man recite it, and he differed from me in a verse. I said to him: “Who had you recite it?” He said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” So I came to him while he was among a group and said: “O Messenger of Allah, did you not have me recite such-and-such a verse?” He said: “Yes.” He said: I said: “But this one claims that you had him recite it such-and-such [way]?” The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed. Then the man who was with him said: “Let each man among you recite as he heard, for those before you were destroyed only by disagreement.” He said: By Allah, I do not know whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him with that or he said it himself.
items.ma-3993: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Abū Bakr narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ … its meaning, and he said: He became angry and his face changed colour, and he said: “Only disagreement destroyed those before you.”
items.ma-3994: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad and ʿAffān narrated to us, they said: Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from Ibn Masʿūd: that a man of the Ahl al-Ṣuffah died, and they found two dīnārs in his cloak. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Two brandings.”
items.ma-3995: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from Ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed the women and said to them: “There is no woman among you who has three die for her except that Allah ﷿ will admit her to Paradise.” The most distinguished of them as a woman said: “O Messenger of Allah, and the one with two?” He said: “And the one with two, in Paradise.”
items.ma-3996: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Dāwūd, meaning Ibn Abī al-Furāt, narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Abū al-Aʿyan al-ʿAbdī, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ al-Jushamī, he said: While Ibn Masʿūd was delivering a sermon one day, a snake passed by, walking on the wall. He cut short his sermon, then struck it with his rod until he killed it. Then he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever kills a snake is as though he killed a polytheist man whose blood is lawful.”
items.ma-3997: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad and Rawḥ narrated to us, they said: Dāwūd ibn Abī al-Furāt narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Abū al-Aʿyan al-ʿAbdī, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ al-Jushamī, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: We asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the apes and the pigs, whether they are from the offspring of the Jews. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ never cursed a people — Rawḥ said: and transformed them — so that they would have offspring until He destroyed them. But this is a creation that already existed. When Allah ﷿ Ghaḍiba ʿalā the Jews, He transformed them and made them like them.”
items.ma-3998: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I said: “O Messenger of Allah, which deeds are most beloved to Allah ﷿?” He said: “Pray the prayer at its appointed times.” I said: “Then which?” He said: “Kindness to parents.” I said: “Then which?” He said: “Then jihād in the way of Allah.” And had I asked him for more, he would have given me more.
items.ma-3999: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Mahdī narrated to us, Wāṣil narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: “I remember the pairs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to join together: eighteen sūrahs from the Mufaṣṣal and two sūrahs from Āl Ḥā Mīm.
items.ma-4000: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Saʿīd informed us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan and al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ziyād, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: We conversed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one night until we had prolonged the conversation … and he mentioned it.
items.ma-4001: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥammād narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We were sitting in the mosque on the evening of Friday. He said: A man of the Anṣār said: “If one of us sees a man with his wife and kills him, you kill him; and if he speaks, you flog him; and if he is silent, he is silent in rage. By Allah, if I live to see the morning in good condition, I will ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” He said: So he asked him and said: “O Messenger of Allah, if one of us sees a man with his wife and kills him, you kill him; and if he speaks, you flog him; and if he is silent, he is silent in rage. O Allah, judge.” He said: Then the verse of liʿān was revealed. He said: And that man was the first to be afflicted with it.
items.ma-4002: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, he said: I saw ʿAbd Allāh throw the Jamrah from the middle of the valley. Then he said: Here — by the One other than whom there is no deity — used to stand the one upon whom Sūrat al-Baqarah was revealed.
items.ma-4003: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I prayed two rakʿahs with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and two rakʿahs with Abū Bakr, raḍiya Allāhu taʿālā ʿanhu, and two rakʿahs with ʿUmar, raḍiya Allāhu taʿālā ʿanhu.
items.ma-4004: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a cave, and {By the emissaries sent forth in succession} was revealed. He said: We were receiving it from his mouth, when a snake came out of its hole, so we hurried to it, but it got ahead of us and entered its hole. He said: “It was protected from your evil, and you were protected from its evil.”
items.ma-4005: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh … the like of it. He said: And we were receiving it from his mouth fresh.
items.ma-4006: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥurr narrated to us, he said: al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah narrated to me, he said: ʿAlqamah took me by my hand and narrated to me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd took him by his hand, and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took ʿAbd Allāh by his hand and taught him the tashahhud in the prayer. He said: “Say: ‘All greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah’ — Zuhayr said: I memorised it from him, if Allah wills — ‘I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.’” He said: “When you have completed this” — or he said: “When you have done this — you have completed your prayer. If you wish to stand, stand, and if you wish to sit, sit.”
items.ma-4007: Abū Dāwūd — meaning al-Ṭayālisī — narrated to us, he said: Zuhayr narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said to a people who stayed away from the Friday prayer: “I had intended to order a man to lead the people in prayer, then burn down the houses of men who stay away from the Friday prayer.”
items.ma-4008: Umayyah ibn Khālid narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, Allah ﷿ has killed Abū Jahl.” He said: “Praise be to Allah, who gave victory to His servant and gave honour to His religion.”
items.ma-4009: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā and Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, they said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: We were on the expedition of Badr, every three of us on one camel. ʿAlī and Abū Lubābah were the riding companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When it was the turn of the Prophet ﷺ, they said: “Ride, O Messenger of Allah, so that we walk in your place.” He would say: “You two are not stronger than I at walking, and I am not in less need of the reward than you.”
items.ma-4010: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, he said: ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah informed us … and he mentioned it with its meaning and its chain of narration.
items.ma-4011: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Mālik ibn Mighwal narrated to us, from al-Zubayr ibn ʿAdī, from Ṭalḥah, from Murrah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken on the night journey, he was brought to Sidrat al-Muntahā, which is in the sixth heaven. To it ends what is raised up from the earth — and once he said: what is made to ascend from the earth — and is taken from it; and to it ends what is sent down from above it, and is taken from it. {When there covered the Lote Tree that which covered} [al-Najm: 16]. He said: Moths of gold. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was given three things: the five prayers, the closing verses of Sūrat al-Baqarah, and the muqḥimāt were forgiven for those of his ummah who do not associate anything with Allah ﷿.
items.ma-4012: Kathīr ibn Hishām narrated to us, he said: Furāt narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Ziyād ibn al-Jarrāḥ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿqil, he said: My father was with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and heard him say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Regret is repentance.”
items.ma-4013: Kathīr narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from Abū ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we were held back from the Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr, Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers, and that was hard on me. Then I said: “We are with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and in the way of Allah.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered Bilāl, and he called the iqāmah for the prayer, and [the Prophet] led us in the Ẓuhr. Then he called the iqāmah and led us in the ʿAṣr. Then he called the iqāmah and led us in the Maghrib. Then he called the iqāmah and led us in the ʿIshāʾ. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went around among us and said: “There is no group on the earth remembering Allah ﷿ other than you.”
items.ma-4014: Muʿammar ibn Sulaymān al-Raqqī narrated to us, he said: Khuṣayf narrated to us, from Ziyād ibn Abī Maryam, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿqil, he said: My father was with Ibn Masʿūd and heard him say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Regret is repentance.”
items.ma-4015: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Ḥaṣīn, from Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb, from Masrūq, he said: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us one day and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said — he said: and he trembled until his garments trembled — then he said: like this, or similar to this.
items.ma-4016: Maʿmar ibn Sulaymān al-Raqqī narrated to us, Khuṣayf narrated to us, from Ziyād ibn Abī Maryam, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿqil, he said: My father was with Ibn Masʿūd and heard him say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “Regret is repentance.”
items.ma-4017: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Aʿmash, Manṣūr, Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Abū Hāshim and Ḥammād, from Abū Wāʾil, and from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ and al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We did not know what to say in the prayer; we would say: “Peace be upon Allah, peace be upon Jibrīl, peace be upon Mīkāʾīl.” He said: So the Prophet ﷺ taught us and said: “Indeed Allah is al-Salām. So when you sit after two rakʿahs, say: ‘All greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah’” — Abū Wāʾil said in his narration from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ: “When you say it, it reaches every righteous servant in the heaven and on the earth” — and Abū Isḥāq said in the narration of ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ: “When you say it, it reaches every angel brought near, or sent prophet, or righteous servant — ‘I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.’”
items.ma-4018: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Abū Isḥāq al-Shaybānī, from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ and passed by a colony of ants, which was burned. The Prophet ﷺ said: “It is not fitting for a human being to punish with the punishment of Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-4019: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Manṣūr and al-Aʿmash, from Dharr, from Wāʾil ibn Mahānah, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Prophet ﷺ addressed us and said: “Give ṣadaqah, O company of women, for you are the majority of the people of Jahannam on the Day of Resurrection.” A woman who was not of the distinguished women stood up and said: “O Messenger of Allah, why are we the majority of the people of Jahannam?” He said: “Because you curse much and are ungrateful to the companion.”
items.ma-4020: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from Ibn Masʿūd, attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Keep watch over the Qurʾān, for it escapes more readily from the hearts of men than camels from their hobbles. How evil it is for one of them to say: ‘I have forgotten such-and-such verse,’ rather he was made to forget.”
items.ma-4021: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: A group came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, a companion of ours is ill. Should we cauterise him?” He was silent for a while, then said: “If you wish, cauterise him, and if you wish, apply heated stones to him.”
items.ma-4022: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: And I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed a servant keeps lying until he is recorded with Allah as a liar, or keeps being truthful until he is recorded with Allah as a ṣiddīq.”
items.ma-4023: Yaʿlā ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿUmārah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, young men who had nothing. He said: “O company of young men, whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry, for it lowers the gaze more and protects the private part more; and whoever is not able, let him fast, for fasting is a restraint for him.”
items.ma-4024: Yaʿlā and Ibn Abī Zāʾidah narrated to us, they said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿUmārah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, he said: al-Ashʿath ibn Qays entered upon ʿAbd Allāh on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ while he was having his morning meal. He said: “O Abū Muḥammad, come near to the meal.” He said: “Is today not ʿĀshūrāʾ?” He said: “And do you know what the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ is? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used only to fast it before Ramaḍān was revealed; when Ramaḍān was revealed, it was left.”
items.ma-4025: Yaʿlā narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, he said: We were sitting with ʿAbd Allāh, and with us was Zayd ibn Ḥudayr, when Khabbāb entered upon us and said: “O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, do all of these recite as you recite?” He said: “If you wish, I will order one of them and he will recite to you.” He said: “Yes.” He said to me: “Recite.” Ibn Ḥudayr said: “You order him to recite, and he is not the best reciter among us!” He said: “By Allah, if you wish I will tell you what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to your people and his people.” He said: So I recited fifty verses of Maryam. Khabbāb said: “You have done well.” ʿAbd Allāh said: “I do not recite anything except that he recites it.” Then ʿAbd Allāh said to Khabbāb: “Is it not time for this ring to be thrown away?” He said: “You will not see it on me after today,” and the ring was of gold.
items.ma-4026: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from al-Rukayn, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh — he attributed it to [the Prophet] for us the first time, then held back from it, meaning Sharīk — he said: “Ribā, even if it increases, its end is toward scarcity.”
items.ma-4027: Abū Kāmil and Yazīd narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī informed us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbdah al-Nahdī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah has not forbidden a sacred thing except that He knew that someone among you would look into it. Beware, I am holding on to your waists lest you fall into the Fire as moths and flies fall.” Yazīd said: “moths, or flies.”
items.ma-4028: Rawḥ narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, he said: Abū al-Mughīrah informed us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbdah al-Nahdī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, and he mentioned the ḥadīth, and said: “moths and flies.”
items.ma-4029: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from Ibn Masʿūd: that the riding companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Badr were ʿAlī and Abū Lubābah. When the turn of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, they said: “Ride, O Messenger of Allah, so that we walk in your place.” He would say: “You two are not stronger than I, nor am I in less need of the reward than you.”
items.ma-4030: Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, Hārūn ibn ʿAntarah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, he said: ʿAlqamah and al-Aswad asked permission to enter upon ʿAbd Allāh. He said: “There will soon be rulers over you who will be occupied away from the time of the prayer, so pray it at its time.” Then he stood and prayed between me and him, then said: “Thus I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
items.ma-4031: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: When this verse was revealed: {Those who have believed and did not mix their belief with wrongdoing} [al-Anʿām: 82], they said: “O Messenger of Allah, which of us does not wrong himself?” He said: “It is not that; it is shirk. Have you not heard what Luqmān said to his son: {Do not associate anything with Allah; indeed shirk is a great wrong} [Luqmān: 13]?”
items.ma-4032: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer, and either he added or he reduced — Ibrāhīm said: the forgetting of that came only from my side — so we said: “O Messenger of Allah, has something happened in the prayer?” He said: “What is that?” We said: “You prayed such-and-such before.” He said: “I am only a human being; I forget as you forget. So when one of you forgets, let him perform two prostrations.” Then he turned and performed two prostrations.
items.ma-4033: Ibn Numayr and Yaʿlā narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, he said: ʿAbd Allāh came to al-Shām, and some people of Ḥimṣ said to him: “Recite to us.” So he recited Sūrat Yūsuf to them. A man among the people stood up and said: “By Allah, it was not revealed like this!” ʿAbd Allāh said: “Woe to you! I recited it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in this way, and he said: ‘You have done well.’” While he was disputing with him, he found the smell of wine on him and said: “Do you drink the filth and deny the Qurʾān? By Allah, you will not deal with me until I flog you.” So he flogged him the ḥadd.
items.ma-4034: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, al-Aʿmash informed us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said — when he saw ʿUthmān pray four rakʿahs at Minā: I prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ two rakʿahs, and behind Abū Bakr two rakʿahs, and behind ʿUmar two rakʿahs. Would that my share of four were two accepted rakʿahs.
items.ma-4035: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, al-Aʿmash informed us, from ʿUmārah ibn ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, he said: We entered upon ʿAbd Allāh, and with him were ʿAlqamah and al-Aswad, and he narrated a ḥadīth. I think he narrated it only for my sake, for I was the youngest of the people in age. He said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, young men who could find nothing. He said: “O company of young men, whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry, for it lowers the gaze more and protects the private part more; and whoever is not able, let him fast, for it is a restraint for him.”
items.ma-4036: Yaʿlā narrated to us, ʿUmar ibn Dharr narrated to us, from al-ʿAyzār, from Tinʿah, that Ibn Masʿūd said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “When a curse is directed, it goes toward the one to whom it was directed. If it finds an opening in him and finds a way against him, it settles on him; and if not, it turns back to its Rabb and says: ‘O Rabb, so-and-so directed me to so-and-so, and I found no way against him and found no opening in him, so what do You command me?’ He says: ‘Return from where you came.’”
items.ma-4037: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Dharr, from Wāʾil ibn Mahānah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O company of women, give ṣadaqah, even from your jewellery, for you are the majority of the people of Jahannam on the Day of Resurrection.” He said: A woman who was not of the distinguished women stood up and said: “Why are we the majority of the people of Jahannam on the Day of Resurrection?” He said: He said: “Indeed you curse much and are ungrateful to the companion.”
items.ma-4038: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said one statement and I said another. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever dies not associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise.” He said: And I said: Whoever dies associating something with Allah will enter the Fire.
items.ma-4039: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When you are three, two are not to converse privately apart from their companion, for that grieves him.”
items.ma-4041: Abū Muʿāwiyah and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, they said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, he said: We were sitting at the door of ʿAbd Allāh, waiting for him to permit us. He said: Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Nakhaʿī came and entered upon him, and we said to him: “Let him know of our place.” He entered and informed him, and it was not long before he came out to us and said: “I know of your place, but I leave you deliberately, for fear that I would weary you. Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give us admonition at intervals during the days, for fear of boredom on our account.”
items.ma-4042: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I am your forerunner at the Ḥawḍ, and I will be contended over with some people, then I will be overcome concerning them. I will say: ‘O Rabb, my companions!’ It will be said: ‘You do not know what they innovated after you.’”
items.ma-4043:
Ibn Numayr narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said one statement and I said another. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever dies while associating something with Allah will enter the Fire.” And I said: Whoever dies while not associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise.
And Abū Bakr agreed with him, from ʿĀṣim, contrary to Abū Muʿāwiyah; Aswad narrated it to us.
items.ma-4044: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no one more Aghyar than Allah ﷿, and for that reason He forbade the indecencies; and there is no one to whom praise is more Aḥabb ilayhi than Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-4045: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, he said: ʿAlqamah and I entered upon ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, and he said: When one of you bows, let him spread his forearms over his thighs. It is as though I am looking at the spreading of the fingers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the prayer.
items.ma-4046: Abū Muʿāwiyah and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, they said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿUmārah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray a prayer except at its time, except two prayers: the Maghrib prayer and the ʿIshāʾ prayer at Jamʿ. And he prayed the Fajr that day before its time. Ibn Numayr said: the two ʿIshāʾ prayers, for he prayed the two of them together at Jamʿ.
items.ma-4047: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿUmārah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I was concealed by the coverings of the Kaʿbah. He said: Three men came, with much fat in their bellies and little understanding in their hearts: a Qurashī and his two in-laws, Thaqafīs, or a Thaqafī and his two in-laws, Qurashīs. They spoke words that I did not understand. One of them said: “Do you think that Allah ﷿ Yasmaʿu this speech of ours?” Another said: “I think that when we raise our voices, Samiʿahu, and when we do not raise our voices, lam yasmaʿhu.” He said: And another said: “If He Samiʿa some of it, He Samiʿahu all of it.” He said: I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ. He said: So Allah ﷿ revealed: {And you were not concealing yourselves lest your hearing, nor your sight, testify against you}, up to His saying: {And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Rabb; it has ruined you, so you have become among the losers} [Fuṣṣilat: 22–23].
items.ma-4048: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shimr ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Mughīrah ibn Saʿd ibn al-Akhram, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not take an estate, lest you become inclined to the world.” He said: Then ʿAbd Allāh said: “And at Rādhān, what is at Rādhān!! And at al-Madīnah, what is at al-Madīnah!!”
items.ma-4049: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever swears an oath in order to take away the property of a Muslim man will meet Allah ﷿ while He is Ghaḍbān with him.” Al-Ashʿath said: “By Allah, that was about me. There was land between me and a man of the Jews, and he denied me, so I brought him before the Prophet ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: ‘Do you have proof?’ I said: ‘No.’ He said to the Jew: ‘Swear.’ I said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, then he will swear and my property will go.’ So Allah ﷿ revealed: {Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price} … to the end of the verse [Āl ʿImrān: 77].”
items.ma-4050: Abū Muʿāwiyah and Wakīʿ narrated to us, they said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Muslim ibn Ṣubayḥ, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed among the people of the Fire most severe in punishment on the Day of Resurrection are the picture-makers.” Wakīʿ said: “most severe of people.”
items.ma-4051: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to sleep lying on his back until he breathed heavily, then he would stand and pray and not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-4052: Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad narrated it to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā narrated to us, Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Fuḍayl, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ … and he mentioned it.
items.ma-4053: Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Prophet ﷺ went out for a need of his and said: “Bring me something with which I may clean myself, and do not bring me a ḥāʾil or a rajīʿ.” Then I brought him water and he performed wuḍūʾ, then stood and prayed. He bent, and joined his hands together when he bowed, and placed them between his thighs.
items.ma-4054: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a man, asking his permission to cauterise him. He was silent. Then we asked him again, and he was silent. Then we asked him a third time, and he said: “Apply heated stones to him, if you wish,” as though he were angry.
items.ma-4055: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from ʿAlqamah and al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say the takbīr at every rising and lowering, and standing and sitting, and give the salutation to his right and to his left: “Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah,” until the side of his cheek was visible. And I saw Abū Bakr and ʿUmar do that.
items.ma-4056: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: It is not Abū ʿUbaydah who mentioned it, but ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the latrine and said: “Bring me three stones.” I searched and found two stones, and did not find the third. So I brought him two stones and a piece of dung. He took the two stones and threw away the dung, and said: “It is rikṣ.”
items.ma-4057: Bahz narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided the spoils of Ḥunayn at al-Jiʿirrānah. He said: They crowded around him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed a servant among the servants of Allah, whom Allah ﷿ sent to his people, was denied by them and they wounded his head. He began wiping the blood from his forehead and saying: ‘O Rabb, forgive my people, for they do not know.’” He said: ʿAbd Allāh said: It is as though I am looking at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiping his forehead, imitating the man.
items.ma-4058: Ibn Abī ʿAdī and Yazīd narrated to us, they said: Ibn ʿAwn informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, he said: Ibn Masʿūd said: I was not kept away from three [things] — Ibn ʿAwn said: ʿAmr forgot one, and I forgot another, and this remained — from private conversation, from such-and-such, and from such-and-such. He said: So I came to him, and with him was Mālik ibn Murārah al-Rahāwī. He said: I caught the end of his speech, and he was saying: “O Messenger of Allah, I am a man to whom has been apportioned the beauty that you see, and I would not like anyone among the people to excel me by two sandal straps or more. Is that not baghy?” He said: “That is not baghy; rather baghy is [the conduct of] one who is foolish toward the truth — or exults over the truth — and looks down on people.”
items.ma-4059: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: A man was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who had slept one night until morning. He said: “That is a man in whose ear — or ears — Shayṭān urinated.”
items.ma-4060: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, he said: ʿAbd Allāh used to give reminders every Thursday. It was said to him: “We would love it if you reminded us every day.” He said: “I dislike wearying you. Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give us admonition at intervals, disliking boredom on our account.”
items.ma-4061: Jarīr narrated to us, from Layth, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from his father, he said: I was with ʿAbd Allāh until he reached Jamrat al-ʿAqabah, and he said: “Hand me some stones.” He said: So I handed him seven stones, and he said to me: “Take the rein of the she-camel.” He said: Then he went back to it and threw seven pebbles at it from the middle of the valley while he was riding, saying the takbīr with every pebble, and said: “O Allah, make it an accepted Ḥajj and a forgiven sin.” Then he said: “Here used to stand the one upon whom Sūrat al-Baqarah was revealed.”
items.ma-4062: Hushaym narrated to us, Sayyār informed us, from Abū Wāʾil, he said: A man came to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and said: “I recited the Mufaṣṣal last night in one rakʿah.” ʿAbd Allāh said: “Scattering like the scattering of poor dates, and rapid like the rapid [recitation of] poetry? Indeed I know the similar [sūrahs] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pair, two sūrahs in one rakʿah.”
items.ma-4063: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, Manṣūr narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a cave, and {By the emissaries} was revealed to him, and we began receiving it from him. A snake came out from the side of the cave, and he said: “Kill it.” We hurried to it, but it got ahead of us, and he said: “Indeed it was protected from your evil, as you were protected from its evil.”
items.ma-4064: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq ibn Salamah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: When we sat with the Prophet ﷺ in the prayer, we used to say: “Peace be upon Allah before His servants, peace be upon Jibrīl, peace be upon Mīkāʾīl, peace be upon so-and-so, peace be upon so-and-so.” He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard us and said: “Indeed Allah is al-Salām. So when one of you sits in the prayer, let him say: ‘All greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah’ — for when he says it, it reaches every righteous servant in the heaven and the earth — ‘I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.’ Then afterwards let him choose whatever supplication he wishes.”
items.ma-4065: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The blood of a man who bears witness that there is no deity except Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah is not lawful except in one of three cases: the previously married person who commits zinā, a life for a life, and the one who abandons his religion, separating from the community.”
items.ma-4066: Muʾammal narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed there will be fitnahs and matters that you will disapprove.” They said: “O Messenger of Allah, what do you command us?” He said: “You will give the right that is upon you, and you will ask Allah ﷿ for what is yours.”
items.ma-4067: Muʾammal said: I found in another place: Sufyān narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
items.ma-4068: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash and Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the cave, and a snake came out upon us. We hurried to it, but it got ahead of us and entered the hole. The Prophet ﷺ said: “It was protected from your evil, as you were protected from its evil.” He said: And al-Aʿmash added in the ḥadīth, he said: We were receiving it from his mouth while it was fresh.
items.ma-4069: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ in a cave, and {By the emissaries sent forth in succession} had been revealed to him. He said: We were taking it from his mouth fresh, when a snake came out upon us. He said: “Kill it.” We rushed to it to kill it, but it got ahead of us. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah protected it from your evil, as He protected you from its evil.”
items.ma-4070: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Mukhāriq al-Aḥmasī, from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, he said: I heard Ibn Masʿūd say: I witnessed from al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad — another said: a scene — such that for me to be its [doer] would be more beloved to me than what is equal to it. He came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was invoking against the polytheists, and said: “We do not say to you as the people of Mūsā said: {Go, you and your Rabb, and fight; indeed we are sitting right here} [al-Māʾidah: 24], but we will fight on your right and on your left, and before you and behind you.” Then I saw the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shine, and that pleased him.
items.ma-4071: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Shuʿbah informed us, from al-Suddī, that he heard Murrah, that he heard ʿAbd Allāh — Shuʿbah said to me: he attributed it [to the Prophet], but I do not attribute it for you — say regarding the saying of Allah ﷿: {And whoever intends in it deviation [by] wrongdoing} [al-Ḥajj: 25], he said: If a man were to intend deviation in it while he was at ʿAdan Abyan, Allah ﷿ would make him taste a painful punishment.
items.ma-4072: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, Jābir narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the Ẓuhr or the ʿAṣr [with] five [rakʿahs], then performed two prostrations and said: “These two prostrations are for whoever among you thinks that he has added or reduced.”
items.ma-4073: Hushaym narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from Abū Qays, from Huzayl ibn Shuraḥbīl, that al-Ashʿarī was brought a case concerning a daughter, a son’s daughter, and a full sister. He said: So he made for the daughter the half, and for the sister what remained, and he made nothing for the son’s daughter. He said: They came to Ibn Masʿūd and informed him. He said: “Then I would have gone astray and I would not be among the guided, if I took his saying and left the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” He said: Then Ibn Masʿūd said: “For the daughter the half, for the son’s daughter the sixth, and what remains for the sister.”
items.ma-4074: ʿAbd al-Quddūs ibn Bakr ibn Khunays narrated to us, from Misʿar, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: It was as though the sitting of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the two rakʿahs was upon heated stones.
items.ma-4075: Muḥammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Khuṣayf, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from his father ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “When you are in the prayer and you doubt between three and four, and most of your thought is toward four, you say the tashahhud, then perform two prostrations while you are sitting before you give the salutation, then say the tashahhud again, then give the salutation.”
items.ma-4076: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, Khuṣayf narrated to us, Abū ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: If you doubt in your prayer while you are sitting, and do not know whether you have prayed three or four, then if most of your thought is that you have prayed three, stand and bow one rakʿah, then give the salutation, then perform two prostrations, then say the tashahhud, then give the salutation. And if most of your thought is that you have prayed four, give the salutation, then perform two prostrations, then say the tashahhud, then give the salutation.
items.ma-4077: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd narrated to us, he said: al-ʿAwwām informed us, Abū Muḥammad, a mawlā of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, narrated to us, from Abū ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever sends ahead three who have not reached the age of ḥinth, they will be for him a strong fortress against the Fire.” Abū al-Dardāʾ said: “I have sent ahead two?” He said: “And two.” Ubayy ibn Kaʿb Abū al-Mundhir, the master of the reciters, said: “I have sent ahead one?” He said: “And one, but that is at the first shock.”
items.ma-4078: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: al-ʿAwwām informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Muḥammad, a mawlā of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from Abū ʿUbaydah, and he mentioned its meaning, except that he said: Abū Dharr said: “I have not sent ahead except two.” And thus Yazīd also narrated it to us, he said: Abū Dharr said: “Two of mine have passed.”
items.ma-4079: Muḥammad and Yazīd narrated to us, they said: al-ʿAwwām narrated to us, he said: Abū Muḥammad, the mawlā of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, narrated to me, from Abū ʿUbaydah. The two differed from Hushaym, and said: Abū Muḥammad, the mawlā of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
items.ma-4080: Hushaym narrated to us, Khālid informed us, from Ibn Sīrīn, that Anas ibn Mālik attended the funeral of a man of the Anṣār. He said: They made the seeking of forgiveness openly heard, and Anas did not object to that. Hushaym said: Khālid said in his narration: and they put him into the grave from the side of the foot of the grave. And Hushaym once said: A man of the Anṣār died in al-Baṣrah, and Anas ibn Mālik attended him, and they made the seeking of forgiveness for him openly heard.
items.ma-4081: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, Khālid narrated to us, from Muḥammad, he said: I was with Anas at a funeral, and he ordered [that] the dead [body] be drawn out, so it was drawn in from the side of the foot of the grave.
items.ma-4082: Abū Dāwūd narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Anas ibn Sīrīn, he said: Anas was the best of people in prayer, in travel and in residence.
items.ma-4083: Hushaym narrated to us, Khālid informed us, from Anas ibn Sīrīn, he said: I saw Anas ibn Mālik stretching up toward something while he was in the prayer, looking at it.
items.ma-4084: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, ʿUmārah narrated to me, al-Aswad ibn Yazīd narrated to me, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said. And Abū Muʿāwiyah: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿUmārah. And Ibn Jaʿfar: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, he said: I heard ʿUmārah, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, the meaning [being the same]. He said: Let none of you give Shayṭān a share of himself, thinking only that it is obligatory upon him to turn away to his right. I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, most of his turning away being to his left.
items.ma-4085: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Sufyān, and Shuʿbah, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ: “How evil it is for one of you to say: ‘I have forgotten such-and-such verse,’ rather he was made to forget.”
items.ma-4086: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, Manṣūr and Sulaymān narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: A man said: “O Messenger of Allah, will we be held to account for what we did in the Jāhiliyyah?” He said: “If you do good, you will not be held to account; and if you do wrong in Islam, you will be taken for the first and the last.”
items.ma-4087: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Sufyān, Manṣūr and Sulaymān narrated to me, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh: that a Jew came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “O Muḥammad, indeed Allah Yumsiku the heavens ʿalā iṣbaʿ, and the earths ʿalā iṣbaʿ, and the mountains ʿalā iṣbaʿ, and the creatures ʿalā iṣbaʿ, and the trees ʿalā iṣbaʿ. Then He says: ‘I am the Malik.’” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed until his molars appeared, and said: {They have not appraised Allah with true appraisal} [al-Zumar: 67]. Yaḥyā said: Fuḍayl — meaning Ibn ʿIyāḍ — said: in wonder and in affirmation of him.
items.ma-4088: Yaḥyā and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from his father, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Every prophet has allies from among the prophets, and my ally among them is my father and the khalīl of my Rabb ﷿.” Then he recited: {Indeed the people most worthy of Ibrāhīm are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who have believed} [Āl ʿImrān: 68].
items.ma-4089: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from al-Masʿūdī, Jāmiʿ ibn Shaddād narrated to me, he said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd say: I saw ʿAbd Allāh go down into the middle of the valley, placing the Jamrah at his right eyebrow and facing the House. Then he threw seven pebbles at it, saying the takbīr after each pebble. Then he said: This, by the One other than whom there is no deity, is the standing place of the one upon whom Sūrat al-Baqarah was revealed.
items.ma-4090: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd and Wakīʿ narrated to us, they said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, the meaning [being the same], from al-Aʿmash, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah narrated to me, from al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd Allāh, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: The one who consumes ribā, the one who feeds it, its two witnesses and its writer, when they know of it, and the woman who tattoos and the woman who has herself tattooed for beauty, and the one who withholds ṣadaqah, and the one who reverts to being a Bedouin after his hijrah, are cursed upon the tongue of Muḥammad ﷺ on the Day of Resurrection.
items.ma-4091: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, and Wakīʿ: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, he said: Zayd ibn Wahb narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to us, and he is the truthful, the one who is believed: “Indeed the creation of one of you is gathered in his mother’s womb in forty days — or he said: forty nights; Wakīʿ said: nights — then he is a clinging clot for the like of that, then a chewed lump for the like of that. Then Allah ﷿ sends the angel to him with four words: his deed, his term, his provision, and wretched or happy. Then the soul is breathed into him. By the One other than whom there is no deity, one of you will do the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is nothing between him and it except a cubit, then the Book precedes him and he is sealed with the deeds of the people of the Fire, so he is of its people. And one of you will do the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is nothing between him and it except a cubit, then the Book precedes him and he is sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise, so he is of its people.”
items.ma-4092: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, Sulaymān narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “No soul is killed unjustly except that upon the son of Ādam is a share of its blood, because he was the first to establish killing.”
items.ma-4093: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ: “When they are three, two are not to converse privately apart from their companion, for that grieves him.”
items.ma-4094: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from al-Taymī, from Abū ʿUthmān, from Ibn Masʿūd: that a man had kissed a woman and came to the Prophet ﷺ asking him about its kaffārah. So Allah ﷿ revealed: {Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with bad deeds} [Hūd: 114]. He said: “O Messenger of Allah, is this for me?” He said: “For whoever of my ummah does it.”
items.ma-4095: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to me, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Indeed Muḥammad ﷺ narrated to us that a man keeps lying until he is recorded with Allah as a liar, and that a man keeps being truthful until he is recorded with Allah as a ṣiddīq.
items.ma-4096: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from al-Taymī, from Abū ʿUthmān, from Ibn Masʿūd: Whoever buys a muḥaffalah — and perhaps he said: a muḥaffalah sheep — let him return it and return with it a ṣāʿ. And the Prophet ﷺ forbade the meeting of [incoming] trade.
items.ma-4097: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Mujālid, ʿĀmir narrated to us, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said once or twice, from the Prophet ﷺ: “There is no judge who judges between people except that he is held on the Day of Resurrection, with an angel holding him by the nape of his neck, until he makes him stand over Jahannam. Then he raises his head to Allah ﷿; if he says: ‘The error,’ he throws him into Jahannam, falling for forty autumns.”
items.ma-4098: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, ʿĀṣim narrated to me, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “The world will not go away — or: the world will not come to an end — until a man from my household rules the Arabs, whose name matches my name.”
items.ma-4099: I read to Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Hishām, Qatādah narrated to us, from Khilās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd was approached and asked about a man who had married a woman without specifying a ṣadāq for her, and then died before consummating with her. He did not say anything about it, so they went back, then came to him again and asked him. He said: “I will give my opinion about it with the utmost effort of my judgement; if I am correct, then Allah ﷿ granted me success in that, and if I am mistaken, then it is from me: she has the ṣadāq of her women, and she has the inheritance, and upon her is the ʿiddah.” A man from Ashjaʿ stood up and said: “I bear witness regarding the Prophet ﷺ that he judged that.” He said: “Come, who will bear witness for you to that?” So Abū al-Jarrāḥ bore witness to that.
items.ma-4100: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, the meaning [being the same], except that he said: concerning Barwaʿ bint Wāshiq. And he said: “Come, [bring] your two witnesses to this.” So Abū Sinān and al-Jarrāḥ, two men of Ashjaʿ, bore witness.
items.ma-4101: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, Shaqīq narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: When we sat with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the prayer, we used to say: “Peace be upon Allah from His servants, peace be upon so-and-so and so-and-so.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not say: ‘Peace be upon Allah,’ for Allah is al-Salām. But when one of you sits, let him say: ‘All greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah’ — for when you say that, it reaches every righteous servant between the heaven and the earth — ‘I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.’ Then let each of you choose the supplication that pleases him most, and let him supplicate with it.”
items.ma-4102: Wakīʿ and Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, the meaning [being the same], they said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “Which sin is greatest?” He said: “That you make a peer for Allah while He created you.” He said: “Then which?” He said: “Then that you kill your child out of fear that he will eat with you.” He said: “Then which?” He said: “Then that you commit zinā with the wife of your neighbour.” He said: Then Allah ﷿ revealed the confirmation of that in His Book: {And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity}, up to His saying: {and whoever does that will meet a penalty} [al-Furqān: 68].
items.ma-4103: Wakīʿ and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, they said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We said: “O Messenger of Allah.” And Ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, he said: I heard Abū Wāʾil narrating from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We said: “O Messenger of Allah, will we be held to account for what we did in the Jāhiliyyah?” He said: “Whoever does good in Islam will not be held to account for what he did in the Jāhiliyyah, and whoever does wrong in Islam will be taken for the first and the last.”
items.ma-4104:
Wakīʿ and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, the meaning [being the same], they said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, he said: While a man was speaking in the Great Mosque, he said: “When it is the Day of Resurrection, a smoke will come down from the heaven and seize the hearing and the sight of the hypocrites, and it will seize the believers like the condition of a cold.”
Masrūq said: So I entered upon ʿAbd Allāh and mentioned that to him. He was reclining, so he sat upright and began to speak, saying: “O people, whoever among you is asked about knowledge that he has, let him speak of it; and if he does not have it, let him say: ‘Allah knows best,’ for it is part of knowledge that you say about what you do not know: ‘Allah knows best.’ Indeed Allah ﷿ said to His Prophet ﷺ: {Say: I do not ask you for any payment for it, and I am not of the pretentious} [Ṣād: 86]. Indeed when Quraysh overcame the Prophet ﷺ and stubbornly disobeyed him, he said: ‘O Allah, help me against them with seven [years] like the seven of Yūsuf.’ So a year seized them in which they ate bones and carrion because of hardship, until one of them would see between himself and the heaven something like the appearance of smoke because of hunger. They said: {Our Rabb, remove from us the punishment; indeed we are believers}. It was said to him: ‘If We remove it from them, they will return.’ So he supplicated his Rabb, and He removed it from them, but they returned, so Intaqama Allāh minhum on the day of Badr. That is His saying, the Exalted: {So watch for the Day when the heaven will bring a visible smoke}, up to His saying: {the Day We seize with the greatest seizure; indeed We are Muntaqimūn} [al-Dukhān: 10–16].” Ibn Numayr said in his narration: ʿAbd Allāh said: “Had it been the Day of Resurrection, He would not have removed it from them.”
items.ma-4105: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Aswad ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I recited to the Prophet ﷺ: {So is there any who will take heed?} with dhāl, and the Prophet ﷺ said: {So is there any who will take heed?} with dāl [al-Qamar].
items.ma-4106: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When you are three, two are not to converse privately apart from one, for that grieves him.”
items.ma-4108: Wakīʿ and Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, they said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Beware of lying, for lying guides to wickedness, and wickedness guides to the Fire, and a man keeps lying until he is recorded with Allah as a liar.” And he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Hold to truthfulness, for truthfulness guides to righteousness, and righteousness guides to Paradise, and he — meaning the man — keeps being truthful and strives for truthfulness until he is recorded with Allah as a ṣiddīq.” Abū Muʿāwiyah said: “A man does not cease to be truthful and to strive for truthfulness.”
items.ma-4109: Wakīʿ and Yazīd narrated to us, Ismāʿīl informed us, from Qays, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no envy except in two: a man whom Allah gave wealth and empowered him to spend it away in the right, and another whom Allah gave wisdom, so he judges by it and teaches it.”
items.ma-4110: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Ḥasan narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥārith, from Abū Mājid al-Ḥanafī, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: We asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about walking with the funeral procession. He said: “[At a pace] below the khabab. The funeral is followed and is not a follower.”
items.ma-4111: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He is not of us who tears the collars, strikes the cheeks, and calls with the call of the Jāhiliyyah.”
items.ma-4112: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿUmārah ibn ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: “O company of young men, whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry, for it lowers the gaze more and protects the private part more; and whoever is not able, let him fast, for it is a restraint for him.”
items.ma-4113: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Khālid, from Qays, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ, and we were young men. We said: “O Messenger of Allah, should we not castrate ourselves?” He forbade us, then permitted us to marry a woman for a garment for a fixed term. Then ʿAbd Allāh recited: {Do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you} [al-Māʾidah: 87].
items.ma-4114: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah narrated to us, from Abū Mūsā al-Hilālī, from his father, that a man was on a journey and his wife gave birth, and her milk was held back. So he began to suck it and spit it out, and it entered his throat. He came to Abū Mūsā, who said: “She has become forbidden to you.” He said: So he came to Ibn Masʿūd and asked him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Nothing is made forbidden by suckling except what makes flesh grow and bone develop.”
items.ma-4115: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, that he said in the sermon of need: Indeed all praise is for Allah; we seek His help and we seek His forgiveness, and we seek refuge with Allah from the evils of ourselves. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead him astray, and whomever He leads astray, none can guide him. I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. Then he recited three verses from the Book of Allah: {Fear Allah as He should be feared, and do not die except as Muslims} [Āl ʿImrān: 102], {Fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs; indeed Allah is ever, over you, a Raqīb} [al-Nisāʾ: 1], {Fear Allah and speak a straight word} up to the end of the verse [al-Aḥzāb: 70].
items.ma-4116: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ and Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught us the sermon of need … and he mentioned the like of this ḥadīth, except that he did not say: “Indeed.”
items.ma-4117: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from Jāmiʿ ibn Shaddād Abū Ṣakhrah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, he said: When ʿAbd Allāh came to the Jamrah — Jamrat al-ʿAqabah — he went down into the middle of the valley, faced the Kaʿbah, and placed the Jamrah at his right eyebrow. Then he threw seven pebbles, saying the takbīr with every pebble. Then he said: From here, by the One other than whom there is no deity, threw the one upon whom Sūrat al-Baqarah was revealed.
items.ma-4118: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “Recite the Qurʾān to me.” I said: “O Messenger of Allah, how can I recite to you when it was revealed to you?” He said: “I desire to hear it from someone other than myself.” He said: So I began Sūrat al-Nisāʾ and recited to him, and when I reached: {So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you against these as a witness?} [al-Nisāʾ: 41], he said: I looked at him, and his eyes were shedding tears.
items.ma-4119:
Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Misʿar, from ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad, from al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Yashkurī, from al-Maʿrūr ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Umm Ḥabībah said: O Allah, let me enjoy my husband the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and my father Abū Sufyān, and my brother Muʿāwiyah. The Prophet ﷺ said: “You have asked Allah ﷿ for appointed terms, numbered days, and apportioned provisions. [He] will never hasten anything before its due time, or delay anything beyond its due time. And had you asked Allah ﷿ to protect you from a punishment in the Fire, or a punishment in the grave, it would have been better and more excellent.”
He said: It was mentioned in his presence that the apes — Misʿar said: I think he said: and the swine — are of those who were transformed. He said: So he ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ has not made for any transformed one offspring, nor descendants; and the apes — I think he said: and the swine — existed before that.”
items.ma-4120: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, al-Thawrī narrated to us, from ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad, the like of it with its isnād, and he did not doubt regarding the swine.
items.ma-4121: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, I declare myself free before every khalīl of his khullah. And if I were to take a khalīl, I would have taken Abū Bakr. Indeed your companion is the Khalīl of Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-4122: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from al-Masʿūdī, from al-Ḥakam, from Dharr, from Wāʾil ibn Mahānah al-Taymī, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “O company of women, give ṣadaqah, for you are the majority of the people of the Fire.” A woman said: Why are we the majority of the people of the Fire? He said: “Because you curse much, and you are ungrateful to the ʿashīr.”
items.ma-4123: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no soul killed unjustly except that upon the first son of Ādam is a kifl of its blood, because he was the first to set the precedent of killing.”
items.ma-4124: Wakīʿ and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, [in] meaning, and this is the wording of Wakīʿ: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, from Ziyād ibn Abī Maryam, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿqil, that his father Maʿqil ibn Muqarrin al-Muzanī said to Ibn Masʿūd: Did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Regret is repentance”? He said: Yes.
items.ma-4125: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from Jābir, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to us, and he is the truthful, the one declared truthful, he said: “The sale of the muḥaffalāt is khilābah, and khilābah is not lawful for a Muslim.”
items.ma-4126: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Zubayd, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, narrating it from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Reviling a Muslim is fusūq, and fighting him is kufr.”
items.ma-4127: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said. And Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, he said: I heard Zayd ibn Wahb say: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ: “Indeed you will see after me favouritism, and fitan, and matters that you will disapprove of.” We said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you command us, for whoever of us reaches that? He said: “You will fulfil the right that is upon you, and ask Allah for what is yours.”
items.ma-4128: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Suddī, from Murrah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: {And there is none of you except that he will come to it} [Maryam: 71], he said: They enter it, or they go into it, then they depart from it according to their deeds. I said to him: Isrāʾīl narrated it to him from the Prophet ﷺ? He said: Yes, it is from the Prophet ﷺ, or words to this meaning.
items.ma-4129:
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Allah has cursed the women who tattoo and the women who have themselves tattooed, the women who pluck [hair], and the women who create gaps [between their teeth] for beauty, those who change the creation of Allah. He said: That reached a woman in the house, who was called Umm Yaʿqūb, so she came to him and said: It has reached me that you said such and such. He said: Why should I not curse the one whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed, in the Book of Allah ﷿?! She said: I have certainly read what is between its two covers, and I did not find it. He said: If you had read it, you would have found it. Have you not read: {And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you from, abstain from it} [al-Ḥashr: 7]? She said: Yes. He said: Indeed the Prophet ﷺ forbade it. She said: I think your wife does it. He said: Go and look. So she looked, and saw nothing of what she wanted. She came and said: I saw nothing. He said: If she were like that, she would not have been joined with us.
He said: And I heard it from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀbis, narrating it from Umm Yaʿqūb, [that] he heard it from her, so I chose the narration of Manṣūr.
items.ma-4130: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbīdah, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “The best of people is my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them” — three or four [times] — “then there will come a people, the testimony of one of whom precedes his oath, and his oath his testimony.” He said: Our companions used to beat us, while we were boys, over testimony and the covenant.
items.ma-4131: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr and al-Aʿmash and Wāṣil, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest with Allah ﷿? He said: “That you make a rival for Allah ﷿ while He created you.” He said: I said: Then what? He said: “Then that you kill your child out of fear that he will eat of your food” — and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān once said: “that he will eat with you” —. He said: Then I said: Then what? He said: “That you commit zinā with the wife of your neighbour.”
items.ma-4132: Bahz ibn Asad narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Wāṣil al-Aḥdab narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū Wāʾil say: ʿAbd Allāh said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Which sin is greatest? … So he mentioned it.
items.ma-4133: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Wāṣil, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ … So he mentioned it.
items.ma-4134: ʿAlī ibn Ḥafṣ narrated to us, Warqāʾ narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest? … So he mentioned it, then he recited: {And those who do not call upon another deity along with Allah} up to: {humiliated} [al-Furqān: 68 and 69].
items.ma-4135: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to say: “O Allah, I ask You for guidance, taqwā, chastity, and sufficiency.”
items.ma-4136: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If I were to take a khalīl, I would take Ibn Abī Quḥāfah as a khalīl.”
items.ma-4137: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿUmārah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray a prayer except at its appointed time, except that he combined the Maghrib and the ʿIshāʾ at Jamʿ, and he prayed the Ṣubḥ prayer that day at other than its appointed time.
items.ma-4138: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿUmārah … its meaning.
items.ma-4139: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: That I swear nine [times] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was killed, indeed killed, is more beloved to me than that I swear once that he was not killed, and that is because Allah ʿazza wa-jalla made him a prophet and took him as a shahīd. He said: I mentioned that to Ibrāhīm, and he said: They used to think, and they used to say: The Jews poisoned him, and Abū Bakr ﵁.
items.ma-4140: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, and ʿAbd al-Razzāq: Sufyān informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: When {So glorify the praise of your Rabb and seek His forgiveness; indeed He was ever a Tawwāb} was revealed — ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: When {When the victory of Allah and the conquest comes} was revealed — the Prophet ﷺ used to say frequently: “Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me, indeed You are al-Tawwāb.”
items.ma-4141: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from al-Suddī, from Murrah, from ʿAbd Allāh: {And there is none of you except that he will come to it} [Maryam: 71], he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The people will all come to the Fire, then they will depart from it according to their deeds.”
items.ma-4142: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, and Yazīd narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd informed us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drew a line for us, then said: “This is the path of Allah,” then he drew lines on his right and on his left, then said: “These are paths — Yazīd said: scattered — on each path of which is a Shayṭān calling to it.” Then he recited: {And that this is My straight path, so follow it, and do not follow the paths, for they will scatter you away from His path} [al-Anʿām: 153].
items.ma-4143: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed among the worst of people are those whom the Hour overtakes while they are alive, and those who take graves as places of prostration.”
items.ma-4144: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The Hour will be established — or: the Hour will not be established except upon the worst of people.”
