items.ma-4145: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We used to speak during the prayer, and some of us would greet others, and one of us would charge another with a need. So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and greeted him while he was praying, and he did not return [the greeting] to me, and what was old and what was new took hold of me. When he had prayed he said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ brings about of His command what He wills, and indeed He has brought about that you do not speak during the prayer.”
items.ma-4146: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, from Abū Qatādah, from Usayr ibn Jābir, he said: A red wind arose in al-Kūfah, and a man came whose only cry was: O ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, the Hour has come!! He said: He was reclining, so he sat up and said: Indeed the Hour will not be established until no inheritance is divided and no one rejoices over booty. He said: An enemy they will gather against the people of Islam, and the people of Islam will gather against them — and he motioned with his hand towards al-Shām. I said: You mean the Romans? He said: Yes. He said: And at that fighting there will be a severe apostasy. He said: So the Muslims will stipulate a detachment for death that will not return except victorious, and they will fight until the night comes between them, then these and those will withdraw, each not victorious, and the detachment will perish. Then the Muslims will stipulate a detachment for death that will not return except victorious, and they will fight until the night comes between them, then these and those will withdraw, each not victorious, and the detachment will perish. Then the Muslims will stipulate a detachment for death that will not return except victorious, and they will fight until they reach the evening, then these and those will withdraw, each not victorious, and the detachment will perish. Then when it is the fourth day, the remainder of the people of Islam will rise against them, and Allah ﷿ will make the rout upon them, and they will be slain in a slaughter — either he said: the like of it is not seen, or he said: we have not seen the like of it — so that a bird would pass by their sides and not get past them until it falls dead. He said: The sons of one father, who were a hundred, will count one another, and will not find that any remained of them except the one man. So over what booty will one rejoice? Or what inheritance will be divided?! He said: While they are like that, they will hear of a calamity greater than that. He said: The crier will come to them [saying] that the Dajjāl has succeeded [them] among their offspring. So they will drop what is in their hands and turn back, and will send ten horsemen as a vanguard. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed I know their names, and the names of their fathers, and the colours of their horses. They are the best horsemen on the face of the earth on that day.”
items.ma-4147: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Abū ʿUthmān, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Let not the adhān of Bilāl — or he said: the call of Bilāl — prevent any of you from his pre-dawn meal, for he gives the adhān — or he said: he calls out — so that your one who is standing [in prayer] may return, and so that he may rouse your sleeper. Then it is not that he says thus — or he said thus — until he says thus.”
items.ma-4148: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a distribution. He said: A man of the Anṣār said: Indeed by this distribution Wajh Allāh ﷿ was not intended. ʿAbd Allāh said: O enemy of Allah, I will certainly inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of what you said. He said: So I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and his face turned red, and he said: “The mercy of Allah be upon Mūsā. He was harmed with more than this, and he was patient.”
items.ma-4149:
Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Dāwūd informed us, and Ibn Abī Zāʾidah — [in] meaning — he said: Dāwūd narrated to us, from al-Shaʿbī, from ʿAlqamah, he said: I said to Ibn Masʿūd: Did any of you accompany the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Night of the Jinn? He said: None of us accompanied him, but we missed him one night, and we said: Was he assassinated? Was he snatched away? What has been done with him? He said: So we spent the worst night that a people ever spent. Then when it was at the face of the morning — or he said: at the pre-dawn — behold, we saw him coming from the direction of Ḥirāʾ. So we said: O Messenger of Allah — and they mentioned what they had been in. He said: “The caller of the jinn came to me, so I went to them and recited to them.” He said: Then he set off with us and showed me their traces and the traces of their fires.
He said: And al-Shaʿbī said: They asked him for provisions. Ibn Abī Zāʾidah said: ʿĀmir said: So they asked him that night for provisions — and they were of the jinn of al-Jazīrah — and he said: “Every bone over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, that falls into your hands, [will be] with the most flesh that it ever had on it; and every dropping or dung is fodder for your animals, so do not cleanse yourselves with them, for they are the provision of your brothers of the jinn.”
items.ma-4150: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, that he performed Ḥajj with ʿAbd Allāh, and that he threw seven pebbles at the Jamrah. He said: And he placed the House on his left and Minā on his right, and said: This is the standing place of the one upon whom Sūrat al-Baqarah was revealed.
items.ma-4151: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, he said: I heard Dharr narrating, from Wāʾil ibn Mahānah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said to the women: “Give ṣadaqah, for you are the majority of the people of the Fire.” A woman who was not of the elite of women, or of the most intelligent of them, said: O Messenger of Allah, concerning what? Or for what? Or by what? He said: “Indeed you curse much, and you are ungrateful to the ʿashīr.”
items.ma-4152: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, al-Ḥakam narrated to me, from Dharr, from Wāʾil ibn Mahānah, of Taym al-Ribāb, of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the women: “Give ṣadaqah, for you are the majority of the people of the Fire.” A woman, who was not of the elite of women, said: Concerning what? And by what? And for what? … So he mentioned the ḥadīth.
items.ma-4153: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, he said: I heard Abū Wāʾil say: I heard ʿAbd Allāh say. I said: Did you hear it from ʿAbd Allāh? He said: Yes, and he raised it. He said: “There is no one more aghyar than Allah ﷿, and for that reason He has forbidden the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden; and there is no one to whom praise is aḥabb ilayhi than Allah ﷿, and for that reason He praised Himself.”
items.ma-4154: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, that he heard Abū Wāʾil narrating, that a man came to Ibn Masʿūd and said: I recited the whole of the Mufaṣṣal in one rakʿah. ʿAbd Allāh said: Rapidly, like the rapid [recitation] of poetry? I certainly know the counterparts that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pair together. He said: Then he mentioned twenty sūrahs from the Mufaṣṣal, two sūrahs, two sūrahs in each rakʿah.
items.ma-4155: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ḥajjāj narrated to us, they said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abū ʿUbaydah — Ḥajjāj said in his narration: I heard Abū ʿUbaydah — from his father ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he sat in the first two rakʿahs, was as if upon hot stones. I said to Saʿd: Until he stood? He said: Until he stood. Ḥajjāj said: Shuʿbah said: Saʿd was moving his lip with something, so I said: Until he stood? He said: Until he stood.
items.ma-4156: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ḥajjāj narrated to us, they said: Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Yazīd: al-Masʿūdī informed us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said — Ḥajjāj said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ, and he said — Yazīd said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gathered us, and we were forty, and I was among the last of those who came to him; he said: “Indeed you will be given victory, and will attain [success], and [conquests] will be opened for you. So whoever reaches that, let him fear Allah, and enjoin the right, and forbid the wrong. And whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire.” Yazīd said: “And let him maintain his ties of kinship.”
items.ma-4157: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And ʿAbd al-Razzāq: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said — ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say —: “May Allah make radiant a man who heard a ḥadīth from us and memorised it until he conveys it; for perhaps one to whom it is conveyed is a better retainer of it than the hearer.”
items.ma-4158: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj: Shuʿbah narrated to me — Ḥajjāj said: he said: I heard ʿUqbah ibn Wassāj — from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “The excellence of a man's prayer in the congregation over his prayer alone is twenty-five degrees.” Ḥajjāj said: Shuʿbah did not raise it for me, but he raised it for others. He said: I am wary of raising it, because ʿAbd Allāh seldom used to raise [narrations] to the Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-4159: Bahz narrated it to me, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah informed us, from Muwarriq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ al-Jushamī, from Ibn Masʿūd: that the Prophet ﷺ used to give preference to the prayer in congregation over the prayer of a man alone by twenty-five prayers, all of them like his prayer.
items.ma-4160:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū Isḥāq narrating from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that he said: Indeed Muḥammad ﷺ was taught the openings of good, its comprehensive [parts], and its conclusions. So he said: “When you sit in every two rakʿahs, say: All greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. Then let one of you choose of supplication what pleases him most, and let him supplicate with it to his Rabb ﷿.”
And indeed Muḥammad ﷺ said: “Shall I not inform you what al-ʿaḍh is?” He said: “It is tale-bearing, the spreading of talk between people.”
And indeed Muḥammad ﷺ said: “Indeed a man speaks the truth until he is recorded as a ṣiddīq, and lies until he is recorded as a habitual liar.”
items.ma-4161: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “If I were to take anyone of my ummah as a khalīl, I would take Abū Bakr.”
items.ma-4162: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to say: “O Allah, I ask You for guidance, taqwā, chastity, and sufficiency.”
items.ma-4163: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to recite this word: {Is there any who will take heed?}
items.ma-4164: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and ʿAffān narrated to us, they said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq — ʿAffān said: Abū Isḥāq informed us — from al-Aswad, and Muḥammad said: from Abū Isḥāq, he said: I heard al-Aswad narrating, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he recited al-Najm and prostrated with it, and those who were with him prostrated, except that an old man took a handful of pebbles, or earth, and raised it to his forehead and said: This is enough for me!! ʿAbd Allāh said: I saw him afterwards killed as a disbeliever.
items.ma-4165: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me while I was praying, and said: “Ask, and you will be given, O Ibn Umm ʿAbd.” ʿUmar said: So Abū Bakr and I hastened, and Abū Bakr preceded me to him, and we never raced to any good except that Abū Bakr preceded me to it. He said: Among my supplications, which I hardly ever leave: O Allah, I ask You for bliss that does not perish, and a delight of the eye that is not exhausted, and the companionship of the Prophet Muḥammad in the highest of Paradise, the Paradise of Eternity.
items.ma-4166: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Yaḥyā, from Shuʿbah, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh, that he said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a tent, about forty [of us]. He said: “Would you be pleased to be a quarter of the people of Paradise?” He said: We said: Yes. He said: “Would you be pleased to be a third of the people of Paradise?” So we said: Yes. He said: “By Him in Whose Yad is the soul of Muḥammad, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. That is because none enters Paradise except a Muslim soul, and you among the people of shirk are only like a white hair in the skin of a black bull, or a black hair in the skin of a red bull.”
items.ma-4167: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salamah say: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd say: Your Prophet ﷺ was given the keys of everything except the five: {Indeed Allah — with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs; and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed Allah is al-ʿAlīm, al-Khabīr} [Luqmān: 34]. He said: I said to him: Did you hear it from ʿAbd Allāh? He said: Yes, more than fifty times.
items.ma-4168: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Yaḥyā ibn al-Mujabbir say: I heard Abū Mājid — meaning al-Ḥanafī — say: I was sitting with ʿAbd Allāh. He said: I certainly remember the first man he cut: a thief was brought, and he commanded that he be cut, and it was as if the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been dusted. He said: They said: O Messenger of Allah, it is as though you disliked cutting him? He said: “And what prevents me? Do not be a help to Shayṭān against your brother. It is proper for the imām, when a ḥadd reaches him, to carry it out. Indeed Allah ﷿ is ʿAfūw, Yuḥibbu al-ʿAfw: {And let them pardon and overlook. Would you not love that Allah forgive you? And Allah is Ghafūr, Raḥīm} [al-Nūr: 22].”
items.ma-4169: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Taymī, from Abū Mājid al-Ḥanafī, so he mentioned its meaning, and said: It was as if the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been dusted — saying: ashes were scattered upon it.
items.ma-4170: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Ibrāhīm ibn Suwayd — and he was the imām of the mosque of ʿAlqamah after ʿAlqamah — he said: ʿAlqamah led us in the Ẓuhr prayer, and I do not know whether he prayed three or five. It was said to him, and he said: And you, O one-eyed one? I said: Yes. He said: Then he performed two prostrations. Then ʿAlqamah narrated from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ … the like of that.
items.ma-4171: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, and Ḥajjāj, from Shuʿbah, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from ʿĪsā al-Asadī, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Ṭiyarah is of shirk, and there is none of us but — but Allah removes it through reliance.”
items.ma-4172: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Jābir, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he used to give the salām to his right and to his left, until I would see the whiteness of his face. And I have not forgotten afterwards, among what I have forgotten: Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah, Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah.
items.ma-4173: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr and Sulaymān, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbīdah al-Salmānī, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “The best of you is my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them, then there will succeed a people whose testimonies precede their oaths, and their oaths their testimonies.”
items.ma-4174: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Manṣūr wrote to me, and I read it to him, he said: Ibrāhīm narrated to me, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed a prayer — I do not know whether he added or diminished — (Ibrāhīm is the one who said: he does not know; ʿAlqamah said: he added or diminished, or ʿAbd Allāh) — then he turned to face us, so we told him of what he had done, and he folded his leg, faced the qiblah, and performed two prostrations, then turned to us with his face and said: “If something had occurred in the prayer, I would have informed you of it. But I am only a human being; I forget as you forget. So if I forget, remind me. And whichever of you doubts in his prayer, let him seek out what is closest to the correct, and complete upon it, and give the salām, then perform two prostrations.”
items.ma-4175: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “When you are three, let not two converse privately apart from their companion, because it would grieve him; and let not a woman have skin-to-skin contact with a woman, because she would describe her to her husband.”
items.ma-4176: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ḥajjāj narrated to us, they said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “How evil it is for one of you — or: for one of them — to say: I have forgotten such-and-such verse; rather he has been made to forget. And keep reviewing the Qurʾān, for it escapes more quickly from the chests of men than livestock [escape] with their hobbles — or: from their hobbles.”
items.ma-4177: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, he said: I heard Abū Wāʾil narrating from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We used to say: Peace be upon so-and-so and so-and-so. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Say: All greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. For if you say: Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah, you will have given the salām to every righteous servant in the earth and in the heaven.”
items.ma-4178: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr and Zubayd, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Reviling a believer is fusūq, and fighting him is kufr.” He said in the narration of Zubayd: I heard Abū Wāʾil.
items.ma-4179: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Rukayn narrated to me, he said: I heard al-Qāsim ibn Ḥassān narrating from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥarmalah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to dislike ten [things]: yellow [dye], changing grey hair, trailing the lower garment, the gold ring — or he said: the gold band — casting the kiʿāb, displaying adornment in other than its place, incantations except with the muʿawwidhāt, amulets, diverting the water, and spoiling a child without forbidding him.
items.ma-4180: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Mughīrah, he said: I heard Abū Wāʾil narrating, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “I am your forerunner at the Ḥawḍ, and men from among you will be brought forward to me, then they will be snatched away from before me, so I will say: O Rabb, my companions! It will be said to me: Indeed you do not know what they innovated after you.”
items.ma-4181: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū al-Tayyāḥ, from a man of Ṭayyiʾ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us from tabaqqur in family and wealth. Abū Jamrah, who was sitting with him, said: Yes, Akhram al-Ṭāʾī narrated to me, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ. He said: ʿAbd Allāh said: So how about one with a family in Rādhān, a family in al-Madīnah, and a family in such-and-such? Shuʿbah said: I said to Abū al-Tayyāḥ: What is al-tabaqqur? He said: Multiplicity.
items.ma-4182: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Rajāʾ, he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Hudhayl narrating, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd narrating, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “If I were to take a khalīl, I would take Abū Bakr as a khalīl, but he is my brother and my companion; and Allah ﷿ has taken your companion as a khalīl.”
items.ma-4183: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Wāṣil, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: And I think he raised it to the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Before the Hour are the days of al-harj, days in which knowledge will vanish and ignorance will appear.” Abū Mūsā said: Al-harj in the tongue of the Abyssinians is killing.
items.ma-4184: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū al-Tayyāḥ, from Ibn al-Akhram, a man of Ṭayyiʾ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he forbade tabaqqur in family and wealth.
items.ma-4185: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū Jamrah narrating, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: And ʿAbd Allāh said: How is one who has three families: a family in al-Madīnah, a family in such-and-such, and a family in such-and-such?
items.ma-4186: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj: Shuʿbah narrated to me, from al-Walīd ibn al-ʿAyzār — Ḥajjāj said: I heard Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī, and Muḥammad said: from Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī — he said: The owner of this house narrated to us — and he gestured with his hand to the house of ʿAbd Allāh, and did not name him to us — he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Which deed is most beloved to Allah ﷿? He said: “The prayer at its time” — al-Ḥajjāj said: “for its time” — He said: Then which? He said: “Then dutifulness to parents.” He said: Then which? He said: “Then jihād in the path of Allah.” And had I asked him for more, he would have given me more.
items.ma-4187: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “A man continues to speak the truth and seek out truthfulness until he is recorded as a ṣiddīq, and a man continues to lie and seek out lying until he is recorded with Allah as a habitual liar.”
items.ma-4188: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, that he said: I am told of your gathering, and what prevents me from coming out to you is fear that I would weary you. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to attend to us with admonition on [certain] days, fearing weariness for us.
items.ma-4189: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, Manṣūr, Ḥammād, al-Mughīrah, and Abū Hāshim, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said in the tashahhud: “All greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.”
items.ma-4190: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr and al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “When you are three, let not two converse privately apart from one, and let not a woman have skin-to-skin contact with a woman so that she describes her to her husband until it is as if he is looking at her.” He said: I think Manṣūr said: “unless there is a garment between them.”
items.ma-4191: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, he said: I heard Abū Wāʾil narrating, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “When you are three …” So he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-4192: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibrāhīm ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached the evening he would say: “We have entered the evening, and the dominion has entered the evening, belonging to Allah; and praise is for Allah. There is no deity except Allah alone, with no partner for Him.”
items.ma-4193: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever sees me in a dream has seen me, for Shayṭān does not take on a form like mine.”
items.ma-4194: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Salamah, from ʿĪsā ibn ʿĀṣim, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Ṭiyarah is shirk, ṭiyarah is shirk, but Allah ﷿ removes it through reliance.”
items.ma-4195: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Qays, from Huzayl, he said: A man came to Abū Mūsā and Salmān ibn Rabīʿah and asked them about a daughter, a son's daughter, and a sister. They said: To the daughter is half, and to the sister half; and go to ʿAbd Allāh, for he will follow us. So he came to ʿAbd Allāh and informed him. He said: I would have gone astray then, and I would not be of the rightly guided. I will judge in it by the judgement of the Messenger of Allah ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam — or he said: the judgement of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — thus Sufyān said —: to the daughter is half, to the son's daughter a sixth, and what remains is for the sister.
items.ma-4196: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “It is not fitting for anyone to be better than Yūnus ibn Mattā.”
items.ma-4197: And Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated it to us with its isnād, he said: “Let none of you say: I am better than Yūnus ibn Mattā.”
items.ma-4198: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿUmārah ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ, he said: Abū Zurʿah narrated to us, a companion of ours narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us and said: “Nothing infects anything, nothing infects anything, nothing infects anything.” A bedouin stood and said: O Messenger of Allah, the small spot of mange on the lip of the camel or on its tail, in a great herd of camels, and then all of them become mangy?! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Then what made the first one mangy? There is no contagion, no hāmah, and no ṣafar. Allah created every soul, and wrote its life, its misfortunes, and its provision.”
items.ma-4199: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I prayed — or: I stood — with the Prophet ﷺ one night, and he kept standing until I intended an evil thing! He said: We said: What did you intend? He said: I intended to sit and leave him.
items.ma-4200: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, he said: I heard Abū Wāʾil narrating, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Indeed the first thing that will be judged between the servants is in bloodshed.”
items.ma-4201: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and ʿAffān narrated to us, they said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān — ʿAffān said: Sulaymān narrated to us — from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “For every treacherous one there will be a banner on the Day of Resurrection.” Ibn Jaʿfar said: “It will be said: This is the treachery of so-and-so.”
items.ma-4203: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, he said: I heard Abū Wāʾil narrating, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: It is as though I am looking at the Prophet ﷺ while he was relating [the story of] a prophet — he said: “His people used to beat him until he was knocked down” — he said: and he wipes his forehead and says: “O Allah, forgive my people, for they do not know.”
items.ma-4204: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, he said: I heard Abū Wāʾil, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a distribution, and a man said: Indeed this is a distribution by which Wajh Allāh was not intended! He said: So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and his face turned red — Shuʿbah said: and I think he said: and he became angry — until I wished that I had not informed him. Shuʿbah said: And I think he said: “May Allah have mercy on us and on Mūsā — Shuʿbah doubted in: May Allah have mercy on us and Mūsā — he was harmed with more than this, and was patient.” In this [part] there is no doubt: “He was harmed with more than that and was patient.”
items.ma-4205: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, he said: I heard Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was suffering fever, and I said: O Messenger of Allah, you are suffering a severe fever? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed I suffer the fever of two men among you.” I said: Is it because you have two rewards? He said: “Yes — or: Indeed.” Then he said: “There is no Muslim who is afflicted by harm, a thorn or what is above it, except that Allah ﷿ sheds his sins from him, as the tree sheds its leaves.”
items.ma-4206: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān and Manṣūr, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he saw that Quraysh had become disobedient to him, said: “O Allah, help me against them with seven [years] like the seven of Yūsuf.” He said: So the famine seized them until it stripped everything bare, until they ate hides and bones — and one of the two said: until they ate hides and carrion — and there began to come out from a man the like of smoke. Abū Sufyān came to him and said: O Muḥammad, your people have perished, so supplicate Allah ﷿ to remove it from them. He said: So he supplicated. Then he said: “O Allah, if they return, then return” — this is in the narration of Manṣūr — then he recited this verse: {So watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke} [al-Dukhān: 10].
items.ma-4207: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ḥakīm ibn Jubayr, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever asks while he has what suffices him, his asking will come on the Day of Resurrection as scratches — or: lacerations — on his face.” They said: O Messenger of Allah, and what is his sufficiency? He said: “Fifty dirhams, or its equivalent in gold.”
items.ma-4208: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “What have I to do with the world? My likeness and the likeness of the world is only as the likeness of a rider who took a midday rest in the shade of a tree on a summer day, then departed and left it.”
items.ma-4209: Wakīʿ narrated to us, ʿĪsā ibn Dīnār, the mawlā of Khuzāʿah, narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Muṣṭaliq, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: We did not fast Ramaḍān in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ twenty-nine [days] more than we fasted thirty.
items.ma-4210: Wakīʿ and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, they said: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Sāʾib, from Zādhān, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said — Wakīʿ said: “Indeed Allah has angels roaming in the earth who convey to me the salām from my ummah.”
items.ma-4211: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from ʿAlqamah, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: I will pray with you the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So he raised his hands at the first.
items.ma-4212: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever swears an oath of ṣabr by which he cuts off the property of a Muslim man, while being a transgressor in it, will meet Allah ﷿ while He is ghaḍbān ʿalayhi.” He said: And this verse was revealed: {Indeed those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price} to the end of the verse [Āl ʿImrān: 77].
items.ma-4213: Wakīʿ and Ḥumayd al-Ruʾāsī narrated to us, they said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil — Ḥumayd said: Shaqīq ibn Salamah — from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The first thing to be decided between the people on the Day of Resurrection is in bloodshed.”
items.ma-4214: Ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, he said: I heard Abū Wāʾil … So he mentioned it.
items.ma-4215: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us. And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Sufyān, from Zubayd, from Ibrāhīm, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He is not of us who strikes the cheeks, tears the garment-openings, and calls with the call of the Jāhiliyyah.”
items.ma-4216: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh. And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr and al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Paradise — and Wakīʿ said, from Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Paradise is certainly nearer to one of you than the strap of his sandal, and the Fire is the same.”
items.ma-4217: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbīdah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best of people is my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them, then there will come a people whose testimony precedes their oaths, and their oaths their testimony.”
items.ma-4218: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Khumayr ibn Mālik, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: I recited from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seventy sūrahs, while Zayd ibn Thābit had a forelock in the kuttāb.
items.ma-4219: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Bashīr ibn Salmān narrated to us, from Sayyār Abū al-Ḥakam, from Ṭāriq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever is afflicted by want and brings it down upon the people, he deserves that his need not be met; and whoever brings it down upon Allah ﷿, Allah will bring him a prompt provision or a delayed death.”
items.ma-4220:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Bashīr Abū Ismāʿīl, from Sayyār Abū Ḥamzah … So he mentioned it.
[ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad said:] My father said: And it is the correct one: Sayyār Abū Ḥamzah. He said: And Sayyār Abū al-Ḥakam did not narrate anything from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb.
items.ma-4221: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿUmārah ibn ʿUmayr al-Taymī, from Wahb ibn Rabīʿah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I was hiding myself by the coverings of the Kaʿbah when two Thaqafī men entered, and their in-law a Qurashī — or two Qurashī men and their in-law a Thaqafī — abundant in the fat of their bellies, little in the understanding of their hearts. They conversed with a conversation among themselves, and one of them said to his companion: Do you think Allah ﷿ Yasmaʿu what we say?! The other said: I think He Yasmaʿu when we raise our voices, and does not Yasmaʿ when we speak softly. The other said: If He Yasmaʿu any of it, then He Yasmaʿuhu all of it. So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and Allah ﷿ revealed: {And you were not concealing yourselves that your hearing would testify against you, nor your sight}, the verse [Fuṣṣilat: 22].
items.ma-4222: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿUmārah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh … So he mentioned its meaning, and there was revealed: {And you were not concealing yourselves that your hearing would testify against you, nor your sight}, up to His saying: {and you have become among the losers}.
items.ma-4223: Wakīʿ narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī narrated to me, he said: The owner of this house narrated to me — meaning Ibn Masʿūd — he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, which deeds are most excellent? He said: “The prayer at its time.”
items.ma-4224: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from al-Aswad and ʿAlqamah — or one of them — from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Prophet ﷺ used to say the takbīr at every rising and lowering. He said: And Abū Bakr and ʿUmar ﵄ did it.
items.ma-4225: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from his father, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh: that the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar ﵄ used to say the takbīr at every lowering and rising.
items.ma-4226: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Prophet ﷺ, when he went to his bed, would place his hand beneath his cheek and say: “O Allah, protect me from Your punishment on the day You raise Your servants.”
items.ma-4227: Wakīʿ narrated to us, he said: Sufyān said: al-Aʿmash said, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “It is not fitting for anyone to say: I am better than Yūnus ibn Mattā.”
items.ma-4228: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to attend to us with admonition on [certain] days, for fear of weariness for us.
items.ma-4229: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Let not a woman have skin-to-skin contact with a woman, describing her to her husband until it is as if he is looking at her.”
items.ma-4230: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Allah has cursed the women who tattoo and those who have themselves tattooed, the women who pluck [hair], and the women who create gaps [between their teeth] for beauty. That reached a woman of Banū Asad, who was called Umm Yaʿqūb, so she came to him and said: I have certainly read what is between the two covers; I did not find what you said! He said: Did you not find: {And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you from, abstain from it} [al-Ḥashr: 7]? She said: I think it is in some of your family? He said: Go and look. He said: So she went and looked, then she came and said: I saw nothing. ʿAbd Allāh said: If she had it, we would not have joined with her.
items.ma-4231: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said a word, and I said another. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever dies associating anything with Allah will enter the Fire,” and I said: Whoever dies not associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise.
items.ma-4232: Ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said … So he mentioned the like of it, except that he said: “makes a rival to Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-4233: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from his father and Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to supplicate, saying: “O Allah, I ask You for guidance, taqwā, chastity, and sufficiency.”
items.ma-4234: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Shimr ibn ʿAṭiyyah al-Kāhilī, from Mughīrah ibn Saʿd ibn al-Akhram al-Ṭāʾī, from his father, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not take an estate, and so desire the world.”
items.ma-4235: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, he said: Abū Isḥāq narrated to me, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, that the Prophet ﷺ recited al-Najm and prostrated in it, and those with him, except an old man who took a handful of pebbles or earth. He said: and he did thus with it, placing it on his forehead. He said: I certainly saw him afterwards killed as a disbeliever.
items.ma-4236: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated to us, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ has not sent down a disease except that He sent down for it a cure; he who knows it knows it, and he who is ignorant of it is ignorant of it.”
items.ma-4237: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah; and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar: Shuʿbah narrated to us, al-Ḥakam narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh: that the Prophet ﷺ prayed the Ẓuhr prayer [with] five [rakʿahs], so it was said to him: Has something been added to the prayer?! He said: “And what is that?” They said: You prayed five. He said: So he folded his leg, then performed two prostrations after he had given the salām.
items.ma-4238:
Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, he said: Sulaymān narrated to us, from ʿUmārah, from Wahb ibn Rabīʿah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I was hiding by the coverings of the Kaʿbah, and three persons came: a Thaqafī and his two in-laws, Qurashīs, abundant in the fat of their bellies, little in the understanding of their hearts. He said: They conversed among themselves with a conversation. He said: One of them said: Do you think Allah ﷿ Yasmaʿu what we say?! The other said: He Yasmaʿu what we raise, and what we lower He does not Yasmaʿ!! The other said: If He Yasmaʿu anything, then He Yasmaʿuhu all of it. He said: So I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: So there was revealed: {And you were not concealing yourselves that there would testify against you} up to His saying: {and they are not of those who are allowed to make amends} [Fuṣṣilat: 22–24].
He said: And Manṣūr narrated to me, from Mujāhid, from Abū Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh … the like of that.
items.ma-4239: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid, from Abū Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh — he said: I heard him once raise it, then he left it — he saw an amīr or a man giving the salām with two taslīmahs, and he said: From where did you pick it up?
items.ma-4240: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: When this verse was revealed: {Those who believe and do not mix their īmān with wrongdoing} [al-Anʿām: 82], that was hard on the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they said: Which of us has not wronged himself? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “It is not as you think; it is only as Luqmān said to his son: {O my son, do not associate [others] with Allah; indeed shirk is a great wrong} [Luqmān: 13].”
items.ma-4241: Wakīʿ narrated to us and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, they said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he used to give the salām to his right and to his left: Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah, Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah, until the whiteness of his cheek was seen. And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: until the whiteness of his cheek was seen from here, and the whiteness of his cheek was seen from here.
items.ma-4242: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from a man, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Walk to the mosque, for it is of the way and the sunnah of Muḥammad ﷺ.
items.ma-4243: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, which deed is most excellent? He said: “The prayer at its time.” He said: I said: Then which? He said: “Dutifulness to parents.” He said: I said: Then which? He said: “Jihād in the path of Allah ﷿.” And had I asked him for more, he would have given me more.
items.ma-4244: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, Manṣūr narrated to me, from Khaythamah, from one who heard Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no night-conversation except for one who prays or a traveller.”
items.ma-4245: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The blood of a Muslim man who bears witness that there is no deity except Allah, and that I am the Messenger of Allah, is not lawful except for one of three persons: a life for a life, the previously married one who commits zinā, and the one who forsakes his religion, separating from the community.”
items.ma-4246: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: I reached Abū Jahl on the day of Badr, and his leg had been struck, and he was thrown down, defending the people from him with a sword of his. I said: Praise be to Allah who has disgraced you, O enemy of Allah! He said: Is he anything but a man whom his own people killed? He said: So I began to reach for him with a sword of mine, to no avail, and I struck his hand and his sword fell. I took it and struck him with it until I killed him. He said: Then I went out until I came to the Prophet ﷺ, as though I were being lifted from the earth, and I informed him. He said: “[Do you swear] by Allah, besides Whom there is no deity?” — and he repeated it three times — I said: By Allah, besides Whom there is no deity. He said: So he went out walking with me until he stood over him, and he said: “Praise be to Allah who has disgraced you, O enemy of Allah! This was the Pharaoh of this ummah.” He said: And my father added in it, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: So he gave me his sword as spoil.
items.ma-4247: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Badr and said: I killed Abū Jahl. He said: “[Do you swear] by Allah, besides Whom there is no deity?” He said: I said: By Allah, besides Whom there is no deity. And he repeated it three times. He said: “Allah is greatest. Praise be to Allah who was true to His promise, and gave victory to His servant, and defeated the confederates alone. Go and show him to me.” So we went, and there he was, and he said: “This is the Pharaoh of this ummah.”
items.ma-4248: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I was walking with the Prophet ﷺ in a tilled field in al-Madīnah, and he passed by a group of the Jews, and some of them said to others: Ask him about the rūḥ. Some of them said: Do not ask him. They said: O Muḥammad, what is the rūḥ? He said: So he stood, leaning on a palm-stalk, while I was behind him, and I thought that revelation was being given to him, and he said: {They ask you about the rūḥ. Say: The rūḥ is of the command of my Rabb, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little} [al-Isrāʾ: 85]. He said: Some of them said: We had said: Do not ask him.
items.ma-4249: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmmār ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Duhnī, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd al-Ashjaʿī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Ibn Sumayyah — two matters were never presented to him except that he chose the more rightly guided of the two.”
items.ma-4250: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah and al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I met a woman in the orchard, and I drew her to me, and touched her skin to skin, and kissed her, and did everything with her except that I did not have intercourse with her. He said: The Prophet ﷺ was silent toward him. Then this verse was revealed: {Indeed good deeds remove evil deeds; that is a reminder for those who remember} [Hūd: 114]. He said: So the Prophet ﷺ called him and recited it to him. ʿUmar said: O Messenger of Allah, is it for him in particular, or for the people altogether? He said: “Rather, for the people altogether.”
items.ma-4251: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to us at Minā while leaning his back against a red tent. He said: “Are you not pleased to be a quarter of the people of Paradise?” We said: Yes indeed. He said: “Are you not pleased to be a third of the people of Paradise?” They said: Yes indeed. He said: “By Allah, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. And I will tell you about that: concerning the fewness of the Muslims among the people on that day — they will not be among the people on that day except like the white hair on a black bull, or like the black hair on a white bull — and none will enter Paradise except a Muslim soul.”
items.ma-4252: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abū Hammām narrated to us, from ʿUthmān ibn Ḥassān, from Fulfulah al-Juʿfī, he said: I was alarmed, among those who were alarmed, [and resorted] to ʿAbd Allāh concerning the muṣḥafs, so we entered upon him, and a man of the group said: We have not come to you as visitors, but we came to you when this news alarmed us!! He said: Indeed the Qurʾān was revealed to your Prophet ﷺ from seven doors, upon seven aḥruf — or he said: ḥurūf — and the Book before it used to be revealed from one door, upon one ḥarf.
items.ma-4253: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Misʿar narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Your Prophet ﷺ was given everything except the five keys of the unseen: {Indeed Allah — with Him is the knowledge of the Hour} [Luqmān: 34].
items.ma-4254:
Sufyān — meaning Ibn ʿUyaynah — narrated to us, from Misʿar, from ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad, from Mughīrah al-Yashkurī, from al-Maʿrūr, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Umm Ḥabībah said: O Allah, let me enjoy my husband the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and my brother Muʿāwiyah, and my father Abū Sufyān. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: “You supplicated Allah ﷿ for appointed terms, and traces that are reached, and apportioned provisions; none of it comes early before its due time, and none of it is delayed. If you had asked Allah ﷿ to deliver you from the punishment of the grave, and the punishment of the Fire.”
And he was asked about the apes and the swine: Are they of those who were transformed, or something that existed before that? He said: “No, rather it was before that. Indeed Allah ﷿ did not destroy a people and then make for them offspring or posterity.”
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad narrated to us, he said: I read to my father from here up to the balāgh, and he affirmed it.
items.ma-4255: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, he said: Zāʾidah narrated to us, ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd narrated to us, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh: that the Prophet ﷺ came to him [as he was] between Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, while ʿAbd Allāh was praying, and he began with al-Nisāʾ and recited it in a flowing manner. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever loves to recite the Qurʾān fresh as it was revealed, let him recite it according to the recitation of Ibn Umm ʿAbd.” Then he came forward to ask, and the Prophet ﷺ began to say: “Ask, you will be given; ask, you will be given.” So he said in what he asked: O Allah, I ask You for īmān that does not turn back, and bliss that is not exhausted, and the companionship of Your Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ in the highest [part] of the Paradise of Eternity. He said: Then ʿUmar, raḍiya Allāhu taʿālā ʿanhu, came to ʿAbd Allāh to give him glad tidings, and found that Abū Bakr, riḍwānu Allāhi ʿalayhi, had preceded him. So he said: If you did so, you have always been one who races ahead in good.
items.ma-4256: I read to my father: ʿAmr ibn Mujammiʿ Abū al-Mundhir al-Kindī narrated to you, he said: Ibrāhīm al-Hajarī informed us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ has made the good deed of the son of Ādam [worth] ten times its like, up to seven hundred fold, except fasting. And fasting is for Me, and I reward for it. And for the fasting person are two joys: a joy at his breaking of the fast, and a joy on the Day of Resurrection. And the changed odour of the mouth of the fasting person is better with Allah than the scent of musk.”
items.ma-4257: I read to my father: ʿAmr ibn Mujammiʿ narrated to you, Ibrāhīm al-Hajarī informed us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “When one of you's servant brings him his food, let him draw him near, let him seat him at it, or let him feed him a morsel, for he has attended to its heat and its smoke.”
items.ma-4258: I read to my father: ʿAmr ibn Mujammiʿ narrated to you, Ibrāhīm al-Hajarī narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Indeed the first to set loose the sawāʾib, and to worship idols, was Abū Khuzāʿah ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir, and indeed I saw him dragging his intestines in the Fire.”
items.ma-4259: I read to my father: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to you, Yazīd ibn ʿAṭāʾ narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq al-Hajarī, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ … the like of it, and he did not mention: “and worshipped idols.”
items.ma-4260: I read to my father: ʿAmr ibn Mujammiʿ narrated to you, Ibrāhīm al-Hajarī narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed the miskīn is not the one who goes around, whom a morsel or two morsels, or a date or two dates, turn away.” I said: O Messenger of Allah, then who is the miskīn? He said: “The one who does not ask the people, and does not find what suffices him, and is not noticed so that ṣadaqah may be given to him.”
items.ma-4261: I read to my father: al-Qāsim ibn Mālik narrated to you, he said: al-Hajarī informed us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Hands are three: Yad Allāh is the uppermost, and the hand of the giver is the one that follows it, and the hand of the asker is the lowest.”
items.ma-4262: I read to my father: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to you, he said: Ibrāhīm al-Hajarī narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A Muslim's reviling his brother is fusūq, fighting him is kufr, and the inviolability of his property is like the inviolability of his blood.”
items.ma-4263: I read to my father: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to you, Ibrāhīm al-Hajarī narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Beware of these two kaʿbatān that are marked, which are cast forcefully, for they are the maysir of the non-Arabs.”
items.ma-4265: I read to my father: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Muslim al-Hajarī informed us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Let one of you guard his face from the Fire, even with half a date.”
items.ma-4266: I read to my father: ʿAlī narrated to us, from al-Hajarī, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When his servant comes to one of you with his food, let him seat him with him, or let him hand him some of it, for he has attended to its heat and its smoke.”
items.ma-4267: I read to my father: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib informed me, he said: I came to Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and he was cauterising a boy. He said: I said: You cauterise him?! He said: Yes, it is the medicine of the Arabs. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ has not sent down a disease except that He has sent down with it a medicine; whoever of you is ignorant of it is ignorant of it, or whoever of you knows it knows it.”
items.ma-4268: I read to my father: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, he said: Zāʾidah narrated to us, Ibrāhīm al-Hajarī narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ opens the gates of the heaven in the remaining third of the night, then Yahbiṭu to the lowest heaven, then Yabsuṭu Yadahu, then says: Is there no servant who asks Me, that I may give him? — until the dawn shines forth.”
items.ma-4269: I read to my father: Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥaddād narrated to us, he said: Sukayn ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-ʿAbdī narrated to us, Ibrāhīm al-Hajarī narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He who is moderate does not become needy.” Up to here I read to my father, and from here my father narrated to me.
items.ma-4270: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Ibrāhīm, from Abū Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh, that he said regarding this verse: {The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split}, he said: It split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two parts, or two halves — Shuʿbah is the one who doubts — so one half was behind the mountain, and one half over the mountain. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, bear witness.”
items.ma-4271: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, that Ibn Masʿūd was met by ʿUthmān at ʿArafāt, and he took him aside and spoke to him. Then ʿUthmān said to Ibn Masʿūd: Would you like a young woman whom I give in marriage to you? So ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd called ʿAlqamah, and narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever of you is able to afford the bāʾah, let him marry, for it is more lowering to the gaze and more protective of the private part; and whoever is not able, let him fast, for fasting is a restraint for him — or: a restraint.”
items.ma-4272: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Ibrāhīm, that al-Aswad and ʿAlqamah were with ʿAbd Allāh in the house, and ʿAbd Allāh said: Have these prayed? They said: Yes. He said: So he prayed with them without adhān or iqāmah, and stood in their midst, and said: When you are three, do thus; and when you are more, let one of you lead you. And let one of you place his hands between his thighs when he bows, and let him bend. It is as though I am looking at the differing of the fingers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-4273: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Khilās, and from Abū Ḥassān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: that Subayʿah bint al-Ḥārith gave birth to her child fifteen nights after the death of her husband, and Abū al-Sanābil entered upon her and said: It is as if you are speaking to yourself of the bāʾah?! That is not for you until the furthest of the two terms has elapsed. So she went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him of what Abū al-Sanābil had said. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Abū al-Sanābil lied. If anyone comes to you with whom you are pleased, come to me with him — or he said: inform me.” And he informed her that her ʿiddah had ended.
items.ma-4274: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bakr narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Khilās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah: that Subayʿah bint al-Ḥārith … So he mentioned the ḥadīth, or something like that, and he said in it: “And when a suitable match comes to you, come to me, or inform me,” and Ibn Masʿūd is not in it.
items.ma-4275: And ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said: from Khilās, from Ibn ʿUtbah, mursal.
items.ma-4276: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: A man marries and does not appoint [a dowry] for her, meaning: then dies: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Khilās and Abū Ḥassān al-Aʿraj, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd, that he said: They kept coming to Ibn Masʿūd concerning that for a month or about that, and they said: You must say something about it. He said: Then I judge for her the like of the dowry of a woman of her women, no deficiency and no excess; and she has the inheritance, and upon her is the ʿiddah. If it is correct, it is from Allah ﷿; and if it is a mistake, it is from me and from Shayṭān, and Allah ﷿ and His Messenger are free of it. Then a group from Ashjaʿ stood, among them al-Jarrāḥ and Abū Sinān, and they said: We bear witness that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged regarding a woman among us who is called Barwaʿ bint Wāshiq, in the like of what you have judged. Ibn Masʿūd rejoiced greatly at that when his statement agreed with the judgement of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-4277:
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bakr narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd narrated to us. My father said: So I read to Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd: Hishām, from Qatādah, from Khilās, and from Abū Ḥassān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd, that Ibn Masʿūd was brought a case concerning a woman whom a man had married and did not name a dowry for her, and he died before he went in to her. He said: They kept coming to Ibn Masʿūd … So he mentioned the ḥadīth, except that he said: Her husband was Hilāl — I think he said: Ibn Murrah.
ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said: And her husband was Hilāl ibn Murrah al-Ashjaʿī.
items.ma-4278: Bahz and ʿAffān narrated to us, they said: Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Khilās and Abū Ḥassān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, that there was a going back and forth to Ibn Masʿūd concerning a woman whom a man had married, and he died … So he mentioned the ḥadīth. He said: Then al-Jarrāḥ and Abū Sinān stood, and testified that the Prophet ﷺ judged by it among them, among al-Ashjaʿ ibn Rayth, concerning Barwaʿ bint Wāshiq al-Ashjaʿiyyah — and the name of her husband was Hilāl ibn Marwān. ʿAffān said: He judged by it among them, among al-Ashjaʿ ibn Rayth, concerning Barwaʿ bint Wāshiq al-Ashjaʿiyyah, and her husband was Hilāl ibn Marwān.
items.ma-4279: ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd al-Ṭanāfisī narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The days will not come to an end, and time will not pass, until there rules over the Arabs a man of my household, whose name agrees with my name.”
items.ma-4280: ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give the salām to his right until the whiteness of his cheek appeared, saying: “Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah,” and to his left until the whiteness of his cheek appeared, saying: “Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah.”
items.ma-4281: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥammad al-Muḥāribī narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, [ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad said:] my father said: and another than him said: from ʿAlqamah, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: While we were in the mosque on the night of Friday, a man of the Anṣār said: By Allah, if a man finds a man with his wife and speaks, he will be flogged, and if he kills him, he will be killed, and if he is silent, he will be silent in rage. By Allah, if morning comes, I will certainly go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When morning came he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, if a man finds a man with his wife and speaks, he will be flogged, and if he kills him, he will be killed, and if he is silent, he will be silent in rage? And he kept saying: O Allah, open; O Allah, open. He said: Then the mulāʿanah was revealed: {And those who accuse their spouses and have no witnesses except themselves … } the verse [al-Nūr: 6].
items.ma-4282: Ibn Idrīs narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUbayd Allāh mention from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, that he informed them from ʿAbd Allāh: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led them in prayer in five [rakʿahs], then turned, and some of the people began whispering to others, and they said to him: O Messenger of Allah, you prayed five. So he turned, and performed two prostrations with them, and gave the salām, and said: “I am only a human being; I forget as you forget.”
items.ma-4283: al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Qays, from al-Huzayl, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the woman who tattoos and the woman who has herself tattooed, the woman who joins [hair] and the woman to whom it is joined, the muḥill and the muḥallal lahu, the one who consumes ribā and the one who feeds it.
items.ma-4284: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Abū Qays, from Huzayl, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the woman who tattoos and the woman who has herself tattooed, the woman who joins [hair] and the woman to whom it is joined, the muḥallil and the muḥallal lahu, the one who consumes ribā and the one who feeds it.
items.ma-4285: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I said: Which deeds are most excellent? He said: “The prayers at their times, dutifulness to parents, and jihād in the path of Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-4286: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from a man, from ʿAmr ibn Wābiṣah al-Asadī, from his father, he said: I was in al-Kūfah in my house when I heard at the door of the house: Peace be upon you, may I enter? I said: And upon you be peace; so enter. When he entered, it was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd. I said: O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, what hour of visiting is this?! — and that was at the height of midday — He said: The day grew long for me, so I thought of someone to talk to. He said: So he began narrating to me from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I narrated to him. He said: Then he began to narrate to me, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “There will be a fitnah in which the one sleeping is better than the one lying down, the one lying down in it is better than the one sitting, the one sitting in it is better than the one standing, the one standing in it is better than the one walking, the one walking is better than the one riding, and the one riding is better than the one running; those slain in it, all of them, are in the Fire.” He said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, and when will that be? He said: “That is in the days of al-harj.” I said: And when are the days of al-harj? He said: “When a man is not safe from his companion.” He said: I said: What do you command me [to do] if I reach that? He said: “Restrain your self and your hand, and enter your house.” He said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if a man enters upon me in my house? He said: “Then enter your room.” He said: I said: And what do you think if he enters upon me in my room? He said: “Then enter your mosque, and do thus” — and he grasped his wrist with his right [hand] — “and say: My Rabb is Allah, until you die upon that.”
items.ma-4287: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh — meaning Ibn al-Mubārak — informed us, Maʿmar informed us, from Isḥāq ibn Rāshid, from ʿAmr ibn Wābiṣah al-Asadī …
items.ma-4288: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, ʿAbdah ibn Abī Lubābah narrated to me, that Shaqīq ibn Salamah said: I heard Ibn Masʿūd say: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “How evil it is for a man, or for a person, to say: I have forgotten such-and-such sūrah, or such-and-such verse; rather he has been made to forget.”
items.ma-4289: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Aʿmash, concerning His saying ﷿: {Indeed he saw of the greatest signs of his Rabb}, he said: Ibn Masʿūd said: The Prophet ﷺ saw a green rafraf from Paradise that had closed off the horizon. He mentioned it from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh.
items.ma-4290: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, that he heard Ibrāhīm narrating, from ʿAlqamah and al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Prophet of Allah, I took hold of a woman in the orchard and did everything to her except that I did not have intercourse with her; I kissed her and clung to her, and did nothing other than that. So do with me what you will. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said nothing to him, so the man went. ʿUmar said: Allah had concealed him, if only he had concealed himself! He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ followed him with his sight and said: “Bring him back to me.” They brought him back to him, and he recited to him: {And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night. Indeed good deeds remove evil deeds} up to: {those who remember} [Hūd: 114]. Muʿādh ibn Jabal said: Is it for him alone, or for the people altogether, O Prophet of Allah? He said: “Rather, for the people altogether.”
items.ma-4291: Surayj narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Simāk, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah and al-Aswad … and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
items.ma-4292: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Simāk, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever helps his people in wrongdoing is like the camel that has fallen down; it pulls by its tail.”
items.ma-4293: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, he said: I departed with Ibn Masʿūd from ʿArafah, and when he came to al-Muzdalifah he prayed the Maghrib and the ʿIshāʾ, each of the two with an adhān and an iqāmah, and put the supper between them, then slept. When someone said: The dawn has risen, he prayed the Fajr, then said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “These two prayers were delayed from their time in this place. As for the Maghrib, the people do not come here until it is dark. And as for the Fajr, this is its time.” Then he stood, and when it became bright he said: If the Commander of the Believers is correct, he will depart now. He said: ʿAbd Allāh had not finished his speech until ʿUthmān departed.
items.ma-4294: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, my father informed me, from Mīnāʾ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on the night of the delegation of the jinn, and when he departed he sighed, and I said: What is the matter with you? He said: “My soul has been announced to me, O Ibn Masʿūd.”
items.ma-4295: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I had certainly intended to command a man to lead the people in prayer, then to look, and burn upon a people their houses, who do not attend the Friday prayer.”
items.ma-4296: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Abū Fazārah al-ʿAbsī, he said: Abū Zayd, the mawlā of ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, narrated to us from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: On the night of the jinn two men of them stayed behind and said: We will attend the Fajr with you, O Messenger of Allah. The Prophet ﷺ said to me: “Do you have water with you?” I said: I have no water with me, but I have a small waterskin with nabīdh in it. The Prophet ﷺ said: “A good date and purifying water.” So he performed wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-4297: Ibrāhīm ibn Khālid narrated to us, Rabāḥ narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “They hold back from the Friday prayer! I had certainly intended to command my young men, so they gather firewood, then to command a man to lead the people, and burn upon a people their houses, who do not attend the Friday prayer.”
items.ma-4298: Ibrāhīm ibn Khālid narrated to us, Rabāḥ narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Qāsim, from his father: that al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah once delayed the prayer, so ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd stood and called out for the prayer, and led the people in prayer. So al-Walīd sent to him: What made you do what you did? Did a command come to you from the Commander of the Believers regarding what you did, or did you innovate? He said: No command came to me from the Commander of the Believers, and I did not innovate; but Allah ﷿ and His Messenger refused for us that we wait for you with our prayer while you are in your need.
items.ma-4299: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAlqamah ibn Qays, from Ibn Masʿūd: that the Prophet ﷺ went for his need, and commanded Ibn Masʿūd to bring him three stones. He brought him two stones and a piece of dung. He threw the dung away and said: “It is foul. Bring me a stone.”
items.ma-4300: Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah narrated to us, he said: ʿĪsā ibn Dīnār narrated to me, from his father, from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Ḍirār, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: I did not fast with the Prophet ﷺ twenty-nine [days] more than I fasted with him thirty.
items.ma-4301: Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to me, from Abū Fazārah, from Abū Zayd, the mawlā of ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “Do you have anything purifying with you?” I said: No. He said: “Then what is this in the small waterskin?” I said: Nabīdh. He said: “Show it to me. A good date and purifying water.” So he performed wuḍūʾ from it and prayed.
items.ma-4302: Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā narrated to us, he said: Ismāʿīl informed me, from Qays, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we had no women. We said: O Messenger of Allah, shall we not have ourselves castrated? He forbade us from that, and said: {O you who believe, do not prohibit the good things that Allah has made lawful for you … } the verse [al-Māʾidah: 87].
items.ma-4303: Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā narrated to us, he said: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Jubayr, from Khishf ibn Mālik, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged concerning the blood-money for [killing by] mistake: twenty ibnat makhāḍ, twenty male ibn makhāḍ, twenty ibnat labūn, twenty ḥiqqahs, and twenty jadhaʿahs.
items.ma-4304: Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā narrated to us, from his father, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Whoever sees me in a dream, then I am the one he saw, for Shayṭān does not assume a likeness through me.”
items.ma-4305: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥurr, from al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah, he said: ʿAlqamah took my hand, he said: ʿAbd Allāh took my hand, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took my hand, and taught me the tashahhud in the prayer: “All greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.”
items.ma-4306: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from Sulaymān, from Shaqīq, he said: I was with ʿAbd Allāh and Abū Mūsā while they were conversing, and they mentioned from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: “Before the Hour are days in which knowledge will be raised, ignorance will descend, and al-harj will be abundant.” He said: They both said: Al-harj is killing.
items.ma-4307: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from Simāk, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: We travelled by night with the Prophet ﷺ. He said: We said: O Messenger of Allah, if only we were to touch the ground and sleep, while our mounts graze? He said: So he did. He said: Then he said: “Let some of you guard us.” ʿAbd Allāh said: I said: I will guard you. He said: Then sleep overtook me and I slept, and I did not wake except when the sun was rising, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not wake except by our talking. So he commanded Bilāl, who gave the adhān, then established the prayer, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer.
items.ma-4308: Zakariyyā ibn ʿAdī narrated to us, he said: ʿUbayd Allāh narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Abū al-Wāṣil, from Ibn Masʿūd, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: “The muḥill and the muḥallal lahu are cursed.”
items.ma-4309: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated to us, Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: They were reciting behind the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “You have confused the Qurʾān for me.”
items.ma-4310: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Ḥajjāj informed us, from Fuḍayl, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He will not enter Paradise in whose heart is the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance.”
items.ma-4311: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq informed us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from his father, he said: I entered upon Ibn Masʿūd, I and my uncle, in the midday heat. He said: He established the prayer, and we stood behind him. He said: He took me by one hand and took my uncle by the other. He said: Then he brought us forward until he placed each man of us on a side, then said: Thus the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do when they were three.
items.ma-4312: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, he said: al-Masʿūdī informed us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from his father Ibn Masʿūd, he said: While a man among those before you was in his kingdom, he reflected, and knew that that would be cut off from him, and that what he was in had occupied him from worship of his Rabb. So he slipped away, and crept out one night from his palace, and in the morning was in the kingdom of another. He came to the seashore, and there he would mould bricks for wages, eating and giving the surplus as ṣadaqah. He did not cease thus, until his matter reached their king — and his worship and his excellence — so their king sent to him that he come to him, but he refused to come to him. He repeated, then repeated to him, and he refused to come to him, and said: What has he to do with me and what have I to do with him?! He said: So the king rode, and when the man saw him he turned away fleeing. When the king saw that, he galloped in his tracks, but did not catch up with him. He said: So he called to him: O servant of Allah, there is no harm upon you from me. So he stopped until he caught up with him. He said to him: Who are you, may Allah have mercy on you? He said: I am so-and-so son of so-and-so, the master of the kingdom of such and such. I reflected on my situation and knew that what I am in will be cut off, and that it had occupied me from the worship of my Rabb; so I left it and came here to worship my Rabb ﷿. He said: You are not more in need of what you did than I am. He said: Then he dismounted from his mount, set it loose, then followed him, and the two of them together worshipped Allah ﷿, and they supplicated Allah to cause them both to die together.
